higher_order_basis: Independent HOX-centered and TALE-cofactor comparisons repeatedly show flat, singleton-only, private, or near-zero-convergence transcriptomic surfaces rather than a shared postnatal neuronal homeobox differentiation module.
scope: Represented HOX-family, TALE/PBX/MEIS/PKNOX, retinoic-acid, Phox, and related developmental comparator perturbations in the assayed P16 postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Represented HOX-family and TALE/homeobox-cofactor perturbations do not form a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptional response module in the assayed P16 brain groups.

higher_order_basis: IFN receptor, STAT, IRF, NF-kB, and selected cytokine-receptor perturbation comparisons repeatedly show flat or singleton non-overlapping surfaces rather than a coherent ligand-gated IFN/JAK-STAT transcriptional response.
scope: Basal juvenile/postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented interferon receptor, STAT/IRF, NF-kB-neighbor, and cytokine receptor pathway components; JAK kinases and ligand stimulation were not tested.
statement: Represented interferon receptor, STAT, and IRF perturbations in basal postnatal neurons fail to produce a recurrent IFN/JAK-STAT transcriptional module, with only isolated nonconvergent single-gene events.

higher_order_basis: The Acsl4 finding directly relates its restricted neuronal signature to the Srebf2 sterol module in the opposite orientation, while Srebf2/Srebf1/Hmgcr findings define the relevant sterol axis and limitations.
scope: Restricted Acsl4 comparator groups overlapping Srebf2 sterol-gene responses in neuronal nuclear RNA readout.
statement: Acsl4 perturbation is linked to a restricted sterol-feedback signature that is inversely oriented to the Srebf2 cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional program rather than phenocopying Srebf2 loss.

higher_order_basis: HNF-family and associated developmental transcription-network comparisons converge on absent, singleton, or non-overlapping RNA outputs in postmitotic neuronal groups.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal atlas perturbation readout across represented HNF/MODY/endoderm/retinoid/Pax/MAF comparators, with several canonical non-neuronal targets absent from the panel.
statement: Represented HNF-family and associated MODY/endoderm transcription-network perturbations do not form an active multigene neuronal transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Across represented PP2A-related perturbations, the supplied findings show disjoint acute neuronal transcriptomic outputs rather than convergence onto a single shared transcriptional axis.
scope: Acute neuronal transcriptomic readout for Set and represented PP2A regulatory-subunit perturbations in this screen.
statement: Represented PP2A regulatory-subunit perturbations and Set perturbation do not collapse into a shared acute neuronal transcriptomic axis in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Both findings show divergence among represented CHD-family perturbations across overlapping postnatal neuronal responder groups while preserving the limitation that progenitor binding or cooperation was not tested.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal responder groups including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
statement: Represented CHD-family perturbations do not produce interchangeable postnatal neuronal transcriptomic phenotypes in matched responder groups.

higher_order_basis: Setdb1 anchors induction of repression-restoration transcripts, Mga supplies a Tasor-linked second target, and Zkscan1 provides a nonresponsive boundary within adjacent chromatin-repression comparisons.
scope: Thalamic and midbrain neuronal responders, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, within represented repressive-chromatin perturbations.
statement: Tasor induction marks a limited compensatory response to perturbation of some repressive-chromatin nodes, including Setdb1 and Mga, but not Zkscan1.

higher_order_basis: Vps35-centered, Washc4-centered, Vps35l-centered, Magel2-centered, and Lbx1-marker comparisons consistently distinguish the modest Vps35 thalamic response from flat or divergent Retriever/Commander/WASH and MUST-linked perturbations.

statement: The modest Vps35 thalamic neuronal transcriptional response is branch-specific and is not phenocopied by represented Vps35l/Retriever-Commander, Washc4/WASH, Magel2, or Lbx1-associated endosomal recycling perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Rab7 independently induced a sterol/lipid biosynthetic branch, and Depdc5 overlapped Rab7 in the same direction on sterol and endolysosomal genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
scope: Rab7 responders and Depdc5 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut state in the postnatal neuronal screen; transcript induction only, without direct sterol abundance or SREBP-processing measurements.
statement: Rab7 loss and Depdc5 loss converged on a sterol/endolysosomal transcriptional state in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: The Calm1 and Camta1 findings directly position the perturbations on opposite sides of a recurrent 151 TH transcriptional signature, with Calm1 defining the affected genes and Vps35 limiting the Camta1 anti-signature interpretation.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut perturbation signatures on recurrent posterior genes represented across the Calm1, Camta1, and Vps35 findings.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Calm1 loss and Camta1 loss produce opposing transcriptional effects on a recurrent posterior gene set that includes Peg3, Aifm3, Coro6, Vamp1, Resp18, Mest, and Vwa5b2.

higher_order_basis: Dyrk1a and Ppp3ca pathway-uncoupling findings anchor absence of convergent calcineurin/NFAT-linked transcription, while reciprocal Nfat5/Nfatc3 contrasts bound the only NFAT-family signal as target-specific.
scope: P16/postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations involving Dyrk1a, Ppp3ca, Nfat5, Nfatc3, and represented calcium-signaling comparators; NFAT localization and phosphorylation were not assayed.
statement: Classical calcineurin/NFAT-linked transcription is not a convergent acute neuronal RNA output of the measured Dyrk1a- or Ppp3ca-adjacent perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly support sparse, non-shared transcriptomic surfaces among measured adrenergic receptor perturbations while preserving the distinct Adra2a and Adra2b contexts.
scope: Measured neuronal cell groups after Adra2a, Adra2b, Adra1a, Adrb2, and Adrb3 perturbations, with Adra2c unavailable as a perturbation target.
statement: Measured adrenergic receptor perturbations show sparse, subtype-divergent neuronal RNA responses rather than a shared adrenergic transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: The Sox11-centered immature-neuron program test and the Sox4-centered paralog comparison both support absence of a shared single-paralog SOXC transcriptional response in recovered P16 postmitotic neuronal nuclei.
scope: Single Sox4 or Sox11 perturbations in recovered P16 postmitotic neuronal groups; combinatorial Sox4/Sox11 knockout and rare immature cells diluted below group-level detection were not tested.
statement: Single Sox4 or Sox11 perturbation in P16 postmitotic neuronal nuclei does not recover a shared SOXC or immature-neuron transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: Several findings describe isolated significant events for individual cholinergic/NMJ-related targets and show that biologically related perturbations do not reproduce those events, supporting target-specific sparse hits rather than a shared pathway response.
scope: Sparse significant neuronal hits from represented cholinergic and NMJ-related perturbations in matched neuronal groups.
statement: Sparse significant neuronal hits from represented cholinergic and NMJ-related perturbations are target-specific rather than evidence of a shared AChR or NMJ pathway response.

higher_order_basis: Across kinesin heavy chains, light chains, KIF1/Rab3/exocytosis comparators, Rhot1, and Miro/TRAK adaptor neighborhoods, physical transport relationships repeatedly fail to translate into a shared soma-detectable nuclear RNA program, while Klc1 and Atcay define sparse target-specific exceptions.
scope: Acute single-gene perturbations of represented neuronal kinesin-1, Kif1a-related, Rab3/exocytosis, Miro/TRAK, Rhot1, and related transport-pathway genes in juvenile/postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; not cargo localization, motor activity, or axonal transport physiology.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented neuronal kinesin-1 and Miro/TRAK transport-pathway genes does not produce a common soma-detectable neuronal nuclear transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Direct CaMKII paralog contrasts consistently reject a shared basal mRNA module, while receptor-linked positive benchmarks bound the result to transcriptomic nonconvergence rather than assay failure.
scope: Represented CaMKII paralog loss-of-function perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq, not kinase activity, phosphoproteomics, spine structure, or unmeasured Camk2d/gain-of-function alleles.
statement: Acute loss of represented CaMKII paralogs does not produce a shared basal postnatal neuronal mRNA module.

higher_order_basis: Both safe-targeting guide perturbations address Cas9 double-strand-break-associated stress readouts and show no persistent harvest-time p53/DNA-damage transcriptional program in recovered neurons, while allowing that transient early responses could have resolved before P37-P44.
scope: Safe_target_59 and Safe_target_74 guide perturbations assayed in recovered postnatal neuronal nuclei at P37-P44 after P16 delivery.
statement: Safe_target_59 and Safe_target_74 perturbations do not produce a persistent harvest-time neuronal p53/DNA-damage transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: AHR receptor, repressor, dimerization partner, and HIF-related findings converge on absence of basal canonical target-gene activation in juvenile NeuN-positive neurons, with explicit caveats about missing ligand, hypoxia, ischemia, and drug challenge contexts.
scope: Basal juvenile NeuN-positive neuronal perturbations without exogenous AHR ligand, hypoxia, ischemia, vascular cells, neural stem cells, or HIF-drug challenge.
statement: Basal juvenile NeuN-positive neurons in this assay lack a tonic ARNT-dependent HIF transcriptional program detectable by perturbing Arnt or Hif1a.

higher_order_basis: Both findings test related small-GTPase or downstream pathway perturbations and independently reject a common neuronal transcriptomic state among represented components.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal DE surfaces for represented FTase substrate, Ras/Rheb, Ras/Rho/Rap, and regulator perturbations; some same-complex processing and direct Rala pathway targets were absent.
statement: Represented small-GTPase, FTase-substrate, and downstream Ras/Rheb pathway perturbations do not converge on a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptional state.

higher_order_basis: Both NR4A perturbation findings fail to recover canonical plasticity or memory-output genes under basal postnatal snRNA-seq conditions, with Nr4a3 additionally showing a distinct narrow marker response.
scope: Basal postnatal neuronal Nr4a1 and Nr4a3 perturbation responses
statement: Basal postnatal neuronal Nr4a1 and Nr4a3 perturbations do not recover the canonical NR4A plasticity or memory-output transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: Both findings separate selective or buffered Son/Ylpm1 behavior from broad transcriptional responses produced by other represented splicing and RNP perturbations in the same screen.
scope: P16 NeuN+ perturbation surfaces for represented nuclear RNP, splicing, and RNA-processing factors
statement: Ylpm1 and Son do not behave as broad core RNA-processing perturbations in this assay, unlike represented splicing and RNP comparators that produce wider transcriptional effects.

higher_order_basis: Across Atxn2, Atxn7, and Camta1-centered comparisons, disease-family adjacency fails to predict shared acute postnatal neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic states in the represented targets.
scope: Represented ataxia and polyglutamine-associated perturbations in matched postmitotic neuronal cell groups; comparisons are transcriptomic loss-of-function contrasts rather than repeat-expansion disease models.
statement: Ataxia or polyglutamine-family membership does not predict a shared acute neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic state in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The component contains one repeated proposition: Arx retains a small postnatal inhibitory-neuron response in matched GABAergic groups, while several related developmental, homeobox, or endocrine transcription-factor perturbations remain flat there.
scope: P16 perturbation assay in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA groups; contrasts among Arx, Pax4, Pax6, Neurog3, and Ebf3.
statement: Arx loss produces a sparse postnatal GABAergic transcriptional response that is not shared by Pax4, Pax6, Neurog3, or Ebf3 perturbations in the same inhibitory-neuron groups.

higher_order_basis: Chd4 provides the direct opposite-sign NuRD-versus-BAF/PBAF contrast, while Smarce1, Smarcc2, and Arid2 findings establish the BAF/PBAF module being contrasted and Arid1a/Smarca4 findings bound its generality.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons under Chd4 and represented BAF/PBAF perturbations
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, represented BAF/PBAF perturbations can oppose rather than phenocopy Chd4-associated NuRD transcriptomic responses.

higher_order_basis: Kcnq2 provides a direct Bdnf-up response in the target cell class, while Kcnb1 recurrence and Kcnb2 non-phenocopy bound the response as activity-like and not a general Kv2 paralog effect.
scope: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons, with Kcnq2 represented by a single Bdnf hit and Kcnb1 by a small activity-like signature; Kcnb2 negative interpretation is limited by weak transcript knockdown and unknown indel strength.
statement: In 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut neurons, Kcnq2 loss exposes a Bdnf-centered activity-coupled transcriptional response that overlaps Kcnb1-associated features but is not phenocopied by Kcnb2.

higher_order_basis: Both independent perturbations of pancreatic endocrine-fate regulators lack the expected islet-cell transcriptional outputs across broad NeuN-enriched neuronal cell groups, supporting a canonical neuronal null rather than a target-local rewrite.
scope: P16 NeuN-enriched neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for Pax4 and Pdx1
statement: Pax4 or Pdx1 loss in postmitotic neurons does not activate a detectable islet endocrine transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: The Gnao1-centered contrast and related muscarinic, Mchr1, opioid, cAMP, and GIRK findings separate a narrow Puf60 response from a broader chronic GPCR transcriptome.
scope: Represented Gi/o, cAMP/GIRK, muscarinic, Mchr1, dopamine, and opioid comparator perturbations in basal postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: The L4/5 IT cortical Puf60 decrease after Gnao1 perturbation is not reproduced by represented Gi/o, cAMP/GIRK, muscarinic, opioid, or other neuromodulatory pathway relatives.

higher_order_basis: Multiple ciliary and ciliopathy-family perturbation comparisons independently show sparse, divergent, or cell-type-shifted RNA effects rather than an interchangeable ciliary gene-loss transcriptional state.
scope: Acute postnatal neuronal CRISPR transcriptomic responses for represented ciliary, transition-zone, and ciliopathy-family genes.
statement: Represented ciliary-gene perturbations can produce sparse neuronal RNA effects, but these effects are component- and cell-type-specific rather than a shared ciliopathy transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: Fe-S assembly/export, respiratory-chain Fe-S clients, lipoate-linked mitochondrial enzymes, and mtFAS-related effector comparisons consistently report absent phenocopying and near-zero shared RNA responses.
scope: Represented mitochondrial Fe-S, OXPHOS, lipoate-linked, and mtFAS-related perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented mitochondrial Fe-S, OXPHOS, lipoate-linked, and mtFAS-related perturbations do not produce a coherent shared acute postmitotic neuronal nuclear transcriptional loss-state in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Bmal1/Clock findings establish a shared measured clock-output axis, while Bmal1 feedback and Bmal2/Cry2 contrasts show asymmetric breadth and specificity.
scope: Postnatal neuronal clock-output genes including Nr1d2, Dbp, Per3, and Hhatl-like outputs across Bmal1- and Clock-responsive groups at a terminal endpoint.
statement: Bmal1 and Clock perturbations converge on measured neuronal clock-output genes, but Clock loss is a sparser phenocopy and Bmal1 loss exposes broader feedback-modified transcriptional effects.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal comparisons among represented ankyrin, spectrin, adducin, actin, and L1CAM-related scaffold perturbations report flat, sparse, or non-overlapping nuclear RNA responses rather than a common scaffold-loss program.
scope: Represented ankyrin/spectrin/adducin/actin/L1CAM membrane-skeleton perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented ankyrin/spectrin/adducin membrane-skeleton components do not converge on a shared postnatal neuronal nuclear RNA program.

higher_order_basis: Both findings support an absence of robust neuronal DE for the represented Myrf/Sox10 lineage neighborhood, while preserving the limitation that oligodendrocytes and several relevant lineage targets were not assayed.
scope: Represented neuronal perturbation surfaces for Myrf, Sox10, and Sox10-related targets; oligodendrocytes were not assayed.
statement: The represented Myrf/Sox10 oligodendrocyte-lineage regulatory neighborhood does not produce a robust postnatal neuronal differential-expression module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The Vps54 target-local warning is retained because multiple independent sphingolipid comparator findings establish that the relevant sphingolipid perturbation space itself lacked a detectable shared transcriptional direction in this assay.
scope: Vps54 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptome compared with represented sphingolipid perturbations; mRNA readout only, without sphingolipid intermediate measurement or pharmacologic myriocin equivalence.
statement: The acute Vps54 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptome does not transcriptionally nominate myriocin-class sphingolipid suppression as a therapeutic direction.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly support shared near-null Tshz2/Tshz3 single-paralog perturbation surfaces and use synaptic/ASD comparators only to bound assay detectability, not to define a positive shared program.
scope: P16 single-gene perturbation assay for represented Teashirt paralogs Tshz2 and Tshz3, with selected synaptic/ASD perturbations only as detectability boundaries; Tshz1 and double perturbations were not tested.
statement: Single-paralog perturbation of the represented Teashirt genes Tshz2 and Tshz3 yields a shared near-null neuronal transcriptional surface at P16.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly establish that an ISR/UPR-like neuronal stress program is detectable and convergent for Opa1-associated and other upstream insults, while Eif4g1 and Mdh1 define non-engaged or buffered boundaries.
scope: Neuronal ISR/UPR-like stress transcription involving Opa1, Elp1, Atp2a2, Gfpt1, Eif4g1, and Mdh1 perturbations.
statement: A detectable neuronal ATF4/ISR-like stress transcriptional state is engaged by Opa1-associated stress perturbations but absent or attenuated after Eif4g1 and Mdh1 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Both findings test represented fast presynaptic release or SNARE-cycle components in steady-state neuronal snRNA-seq and show flat, sparse, or divergent responses rather than a shared module.
scope: Steady-state postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq readouts for represented NSF/NAPB/SNARE and related release-machinery perturbations.
statement: Perturbing represented fast presynaptic release and SNARE-cycle machinery does not produce a shared steady-state neuronal transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: All supplied findings independently test measurable Dlx-family or adjacent forebrain GABAergic developmental perturbations and converge on absence of a shared postnatal RNA program, while retaining assay-detectability and missing-target caveats.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbations of represented Dlx-family and adjacent forebrain GABAergic developmental transcription-factor targets; Dlx1/2/5 and Lhx6 were not assayed as perturbation targets.
statement: Measured postnatal neuronal perturbations of Dlx3, Dlx6, Nkx2-1, and Arx-pathway proxies do not reconstitute a shared Dlx/Nkx2-1/Arx forebrain GABAergic transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: Across Gls-, Slc1a2-, Glud1-, and Slc1a1-centered contrasts, represented glutamate metabolic, GABA-branch, and transporter perturbations are flat, minimal, or mutually nonconvergent rather than forming a corrected neuronal snRNA-seq module.
scope: Represented glutamate metabolism, GABA-branch, alpha-ketoglutarate, and SLC1 glutamate-transporter perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq readouts.
statement: Represented glutamate metabolic, GABA-branch, and SLC1 glutamate-transporter perturbations generally do not produce a shared cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Across multiple Htr-family target-centered contrasts, represented serotonin receptor perturbations are repeatedly flat, sparse, near-zero correlated, or non-overlapping rather than collapsing into a common basal neuronal expression module.
scope: Single-gene perturbations of represented Htr1/2/3/4/6/7 serotonin receptors in unstimulated postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; ligand-evoked physiology and unrepresented receptors are outside scope.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented serotonin receptors do not produce a shared basal neuronal transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The supplied findings from Sin3a and Zswim6 show that chromatin/NDD-adjacent perturbations represented in this assay remain distinguishable rather than collapsing into one shared transcriptomic state.
scope: Measured postnatal neuronal transcriptomic perturbation space, with direct HDAC and SUZ12 perturbations absent.
statement: Represented Sin3a, Mecp2, Rest, and Zswim6 neuronal perturbations do not form one shared postnatal transcriptomic state in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Retinoid, RAR/RXR, Stra6, Greb1l, NR1H/LXR, PPAR, and RXR-partner findings repeatedly report flat, singleton, sparse, or nonconvergent outputs after acute single-gene perturbation rather than a shared basal neuronal receptor module.
scope: Represented retinoid/RAR/RXR and lipid nuclear-receptor single-gene perturbations in sampled postmitotic neuronal groups; Rara, Nr1h3, ligand addition, and combinatorial receptor loss were not tested.
statement: Represented retinoid/RAR/RXR and lipid nuclear-receptor single-gene perturbations do not produce a coherent shared acute neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: A direct Fntb sparse-response finding and an Hmgcr-related cross-perturbation contrast agree that Fntb does not behave as a generic lipid-regulator or downstream farnesylation transcriptional response in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
scope: Postmitotic juvenile neuronal perturbations involving Fntb and Hmgcr-related lipid regulator comparisons.
statement: Fntb perturbation is transcriptionally buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons and does not produce a generic lipid-regulator or downstream farnesylation response resembling Hmgcr perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Same-direction convergence findings place Kdm5c, Zmynd8, and Nsd1 in a shared thalamic chromatin-response module, while signature content and Zmynd11 contrast bound the module as derepressive, lineage-atypical/cryptic-like, and not generic to related ZMYND perturbation.
scope: Kdm5c, Zmynd8, Nsd1, and Zmynd11 perturbation signatures, primarily in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut where specified.
statement: Kdm5c, Zmynd8, and Nsd1 perturbations converge on a same-direction thalamic neuronal derepression module that is enriched for lineage-atypical or cryptic-like up-regulated genes and is not phenocopied by Zmynd11.

higher_order_basis: Cytolinker, plakin, spectraplakin, and related scaffold comparisons are flat or orthogonal in neuronal nuclear RNA readouts rather than forming a common cytoskeletal stress module.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq DE surfaces for represented cytolinker, plakin/spectraplakin, and related scaffold perturbations; protein loss and structural function were not directly assayed.
statement: Represented cytolinker, plakin/spectraplakin, and related scaffold perturbations do not produce a shared acute postnatal neuronal nuclear RNA module.

higher_order_basis: Two perturbations expected to affect neuronal excitability or cholinergic signaling independently lack sustained immediate-early/activity-regulated transcriptional responses in the weeks-after-perturbation nuclear RNA assay.
scope: Sparse postnatal Plcb1 and Ache loss in assayed neuronal nuclei, without stimulus locking and without sensitivity to minute-scale transients.
statement: Sparse postnatal loss of Plcb1 or Ache does not produce a sustained activity-regulated immediate-early transcriptional state detectable by this neuronal nuclear RNA assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple calcium-homeostasis perturbation contrasts identify Atp2a2/SERCA2 loss as the source of the detectable ER-stress UPR/ISR response, while related channels and pumps fail to phenocopy it in sampled neuronal contexts.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with supporting calcium-pump contrasts across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
statement: Atp2a2/SERCA2 loss selectively activates an ER-stress ISR/UPR neuronal transcriptional state that is not reproduced by assayed PMCA, SPCA1, calcium-release-channel, or isolated ATF6 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Group-I PAK paralog contrasts reject transcriptional interchangeability among Pak1, Pak2, and Pak3 while preserving that biochemical and spine-level convergence was not measured.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of Pak1, Pak2, Pak3, and proximal Rac/Cdc42/Limk comparators.
statement: Group-I PAK paralogs do not form an interchangeable shared neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The findings distinguish Zeb2's sparse, cell-type-selective postmitotic neuronal effect from absent Prop1 and pituitary-development comparator responses in the same measured neuronal groups.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbation responses involving Zeb2 and represented PROP1 pituitary-development comparator genes.
statement: Zeb2 has a sparse postmitotic neuronal transcriptional effect concentrated mainly in Pvalb GABA neurons that is not phenocopied by Prop1 or represented pituitary-development pathway comparators.

higher_order_basis: Both findings distinguish Pitpna from the sampled PI-transfer/phosphoinositide signaling neighborhood by showing a detectable Pitpna response that is not reproduced by Pitpnm3 or other sampled PI/PLC/PKC components.
scope: Matched thalamic, pineal/glutamatergic, and brainstem/myelencephalic neuronal groups represented for Pitpna/Pitpnm3 comparisons
statement: Pitpna perturbation elicits a distinct neuronal transcriptional response that is not a generic consequence of perturbing the sampled PI-transfer, PI4P-turnover, PLC, or PKC components.

higher_order_basis: Both Arl2bp- and Arl3-centered perturbation findings reject a shared neuronal DE signature for the biochemical ARL3/ARL2BP relationship, and broader ciliary comparator findings show that this pairwise nonconvergence occurs within a generally buffered ciliary perturbation landscape.
scope: Arl3, Arl2bp, and represented ciliopathy comparator perturbations in postnatal brain-neuron nuclei.
statement: The biochemical ARL3/ARL2BP ciliary relationship does not translate into a shared postnatal neuronal differential-expression signature.

higher_order_basis: Proposal 1a7463fb combines a broader proteostasis-machinery non-equivalence facet with an ER-client-stress facet. The broader facet is retained separately because Psmb4:F008 directly anchors that accessory stress regulators do not reproduce core proteasome damage, with ER findings supporting the general non-equivalence of nearby proteostasis components at the RNA-program level.
scope: Represented proteostasis and ER-stress regulators in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation readouts; RNA programs recovered after basal single-gene perturbation.
statement: Perturbing upstream stress regulators or accessory proteostasis genes does not reproduce the recovered RNA programs caused by damaging core proteostasis machinery in juvenile neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Abhd12 and Abhd2 independently reject convergence among represented ABHD/endocannabinoid/progesterone perturbations, while AMPAR findings bound the lack of coupling to a broader buffered receptor-complex context.
scope: Represented juvenile neuronal perturbations involving Abhd12, Abhd2, Cnr1, Pgr, and sampled AMPAR-complex comparators.
statement: Abhd12 and Abhd2 perturbations do not define an acute neuronal transcriptional module shared with represented 2-AG/cannabinoid, progesterone, or AMPAR-complex comparators.

higher_order_basis: Cry2 shares specific thalamic output directions with positive-limb perturbations, and Bmal1/Clock findings establish the relevant activator-loss comparator, bounding the result against simple negative-repressor inversion.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut clock-output genes Dbp and Nr1d1 under Cry2, Bmal1, and Clock perturbations at a single terminal endpoint.
statement: Cry2 loss is not the inverse of Bmal1/Clock activator loss for Dbp and Nr1d1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

higher_order_basis: Across multiple alpha and beta nicotinic receptor subunit perturbations, known receptor-family or co-assembly relationships repeatedly fail to yield shared-direction overlap or matched basal neuronal RNA signatures, with only isolated non-overlapping singleton responses.
scope: Represented nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit and selected cholinergic comparator perturbations in basal postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Single-subunit nicotinic acetylcholine receptor perturbations do not produce a shared basal neuronal transcriptional state among represented receptor-family members in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Direct PPAR/RXR-family perturbations and PPAR-adjacent contexts repeatedly show flat or nonconvergent responses, while individual Ppard-associated transcript changes are bounded as non-driver readouts.
scope: Basal neuronal perturbation signatures for represented PPAR/RXR receptors, coactivators, and PPAR-adjacent comparator contexts; ligand state and PPAR protein activity were not measured.
statement: The basal neuronal screen lacks a robust ligand-activated PPAR/RXR transcriptional perturbation module, even when Ppard is induced as a transcript-level component of another response.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal inverse-neighbor evidence centered on Dctn1 and Srebf2 establishes that the recurrent sterol gene set corresponds to SREBF2-dependent cholesterol regulon activity, while convergent Mib1/Htt/Marchf6/Selenoi findings show the endpoint recurs across perturbation contexts.
scope: Srebf2 significant sterol features and matched neuronal groups spanning Mib1, Dctn1, Htt, Marchf6, Selenoi, and related perturbations; upstream biochemical route is not established.
statement: Mib1, Dctn1, and related neuronal perturbations activate sterol genes that Srebf2 is required to maintain, identifying the recurrent module as SREBF2-linked cholesterol regulon activation.

higher_order_basis: Independent perturbation-centered comparisons across small GTPases, PAK/LIMK/cofilin, WRC, GEF/GAP, EphB, Tiam1, and Kalrn-related nodes report flat, singleton, or nonconvergent RNA outputs rather than recurrent pathway-wide nuclear expression.
scope: Represented Rho/Rac/Cdc42, Rac/EphB/PAK/WAVE, Kalirin/Tiam1, PAK/LIMK/cofilin, and related actin-cytoskeleton perturbations in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq surfaces.
statement: Represented Rac/Cdc42-linked actin-cytoskeleton signaling perturbations are transcriptionally buffered in assayed juvenile neurons rather than forming a recurrent shared nuclear mRNA module.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly compare AMPK/LKB1/SAD/MARK and mTOR/TSC-adjacent perturbations and distinguish flat or nonconvergent upstream/neighborhood perturbations from a detectable but independent Tsc2 transcriptional response.
scope: Postmitotic basal neuronal perturbation screen across represented AMPK, LKB1/SAD/MARK, mTOR, Raptor, and TSC-axis targets.
statement: Represented AMPK/LKB1-adjacent perturbations are transcriptionally uncoupled from the Tsc2/mTOR-axis response in postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: The findings separate cytosolic Hsp70, HSF1, DNAJB6, Hsp90ab1, and Hspa5 perturbation consequences rather than supporting one generic chaperone-loss or heat-shock/UPR transcriptional state.
scope: Represented chaperone, co-chaperone, HSF1, and ER-chaperone perturbations in the stated postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Represented chaperone and co-chaperone perturbations do not collapse onto a single heat-shock or UPR transcriptomic program in this postnatal neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: Both reciprocal findings support the absence of a detectable neuronal DE program for the represented ORC subunits, while noting that other ORC/pre-RC components were not represented.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal perturbation surfaces where Orc4 and Orc6 were represented; other ORC/pre-RC components were not tested.
statement: The represented ORC subunits Orc4 and Orc6 do not produce a detectable postmitotic neuronal differential-expression program in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Vps53, Vps54, and Cog5 findings each reject generic trafficking-pathway phenocopy among represented Golgi, retrograde trafficking, glycosylation, SNARE, retromer, and endolysosomal perturbations.
scope: Represented Golgi, COG, endosome-to-TGN, retromer, SNARE, and glycosylation perturbations in the acute neuronal loss-of-function assay.
statement: Represented Golgi and retrograde trafficking perturbations do not collapse into a generic neuronal transcriptional stress state in this assay.

higher_order_basis: All three findings test HIVEP paralogs and pathway-adjacent perturbations and converge on absence of an interchangeable acute neuronal transcriptomic response, with Hivep3's small response bounded as idiosyncratic.
scope: Postnatal neuronal transcriptomic perturbation assay across matched HIVEP-family and represented NF-kB/BMP/Runx2 comparators.
statement: Measured HIVEP paralog and canonical pathway-side perturbations do not form an interchangeable acute neuronal transcriptomic response in this dataset.

higher_order_basis: Both findings test expected embryonic NeuroD1/TCF12-linked developmental outputs after postnatal neuronal perturbation and find no detectable coherent secondary transcriptional program.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for Tcf12 and Neurod1 in measured neuronal groups.
statement: Postnatal Tcf12 or Neurod1 perturbation does not produce a detectable embryonic neuronal differentiation, cortical migration, or dopaminergic transcriptional program in the measured neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Two PAQR/progesterone-axis perturbation contrasts independently reject shared basal signatures, while Adipor2 provides a narrow singleton boundary rather than a convergent module.
scope: Measured PAQR/progesterone/adiponectin-receptor perturbations in basal juvenile neuronal nuclei; unmeasured PAQR and receptor-family members were not tested.
statement: The represented PAQR and progesterone-receptor perturbations do not produce a shared basal neuronal snRNA-seq module, apart from a narrow Adipor2-linked singleton response.

higher_order_basis: Both supplied findings test overlapping retinal and photoreceptor-axis genes from different target perspectives and converge on absence of a shared photoreceptor-like transcriptional state in sparse P16 brain neuronal groups.
scope: Represented retinal-lineage and photoreceptor-axis perturbations in sparse P16 brain CRISPR neuronal groups; not a retina assay.
statement: Represented photoreceptor-lineage perturbations fail to produce a shared photoreceptor-like transcriptional program in the assayed postnatal brain-neuron groups.

higher_order_basis: Hif1a, Arnt, Ahr, Ahrr, and Npas3 findings converge on a flat ARNT/AHR/HIF-axis response under basal postmitotic neuronal conditions, with Bmal1/Clock providing an internal assay-positive PAS-family contrast.
scope: Basal postmitotic neuronal groups tested for Hif1a, Arnt, Ahr, Ahrr, Npas3, and related bHLH-PAS perturbations; ligand, oxygen, and stimulus contexts were not directly varied.
statement: Basal postmitotic neuronal nuclei in this assay do not show a detectable ARNT/AHR/HIF-dependent transcriptional state after acute perturbation of represented ARNT/AHR/HIF-axis genes.

higher_order_basis: The Grin2a finding establishes an induced activity-linked adaptive RNA response after NMDAR perturbation, while the Calm2 comparison shows this response is not reproduced by loss of a Ca2+/CaM pathway neighbor.
scope: Cortical and thalamic neuronal RNA responses after Grin2a and Calm2 loss-of-function perturbations.
statement: Grin2a loss can induce activity-dependent adaptive transcriptional genes in cortical responders, whereas Calm2 loss does not phenocopy that Ca2+/CaM-activity RNA program.

higher_order_basis: Multiple DGC/DAPC, dystroglycan, sarcoglycan, and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation perturbation comparisons independently report flat, near-flat, sparse, or non-overlapping neuronal snRNA-seq surfaces, with protein/glycan and developmental timing limitations preserved.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation assay across represented DGC/DAPC, dystroglycan, sarcoglycan, alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, matriglycan, neurexin, and related muscular-dystrophy comparator targets.
statement: Represented dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation perturbations do not produce a coherent shared postnatal neuronal nuclear RNA module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Findings centered on Rtn4r, Lingo2, S1pr2, and Lingo1 repeatedly test receptor-complex or pathway-neighbor convergence and find isolated, flat, or divergent transcriptomic effects rather than a recurrent Nogo receptor-complex mRNA program.
scope: Represented Nogo/LINGO/NGFR/RTN4R/S1PR2-axis perturbations in uninjured juvenile neuronal nuclei.
statement: Represented Nogo receptor-complex and S1PR2-axis perturbations do not generate a recurrent shared neuronal transcriptomic program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple matched comparator findings separate assay-detectable receptor-subunit RNA responses from flat or nonconvergent downstream scaffold, CaMKII/calmodulin, and RapGEF-related perturbation surfaces.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal single-nucleus CRISPR perturbation groups represented for NMDAR/AMPAR subunits, PSD scaffolds, Syngap1, Camk2b/calmodulins, and Rapgef2/Magi2-related targets.
statement: Assay-detectable NMDAR subunit perturbations do not imply a shared acute transcriptomic response for downstream CaMKII, calmodulin, PSD scaffold, AMPAR, or RapGEF2/Magi2-related perturbations in matched postnatal neurons.

higher_order_basis: Mesp2 and Tbx6 findings jointly establish that canonical embryonic segmentation-clock/somitogenesis genes are not engaged in this postnatal neuronal context, while the disease-module warning bounds interpretation without adding a separate atomic proposition.
scope: Postnatal neuronal Mesp2 and Tbx6 perturbations, including CTX-CGE GABA for Tbx6
statement: Postnatal neuronal Mesp2 and Tbx6 perturbations do not engage the canonical embryonic somitogenesis/Notch segmentation-clock transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: BCAA/leucine catabolic, BCKDH regulatory, electron-transfer, ISR, mTOR, and organic-acid comparator findings converge on flat or nonconvergent neuronal transcriptomic surfaces despite pathway adjacency.
scope: Represented mitochondrial BCAA/leucine catabolism, BCKDH-axis, ETF-adjacent, ISR, mTOR-pathway, and organic-acid catabolic targets in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Basal postnatal neuronal perturbation of represented BCAA and related organic-acid catabolic nodes is transcriptionally buffered rather than converted into a detectable nuclear BCAA-flux, ATF4/ISR, mTOR, or catabolic-feedback program.

higher_order_basis: The component contains a detectable Rora neuronal transcriptional response, but represented IL-23/IL-12 receptor, STAT, and Th17-related perturbations are flat or singleton-only and do not phenocopy that response.
scope: Il23r-matched neuronal groups comparing Rora with represented IL-23/IL-12 receptor, STAT, NF-kB, and Th17-related perturbations.
statement: Rora's strong neuronal transcriptional response is separable from, and should not be interpreted as, an IL-23R/IL-12/23 receptor or STAT pathway phenocopy in this dataset.

higher_order_basis: Reln-centered negative readouts and broader pathway buffering together support absence of a sustained nuclear compensation program after sparse postnatal Reln loss.
scope: Postnatal sparse Reln loss-of-function nuclear RNA response after a 3-4 week interval; not acute ligand addition or enhancer activation assays.
statement: Postnatal sparse Reln loss does not induce a sustained immediate-early, synaptic-plasticity, receptor-feedback, or enhancer-associated nuclear RNA compensation program detectable by this assay.

higher_order_basis: Retinal/ciliary-gate and ciliopathy-associated perturbation findings centered on Rpgr, Iqcb1, Spata7, Rpgrip1l, Arl3, and Cep290 repeatedly show flat, sparse, or orthogonal nuclear RNA surfaces rather than shared brain-neuron transcriptomic phenocopies.
scope: Represented retinal/ciliary-gate and ciliopathy-associated perturbations in postnatal NeuN+ brain-neuron snRNA-seq; protein trafficking, photoreceptor-specific contexts, and unrepresented ciliary targets were not directly tested.
statement: Represented retinal/ciliary-gate disease relationships are not reflected as shared basal transcriptomic phenocopies in assayed postnatal brain neurons.

higher_order_basis: Bach2 and Mafg pathway-uncoupling findings establish that the Hmox1/ARE-like response is not a generic Bach/NRF/Maf-family loss response, with Nfe2l2 and Maf comparisons bounding the scope.
scope: Pvalb and matched neuronal responses involving Bach2, Mafg, Nfe2l2, and represented Maf-family comparators.
statement: Mafg loss selectively engages an Hmox1-associated Pvalb response that is not reproduced by Bach2 loss, Nfe2l2 loss, or represented large-Maf perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Across multiple MAS components in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, cytosolic enzyme perturbations repeatedly show small amino-acid/stress and synaptic signatures, whereas mitochondrial enzyme and carrier perturbations are flat or nearly flat.
scope: Malate-aspartate-shuttle perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons; transcriptomic contrasts do not establish metabolite flux.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, the acute malate-aspartate-shuttle transcriptional response is selective for the cytosolic Got1/Mdh1 arm rather than a generic response to perturbing mitochondrial or carrier MAS components.

higher_order_basis: Cux2:F001 provides the direct Sun1-up perturbation effect, while Cux1:F003 supplies distinct-target paralog contrast against a convergent Cux1/Cux2-family module.
scope: 053 Sst Gaba and Cux1/Cux2 perturbations represented in the assayed neuronal screen
statement: Cux2 loss produces Sun1 up-regulation in 053 Sst Gaba that is not part of a convergent Cux1/Cux2-family transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: Both cohesin-related perturbations in the same thalamic neuronal class converge on down-regulated neuronal connectivity/signaling transcriptomic gene classes, with the assay caveat that chromatin contacts and electrophysiology were not directly measured.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons after postnatal Smc1a or Stag2 perturbation.
statement: Smc1a and Stag2 loss both depress a thalamic postmitotic neuronal connectivity/signaling transcriptomic module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: The represented WNK/SPAK/CCC pathway members repeatedly show no common FDR-level transcriptional convergence, while findings preserve the limitation that canonical biology may occur through phosphorylation, chloride flux, or non-RNA endpoints.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation readouts for represented WNK1/WNK3/STK39/SLC12A2-centered chloride-cotransporter pathway members.
statement: Acute single-gene perturbation of represented WNK-SPAK/cation-chloride cotransporter pathway members does not produce a shared basal neuronal nuclear-RNA signature in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Both Maf- and Mafb-centered findings independently test expected neonatal Maf/Mafb interneuron-program genes and find them absent after sparse single-gene P16 perturbation.
scope: Sparse single-gene Maf or Mafb perturbation in P16 postmitotic interneuron populations represented here.
statement: The canonical neonatal Maf/Mafb MGE-interneuron transcriptional program is not reactivated by sparse single-gene Maf or Mafb perturbation at P16.

higher_order_basis: Cry1-specific and related clock-node contrasts show that the 151 thalamic group can detect broad clock programs, yet Cry1 loss remains Per2-selective and non-phenocopying.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut clock-network perturbation readouts at a single endpoint; phase-only effects are not tested.
statement: Cry1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produces a Per2-selective RNA response rather than a broad core-clock reset or a phenocopy of other active clock-loop perturbations.

higher_order_basis: mTORC1-related findings show that same-pathway membership is not interchangeable at the basal neuronal RNA endpoint: positive core or upstream PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 nodes are flat or mutually non-phenocopying, while downstream or negative-regulator contexts remain distinguishable.
scope: Basal juvenile neuronal transcriptomic screen for represented PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway perturbations, including Mtor, Rptor, Depdc5, Strada, Pik3r1, Pik3cb, Akt3, and Tsc2-related comparators.
statement: In basal juvenile neurons, represented upstream PI3K/Akt and positive mTORC1-associated perturbations are transcriptionally buffered or mutually non-phenocopying rather than forming a shared PI3K/mTOR RNA signature.

higher_order_basis: The reciprocal paralog-centered findings reject a shared generic NR2C-family neuronal transcriptomic response while preserving the assay limits of represented targets and single-gene perturbations.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal perturbation signatures for represented NR2C-family targets in the supplied neighborhood.
statement: Nr2c1 and Nr2c2 loss produce non-interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic signatures rather than a shared generic NR2C-family response.

higher_order_basis: Ctnnb1 perturbation establishes that canonical beta-catenin/Wnt feedback targets are detectable in the assay, while Prickle1 perturbation shows those targets are not derepressed by Prickle1 loss.
scope: Prickle1 and Ctnnb1 perturbations in the supplied juvenile neuronal snRNA assay, with strongest positive Wnt readout in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Prickle1 loss does not act as a dominant basal brake on canonical beta-catenin target transcription in these juvenile neurons, despite assay-detectable Ctnnb1-dependent Wnt feedback transcripts.

higher_order_basis: The Cpe-, Pcsk2-, and Pcsk5-centered findings reciprocally test represented neuropeptide/proprotein-processing targets and consistently report sparse, nonoverlapping, nonconvergent RNA responses.
scope: Represented Cpe, Pcsk2, and Pcsk5 perturbations in the postnatal neuronal nuclear transcriptomic assay; Pcsk1, Furin, Pam, and related targets were not directly tested.
statement: Represented Cpe, Pcsk2, and Pcsk5 neuropeptide/proprotein-processing perturbations do not form a shared basal neuronal nuclear transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: Both findings independently distinguish postnatal neuronal loss-of-function signatures for MAPK pathway genes from germline developmental gain-of-function RASopathy mechanisms.
scope: P16 NeuN+ neuronal CRISPR loss-of-function perturbations of Map2k1 and Braf with RASopathy-related pathway comparators.
statement: Postnatal neuronal loss of Map2k1 or Braf does not model the broad transcriptional activation expected from developmental gain-of-function RASopathy alleles.

higher_order_basis: The reciprocal Grin2a and Mef2c findings support a restricted shared cortical activity-linked state while excluding a generic NMDAR/calcium pathway phenocopy.
scope: L4-5 IT CTX Glut and L2-3 IT CTX Glut perturbation signatures for Mef2c, Grin2a, and related NMDAR/calcium comparators.
statement: Mef2c and Grin2a perturbations share a restricted cortical activity-linked transcriptional state that is not a generic NMDAR, CaMK, calcineurin, or Syngap1 loss signature.

higher_order_basis: Multiple same-complex GABA_B receptor, KCTD auxiliary, GIRK/channel, and proximal effector perturbations either remain flat or fail to share directional transcriptomic responses, with a restricted Gabbr1 exception.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation readout for represented GABA_B receptor, KCTD auxiliary, GIRK, channel, and proximal signaling targets.
statement: The represented GABA_B receptor/auxiliary/effector cassette does not generate a shared stable nuclear RNA program in the neuronal CRISPR screen.

higher_order_basis: Each finding reports flat, isolated, near-orthogonal, or non-overlapping signatures among directly represented NRG ligands and ERBB receptors in the same sparse neuronal perturbation setting.
scope: Cell-autonomous sparse neuronal perturbations of represented NRG ligands, ERBB receptors, and Adam10 in the juvenile snRNA screen.
statement: Directly represented NRG ligand and ERBB receptor perturbations do not resolve into a coherent cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional module in this postnatal mosaic snRNA assay.

higher_order_basis: Endomembrane pH, NHE, CLC, and V-ATPase comparator findings show non-convergence among acidification-related perturbations, while Cltc responsiveness bounds the result as not global inability to detect vesicle-related transcription.
scope: P16 postmitotic neuronal snRNA perturbation readouts for represented endomembrane acidification, NHE, CLC, V-ATPase, and vesicle-trafficking genes.
statement: Shared endomembrane acidification annotation is insufficient to produce a conserved neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation module among represented NHE, CLC, and V-ATPase relatives.

higher_order_basis: Snta1 and sodium-channel findings jointly show that membrane-localization or channel-partnership biology is not mirrored by a shared NeuN+ neuronal nuclear RNA program.
scope: NeuN+ neuronal RNA readouts for Snta1 and represented sodium-channel-associated perturbations; glial compartments and protein localization are outside scope.
statement: Canonical Snta1-linked membrane-localization and sodium-channel-associated biology is not recovered as a shared NeuN+ neuronal mRNA program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The supplied Hcn1, Hcn2, and Ptchd1-centered findings all constrain electrically or pharmacologically related HCN/SK components as lacking a robust shared RNA response in sampled postmitotic neuronal groups, with electrophysiological and TRN limitations preserved.
scope: Sampled non-TRN P16-edited postmitotic neuronal groups in the mosaic snRNA-seq assay; Hcn3, Hcn4, TRIP8b/Pex5l, DNA indel status, electrophysiology, and TRN functional rescue are not directly assayed.
statement: Electrical or pharmacological relationships among Ptchd1-linked SK/HCN components and Hcn1/Hcn2 do not manifest as a shared SK/HCN transcriptional response in the sampled postmitotic neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Across distinct perturbations of the hexosamine/O-GlcNAc axis, O-GlcNAc-cycle transcripts move downward rather than showing simple reciprocal writer/eraser induction, with Gpi1 limiting the inference to transcript-level and context-dependent responses.
scope: O-GlcNAc-cycle transcript responses in the supplied neuronal cell groups, without direct O-GlcNAc protein or metabolite measurements.
statement: Neuronal perturbations of Gfpt1 and Ogt repress O-GlcNAc-cycle transcripts Ogt and/or Oga rather than inducing simple reciprocal O-GlcNAc-cycle compensation.

higher_order_basis: Both SALL-centered findings reject shared transcriptomic convergence with represented SALL/NuRD-related comparators in postnatal neuronal perturbation contexts.
scope: Represented SALL and NuRD-related perturbations in postnatal neuronal CRISPR transcriptomes.
statement: Represented SALL-family perturbations do not produce a shared SALL/NuRD-like postmitotic neuronal transcriptional phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Both collagen-centered findings test cartilage or chondrocyte-associated genes and perturbation comparators in sampled neuronal nuclei and find no coherent cartilage-like ECM remodeling program, with inference limited to represented genes and neuronal nuclear RNA.
scope: Col11a1 and Col2a1 cartilage-collagen/chondrocyte-regulator perturbation context in sampled postnatal neuronal nuclei.
statement: Cartilage-collagen perturbations do not induce a coherent chondrocyte-like ECM remodeling transcriptional program in sampled postnatal neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: The Atp6v1e1 finding defines the restricted V-ATPase-associated response, while the Manba comparator finding shows V-ATPase perturbations do not align with a generic Manba-like lysosomal transcriptomic phenotype.
scope: Manba, Atp6v0a1, and Atp6v1e1 perturbations in the matched neuronal groups represented in this neighborhood.
statement: V-ATPase perturbations do not produce a generic lysosomal transcriptomic phenotype in this assay; Atp6v0a1 is flat and Atp6v1e1 yields only a weak, restricted neuronal signaling-state response.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal cross-perturbation contrasts among the assayed 14-3-3 paralogs converge on non-phenocopy and near-null transcriptomic responses, with scope limited by unmeasured paralogs and absent protein-stoichiometry data.
scope: Assayed Ywhae, Ywhag, and Ywhaz perturbations in the P16 postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic screen.
statement: Acute loss of the assayed 14-3-3 paralogs does not produce an interchangeable shared neuronal RNA program in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly contrast strong detectable RBP/RNA-processing responses with weak or flat hnRNP-family surfaces and reject simple family-level phenocopy among measured hnRNP-family perturbations.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbation responses among measured hnRNP-family and related nuclear RNA-binding proteins.
statement: Measured hnRNP-family perturbations are not interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic states, with Hnrnpu/Hnrnpc-like RBP responses remaining distinct from weak or flat Hnrnpdl and Hnrnpa2b1 surfaces.

higher_order_basis: Across EphA and EphB receptor perturbations and proximal signaling-node comparisons, the findings repeatedly show flat, singleton-only, or non-overlapping neuronal RNA surfaces rather than a shared Eph-family nuclear module.
scope: Represented Eph-family receptor and proximal Eph signaling perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Single represented Eph receptor perturbations in postnatal neurons do not produce a common Eph-family nuclear transcriptomic program, instead showing flat or receptor-specific sparse effects.

higher_order_basis: Across perturbations of Schwann-cell, oligodendrocyte, myelin, and neural-crest regulators, the expected lineage programs are repeatedly absent in NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei, indicating assay-compartment mismatch rather than falsification of canonical glial biology.
scope: NeuN-enriched postnatal neuronal perturbation surfaces for Adgrg6, Sox10, Nkx6-2, Myrf, and Egr2; not direct tests of glial, Schwann-cell, neural-crest, or myelination-window biology.
statement: Canonical Schwann-cell, oligodendrocyte, neural-crest, and myelin transcriptional programs are not recovered after perturbing their represented regulators in the sampled NeuN-enriched postnatal neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple represented Kv7-family contrasts converge on sparse, target-specific transcriptional effects rather than a shared Kcnq1/Kcnq2/Kcnq3 neuronal RNA program, with Akap9 limiting interpretation outside neuronal snRNA-seq.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA Perturb-seq across represented Kcnq1, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, and Akap9 perturbations; Kcnq5 was not represented as a perturbation target.
statement: Represented Kv7-family channel perturbations produce sparse, paralog-specific neuronal transcriptional outputs rather than a shared Kcnq1/Kcnq2/Kcnq3 response program.

higher_order_basis: Both findings directly test represented polyamine-neighborhood perturbations and find absence of convergent neuronal RNA programs, with caveats that many core polyamine nodes and flux measurements were not assayed.
scope: Represented polyamine/ATP13/EIF5A/Sms perturbations in this neuronal screen; Atp13a4, Atp13a5, and many core polyamine enzymes were not represented, and polyamine flux was not measured.
statement: Represented polyamine-neighborhood perturbations did not produce interchangeable Sms- or Atp13a3-like neuronal transcriptional phenotypes in this dataset.

higher_order_basis: Bmal2, Btbd9, and Rorb each fail to engage the detected Bmal1/Clock/Nr1d-type clock transcript program, while Bmal1/Clock convergence provides the assay-positive comparator.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation contexts for Bmal2, Btbd9, Rorb, and measured Bmal1/Clock/Nr1d clock comparators.
statement: Bmal2, Btbd9, and Rorb perturbations are transcriptionally uncoupled from the clock-output program detected after core Bmal1/Clock/Nr1d-axis perturbations in this neuronal screen.

higher_order_basis: Direct hydrolase and M6P-trafficking comparisons show repeated matched-group flatness, with the Gnptg finding providing a biologically plausible but unmeasured mosaic rescue caveat.
scope: Represented soluble lysosomal hydrolase, cargo and M6P-pathway perturbations in acute sparse neuronal CRISPR snRNA-seq; enzyme cross-correction and storage burden were not directly measured.
statement: Represented lysosomal hydrolase and M6P-pathway perturbations are largely buffered at the acute neuronal mRNA level in this sparse mosaic assay rather than converging on a broad storage-stress transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: All represented kainate-receptor subunit findings report flat, near-zero, or sparse idiosyncratic downstream RNA effects rather than recurrent family-level transcriptomic convergence.
scope: Represented kainate receptor subunit perturbations in the postnatal mosaic neuronal snRNA-seq screen; Grik2 and Neto auxiliary subunits were not tested, and shared electrophysiological effects are not excluded.
statement: Represented kainate receptor subunit perturbations do not form a shared basal neuronal transcriptomic response module.

higher_order_basis: The Cblb-centered immune-program absence is biologically distinct from generic PI3K buffering because it localizes canonical Cbl-b immune-checkpoint transcription outside the NeuN+ neuronal context, while PI3K-neighbor findings support the absence of a hidden neuronal proximal pathway response.
scope: NeuN+ neuronal assay lacking T/NK cell contexts and most TCR components.
statement: The canonical Cbl-b immune-checkpoint transcriptional program is absent from the assayed NeuN+ neuronal populations.

higher_order_basis: Nsd1, Nsd2, and Ash1l findings consistently show weak, null, or divergent transcriptomic surfaces among represented H3K36-linked regulators, with detectable Setd1a/Sin3a responses limiting the interpretation to selective buffering or nonconvergence rather than assay-wide insensitivity.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal mRNA responses to represented H3K36-axis and related chromatin-regulator perturbations.
statement: Represented H3K36-linked chromatin regulator perturbations do not behave as interchangeable sources of a shared postmitotic neuronal transcriptional response.

higher_order_basis: Both matrix-associated perturbations fail to engage expected extracellular-matrix-linked TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD transcriptional programs in postmitotic neurons.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal perturbation assay for represented fibrillin, Adamts17, TGF-beta/BMP receptor, integrin, ECM, and SMAD targets; conclusion is absence of a detectable module, not proof of complete knockout for each comparator.
statement: Fbn1 and Adamts17 perturbations do not engage a detectable extracellular-matrix-linked TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD transcriptional module in the assayed postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: The component contains direct Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 same-direction convergence in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and an independent Nr5a2 contrast showing that a related transcription-factor loss does not reproduce that Wnt/TCF-like thalamic response; Ctnnb1 neighborhood data bound the claim against overinterpreting all shared Ctnnb1 biology as exclusively Wnt/TCF.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut β-catenin/TCF transcriptomic response
statement: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 loss converge on a 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Wnt/TCF-associated transcriptional signature that is not reproduced by Nr5a2 loss.

higher_order_basis: The two reciprocal represented-TMEM63 paralog contrasts agree that TMEM63-family relatedness does not produce interchangeable acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomic loss-of-function surfaces under this assay.
scope: Represented Tmem63b and Tmem63c perturbations in the postnatal neuronal transcriptomic assay; Tmem63a and paralog co-deletion were not tested.
statement: Tmem63b and Tmem63c loss produce non-interchangeable postnatal neuronal transcriptomic surfaces despite represented TMEM63-family channel relatedness.

higher_order_basis: Direct IRF1 and STAT1 negative gene-panel evidence, plus cross-perturbation IRF/STAT/receptor/pathogen-sensor contrasts, shows no coherent basal IFN, ISG, MHC-I antigen-processing, or inflammatory RNA module in postmitotic neuronal nuclei.
scope: Unchallenged juvenile/postnatal postmitotic neuronal nuclei across represented IFN receptor, STAT, IRF, NF-kB-neighbor, and pathogen-sensor perturbations.
statement: Basal loss or perturbation of represented IFN-receptor, STAT, IRF, NF-kB-neighbor, and pathogen-sensor genes does not engage a coherent neuronal IFN/ISG/MHC-I inflammatory transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: One finding establishes a recurrent Opa1-positive ATF4/ISR-like mitochondrial stress program, while multiple independent mitochondrial target findings use Opa1 as an internal positive benchmark to show that other perturbations remain below that transcriptional response threshold.
scope: Mitochondrial perturbations measured in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq, especially Opa1-responsive subcortical neuronal groups; Opa1 is a mitochondrial-stress comparator rather than a same-complex phenocopy for the other targets.
statement: In this neuronal snRNA-seq assay, Opa1 perturbation activates a detectable ATF4/mitochondrial ISR-like amino-acid stress program, whereas represented mitochondrial comparators including Gfm2, Coa8, Ndufs2, Sucla2, Mff, Isca2, Ndufv1, Sod2, and Ndufa4 do not cross that transcriptional-response threshold.

higher_order_basis: Mib1- and Dll1-centered findings separate recurrent Mib1 sterol-gene induction from Dll1 loss and from canonical Delta-Notch receptor/protease transcriptional readouts.
scope: Mib1, Dll1, and represented Notch receptor/protease perturbations in postmitotic neuronal groups.
statement: Mib1 perturbation drives a recurrent neuronal sterol-biosynthetic transcriptional response that is uncoupled from canonical Dll1-Notch transcriptional signaling.

higher_order_basis: Direct positive perturbation findings across translation-quality, mitochondrial, ER-calcium, and Thap11 contexts report overlapping amino-acid transporter, tRNA-charging, and serine/one-carbon transcripts, with strongest shared thalamic representation for Elongator/Thap11 facets.
scope: Susceptible postmitotic neuronal populations, prominently 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Opa1-, Elp1-, Elp2-, Thap11-, and Atp2a2-responsive groups; transcriptomic assays do not directly measure flux, eIF2α phosphorylation, or tRNA chemistry.
statement: Selected Opa1, Elp1, Elp2, Atp2a2, and Thap11 perturbations induce an ATF4-like neuronal metabolic stress program coupling amino-acid import, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase transcripts, and serine/one-carbon metabolism in susceptible postmitotic neuronal populations.

higher_order_basis: Both IFNGR receptor subunits and downstream STAT/IRF pathway evidence fail to recover expected IFN-gamma/MHC-I antigen-presentation RNA programs in basal postmitotic neurons, restricting such mechanisms to cytokine exposure, developmental timing, or specific circuits not tested here.
scope: Basal loss-of-function perturbations in juvenile postmitotic mouse neuronal groups without exogenous IFN-gamma stimulation or developmental progenitor exposure.
statement: Basal loss of Ifngr1, Ifngr2, or Stat1 in juvenile postmitotic neurons does not activate, reverse, or expose the expected interferon-stimulated MHC-I antigen-presentation RNA program.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly test represented ESC/self-renewal and reprogramming-axis factors in postnatal neurons and support absence of a convergent neuronal transcriptomic module, with missing-partner caveats preserved.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbation assay for represented ESC/self-renewal and reprogramming-axis factors.
statement: Canonical ESC/self-renewal and reprogramming-axis factors do not form a convergent postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Iron entry, IRP2 regulation, Fe-S/heme-adjacent biology, and TfR-recycling-related findings agree that canonical iron-homeostasis mRNA programs are absent or nonconvergent in assayed juvenile neurons.
scope: Acute P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neuronal nuclear RNA perturbation readouts involving Tfrc, Ireb2, Reps1, Abcb7, and represented iron/HIF/Fe-S comparators.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented iron-entry, IRP2, Fe-S/heme-adjacent, and TfR-recycling-related genes does not elicit a shared canonical iron-homeostasis mRNA program in assayed juvenile neurons.

higher_order_basis: NFI-family findings repeatedly reject strong single-paralog phenocopy in postmitotic neurons, while Bbx bounds developmental NFIX-related circuitry to progenitor or developmental contexts not assayed here.
scope: Acute single-gene perturbations of represented NFI paralogs in sampled postnatal neuronal nuclei; does not test embryonic progenitors, astrocytes, subtle compensation, or combined NFI perturbations.
statement: Single NFI paralog perturbations in sampled postnatal neurons do not reveal an interchangeable NFI-family transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: Three KRAB-ZFP-centered findings independently show flat or non-phenocopying individual zinc-finger perturbations despite a detectable Setdb1-associated neuronal response.
scope: Zfp1, Zfp950, Zfp846, and Setdb1 comparisons in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: The individual KRAB/C2H2 zinc-finger perturbations Zfp1, Zfp950, and Zfp846 are not rate-limiting for the Setdb1-sensitive neuronal repressive transcriptomic response detected in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple complex-III perturbation comparisons jointly show that structural complex-III genes generally produced weak or absent neuronal snRNA-seq responses, while the few recovered downstream events were isolated and target-specific rather than a shared complex-level transcriptomic program.
scope: Represented complex-III perturbations in assayed neuronal snRNA-seq cell groups; not direct respiratory-chain activity measurements.
statement: Represented respiratory complex III components are largely transcriptionally buffered in neuronal nuclei and do not induce a shared complex-III depletion RNA signature.

higher_order_basis: Across REST-adjacent, methyl-CpG reader/writer, MBD-family, ZMYND-family, and represented NuRD comparisons, related chromatin perturbations are measurable but largely non-interchangeable at the neuronal RNA-surface level.
scope: Represented REST-adjacent, methyl-CpG reader/writer, MBD-family, ZMYND-family, NuRD-related, and chromatin-NDD perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq surfaces.
statement: Represented chromatin-repressor, methyl-CpG, MBD-family, ZMYND-family, and NuRD-adjacent perturbations produce target-selective neuronal RNA phenotypes rather than one shared generic chromatin-regulator loss signature.

higher_order_basis: Calcineurin regulatory and catalytic subunit findings show weak, selective RNA responses concentrated in Ppp3r1 and partly Ppp3ca, while Ppp3cc, Ppib, Fkbp1a, and Nfatc3 are flat or non-interchangeable.
scope: Measured calcineurin, NFAT, FKBP/immunophilin, and calcium-channel related perturbations, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and matched cortical/thalamic contexts.
statement: Detectable calcineurin-axis RNA responses in this assay are subunit-selective and centered on Ppp3r1 and partly Ppp3ca rather than a shared NFAT-like or immunophilin-equivalent neuronal transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: A direct Klf7 perturbation response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is paired with failure of Fbxo38 loss to reproduce that same transcriptomic state in the matched cell group.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut juvenile thalamic neurons in the postnatal transcriptomic perturbation assay.
statement: Klf7 loss produces a juvenile thalamic transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut that is not reproduced by Fbxo38 loss in the same cell group.

higher_order_basis: All supplied findings test represented RTK-family members or proximal signaling comparators and report flat, sparse, or nonconvergent neuronal transcriptional effects rather than a shared RTK module.
scope: Represented neuronal type-III RTK, neurotrophin-RTK, and proximal signaling perturbations in the supplied component.
statement: Represented Kit, Csf1r, Pdgfrb, and Flt3-related RTK perturbations do not define a shared postmitotic neuronal RTK transcriptional module in the assayed contexts.

higher_order_basis: The two cross-perturbation findings test clinically adjacent Rett/DEE genes and reject interchangeability of their acute neuronal transcriptomic states, while preserving that some comparators are detectable and others are quiet.
scope: Acute neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of represented Rett/DEE-neighbor genes.
statement: Clinically related Rett/DEE genes do not define a single interchangeable acute cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptomic state in this assay.

higher_order_basis: One finding establishes the Lrp6-Ctnnb1 thalamic convergence, while two distinct target-gene contrasts define non-engagement by Antxr2 and Lrp4 in overlapping thalamic comparisons.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and overlapping thalamic neuronal comparisons in the postnatal snRNA-seq assay; convergence is strongest for the shared Axin2-containing direction.
statement: The thalamic Axin2-containing Wnt/beta-catenin transcriptional response is engaged by Lrp6-Ctnnb1 perturbation convergence but not by Antxr2 or Lrp4 loss.

higher_order_basis: The Vcp finding provides the positive proteostasis-neighbor signal, while the Kbtbd7 finding limits that signal away from a Kbtbd7-dependent VANGL ERAD/Wnt-PCP transcriptomic program.
scope: Vcp and Kbtbd7-centered proteostasis/ERAD-related perturbations in the reported responder neuronal groups
statement: The small Vcp-associated neuronal transcriptional response aligns with measured proteostasis perturbations but does not extend to a Kbtbd7-dependent VANGL ERAD/Wnt-PCP response.

higher_order_basis: Calm3 and Ppp3ca pathway-uncoupling findings anchor nonconvergence among canonical CaM/calcineurin/CaMKII-adjacent effectors, with CaMKII contrasts extending the pattern while preserving assay limitations.
scope: Steady-state postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq readouts for represented calmodulin, calcineurin/NFAT, CaMKII, PKC, and IP3R-related perturbations; not calcium dynamics, localization, or phosphoproteomic signaling.
statement: Represented Ca2+/calmodulin and calcineurin-adjacent effector perturbations do not collapse onto a common steady-state neuronal transcriptional readout in this assay.

higher_order_basis: All three findings compare PUR-family perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups and consistently show robust Pura-specific transcriptional output with Purb weak/private and Purg absent.
scope: PUR-repeat family perturbations in acute postnatal neuronal Perturb-seq.
statement: PUR-repeat paralogs are not transcriptionally interchangeable in P16 neurons, with robust neuronal mRNA consequences localized to Pura loss rather than generic PUR-family depletion.

higher_order_basis: The direct Prdm10 module and multiple PRDM-family contrasts distinguish a recurrent Prdm10 neuronal RNA response from flat or non-overlapping responses for represented Prdm2, Prdm5, and Prdm16 perturbations.
scope: Postnatal neuronal transcriptomic perturbation assay across represented PRDM-family targets; Prdm15 was not represented and evidence is transcriptomic rather than chromatin-binding based.
statement: Prdm10 loss produces a distinct recurrent mostly down-regulated postnatal neuronal RNA module that is not shared by represented Prdm2, Prdm5, or Prdm16 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Synuclein-centered and presynaptic-vesicle/endocytic contrasts repeatedly show flat, sparse, or nonconvergent soma-transcriptional surfaces, while Cltc-related findings bound this as biological nonconvergence rather than total assay invisibility.
scope: Represented synuclein, synaptic-vesicle, SNARE-associated, uncoating, and dynamin perturbations in the acute postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq screen.
statement: Represented synuclein and presynaptic-vesicle perturbations do not form a shared acute neuronal soma-transcriptional module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The Glis3 negative result is bounded by a positive Manf detector perturbation, supporting assay capacity to detect UPR signatures while preserving cell-group restriction.
scope: Measured postnatal neuronal groups in the snRNA perturbation assay, with Manf serving as a UPR detectability comparator rather than a same-complex GLIS3 comparator.
statement: Acute Glis3 loss is uncoupled from a detectable neuronal UPR/autophagy ER-stress transcriptional response despite assay capacity to detect Manf-induced UPR signatures.

higher_order_basis: Several TLR-family, CD14, NF-kappaB/IRF, and IFN-pathway perturbation contrasts independently show null, near-zero-correlated, or isolated non-overlapping responses rather than a coherent basal TLR/PRR transcriptional program.
scope: Basal matched neuronal Perturb-seq groups with represented TLR-family, CD14, innate immune receptor, NF-kappaB/IRF, and IFN-pathway perturbations; ligand challenge and several adaptors were not tested.
statement: Represented TLR/CD14 and innate receptor perturbations in unchallenged neuronal Perturb-seq conditions do not form a coherent shared TLR/PRR-to-NF-kappaB/IRF transcriptional module, aside from isolated target-specific singleton responses.

higher_order_basis: Multiple pituitary, Rathke's-pouch, anterior-neural, and endocrine-lineage transcription-factor perturbation panels independently report flat, null, singleton-only, or noncoordinated behavior in P16 postmitotic neuronal groups, with Tbr1 providing an assay-positive contrast.
scope: P16 postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal snRNA-seq groups tested for represented pituitary, Rathke's-pouch, anterior-neural, and endocrine developmental transcription-factor perturbations.
statement: Canonical pituitary, Rathke's-pouch, and anterior-neural developmental transcription-factor networks are not engaged as coordinated postnatal neuronal mRNA modules in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Nsmce2 flatness is supported as a real assay-context result, while the Zfp451/Ranbp2 comparison prevents overgeneralizing that all represented SUMO E3-related perturbations are invisible to the assay.
scope: NeuN-enriched juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of Nsmce2, Zfp451, and Ranbp2 SUMO E3-related targets.
statement: Neuronal transcriptomic consequences of represented SUMO E3 perturbations are scaffold-specific, with Nsmce2 and Zfp451 buffered while Ranbp2 is detectable in the same assay.

higher_order_basis: All three reciprocal receptor-family findings show flat or singleton-only non-convergent neuronal perturbation surfaces, supporting a single family-level absence of a shared basal GPHR transcriptional module.
scope: Sampled postnatal neuronal groups for measured Tshr, Fshr, and Lhcgr loss-of-function perturbations without ligand or antibody stimulation.
statement: Tshr, Fshr, and Lhcgr perturbations do not produce a shared basal glycoprotein-hormone receptor transcriptional module in sampled postnatal neurons.

higher_order_basis: Two target-centered POU comparisons show nonconvergence among measured POU-domain perturbation surfaces in the neuronal assay, with Pou5f1 additionally contrasted against ESC/pluripotency partners.
scope: Measured POU-domain relatives in P16 neuronal perturbation surfaces
statement: Measured POU-domain relatedness is insufficient to produce a shared postnatal neuronal perturbation signature in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Both melanogenesis-related perturbations independently show absence of canonical pigment-cell transcriptional programs in NeuN+ neuronal nuclei, supporting a lineage-context limitation rather than contradicting melanocyte biology.
scope: Mc1r and Lrmda perturbations assayed in NeuN+ neuronal nuclei rather than pigment cells.
statement: Canonical melanogenic and melanosome transcriptional programs are not recovered from Mc1r or Lrmda perturbation in NeuN+ neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: The component directly compares an Adnp-responsive neuronal surface with Pogz flatness, supporting a bounded non-equivalence claim rather than a general ADNP/POGZ mechanism.
scope: P16 mosaic juvenile neuronal assay across the Adnp-responsive groups
statement: Postnatal cell-autonomous Pogz loss does not reproduce the sparse Adnp-dependent neuronal transcriptional response in the measured Adnp-responsive groups.

higher_order_basis: Both findings show lack of transcriptomic convergence among Fyn/PrP/APP/tau/mGluR5-related perturbations in basal juvenile neurons while preserving the limitation that proteopathic, ligand, aged, or peripheral-glial contexts were not assayed.
scope: Normal juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq loss-of-function perturbations of Fyn/Prnp and related amyloid, tau, PrP-synaptic, and myelin-maintenance partners.
