statement: The Fyn-PrP-APP/tau synaptic disease pathway does not manifest as a coherent basal juvenile neuronal loss-of-function transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: The evidence separates mostly flat or weak cadherin/catenin scaffold perturbation surfaces from the transcriptionally visible Ctnnb1 nuclear Wnt-effector boundary in the same assay universe.
scope: Represented neuronal catenin perturbations, including Ctnna3, Ctnna2, Ctnnd2, and Ctnnb1, in the sampled postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Represented cadherin/catenin scaffold perturbations do not produce a broad shared neuronal transcriptomic program, whereas Ctnnb1 is transcriptionally visible in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Independent FAME repeat-host perturbation contrasts consistently show lack of coding-LoF convergence and separate repeat-allele disease grouping from shared host-gene loss transcriptional biology.
scope: Coding CRISPR loss-of-function perturbations of represented FAME repeat-locus host genes in juvenile mouse neurons.
statement: Represented FAME repeat-locus host genes do not share a coding-loss neuronal snRNA-seq module, supporting separation of FAME repeat-allele biology from host-gene loss-of-function transcriptional effects.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly separate detectability of Nfe2l1 perturbation responses from evidence for a Pbx1-to-Nfe2l1 regulatory arm in the same recovered neuronal contexts.
scope: Recovered thalamic and brainstem-like neuronal groups in the P16 CRISPR snRNA-seq assay.
statement: Nfe2l1 loss produces detectable basal transcriptional responses only in narrow neuronal responder groups, without evidence for active Pbx1 regulation of Nfe2l1 in those groups.

higher_order_basis: Both paralog-focused findings indicate that individual Cplx1 or Cplx2 perturbation yields sparse or flat neuronal nuclear transcriptomic effects without a shared downstream complexin module.
scope: Acute Cplx1 and Cplx2 perturbation in the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq readout, excluding untested Cplx3/Cplx4 and release physiology.
statement: Single loss of the measured class-I complexins Cplx1 or Cplx2 is broadly buffered at the basal neuronal nuclear transcriptome level.

higher_order_basis: A direct B9d1 308 CB GABA synaptic/signaling signature is positively recapitulated by Ranbp2, oppositely regulated by Wdr26, and absent from multiple related or unrelated comparator perturbations.
scope: 308 CB GABA neuronal snRNA-seq signatures involving B9d1, Ranbp2, Wdr26, and measured ciliary or unrelated comparator perturbations.
statement: B9d1 perturbation defines a compact, regulatable 308 CB GABA synaptic and neuronal-signaling RNA module that recurs with Ranbp2, is reversed by Wdr26, and is not broadly phenocopied by represented ciliary-gene perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Multiple findings independently report flat or nonconvergent neuronal Perturb-seq responses among represented PFBC, phosphate-homeostasis, and calcification-related perturbations, with caveats for absent targets and non-transcriptional or non-neuronal biology.
scope: Represented PFBC/phosphate-homeostasis/calcification genes in acute juvenile postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal Perturb-seq.
statement: Represented PFBC and phosphate-homeostasis genes do not form a shared acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptional module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The reciprocal histone-comparator findings show lack of convergence among represented single core-histone perturbations in the matched postmitotic neuronal assay, with H4c11 limited to one isolated Ryr2 hit.
scope: Represented H4c11, H2ac8, and H3f3a perturbations in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, with other same-family paralogs not tested.
statement: Represented single core-histone gene perturbations in this postmitotic neuronal assay do not form a shared histone-loss RNA module.

higher_order_basis: The two formin-centered findings show that represented RHO/formin relatives failed to generate convergent downstream FDR transcriptional signatures in matched juvenile neuronal surfaces, without inferring unmeasured paralogs or structural phenotypes.
scope: Represented Diaph2, Fmn1, Fmn2, Cdc42, Rac1, and Rala perturbations in matched juvenile neuronal cell classes.
statement: Represented RHO/formin actin-regulatory perturbations do not form a convergent neuronal snRNA-seq module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: KAT6 catalytic paralog perturbations are flat as single-gene neuronal perturbations, and represented HAT/MYST catalytic comparators fail to account for Brd1 through a shared generic HAT-loss phenotype.
scope: Sparse single-gene perturbations of Kat6a, Kat6b, Brd1, and represented HAT/MYST comparators in postmitotic neuronal nuclei.
statement: Single-gene perturbation of represented KAT6/MYST-HAT catalytic components in postmitotic neurons is transcriptionally buffered or non-convergent rather than producing a generic HAT-loss neuronal RNA program.

higher_order_basis: Multiple juvenile perturbations of known cortical or hippocampal projection-neuron specification regulators failed to alter expected fate-switch or repression programs, while Tbr1 activity shows the assay could detect some cortical TF effects.
scope: Juvenile P16 perturbations assayed by snRNA-seq in broad P37-P44 cortical and related glutamatergic neuronal bins; excludes claims about embryonic deletion, laminar position, axon routing, or purified corticothalamic subtypes.
statement: Juvenile perturbation of represented cortical projection-neuron specification regulators does not detectably reopen or invert canonical embryonic projection-identity transcriptional programs in the assayed postmitotic cortical glutamatergic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Both same-complex partner findings independently report a shared absence of downstream transcriptomic response for represented GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase M6P tag-synthesis components, while noting that biochemical hydrolase-phosphorylation effects were not measured.
scope: Gnptab and Gnptg perturbations across the sampled P16 neuronal groups in this screen.
statement: Perturbing the represented GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase M6P tag-synthesis components Gnptab and Gnptg yields a shared flat neuronal transcriptomic surface rather than a coherent downstream RNA response.

higher_order_basis: The Nrf1 finding establishes the recurrent noncanonical Nrf1-sensitive transcriptomic core, while the Slc25a4 contrast shows this response is not explained by a general inability to detect mitochondrial-regulatory transcription in matched neuronal groups.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal groups including 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
statement: Nrf1 loss produces a recurrent noncanonical neuronal transcriptomic core marked by Cdc7/Kifc2 down-regulation and Pigp/Itfg2 up-regulation, whereas Slc25a4 loss is mostly buffered despite detectability of this mitochondrial-regulatory response.

higher_order_basis: Thra-, Thrb-, Rxrb-, Tbl1x-, and coactivator-related findings separate a small detectable Thra-associated thyroid-axis response from Thrb, RXR, TBL1X/NCoR, and p160 coactivator perturbations.
scope: Represented thyroid receptor/RXR/coactivator/TBL1X-related perturbations in measured postnatal neuronal groups; NCOR/HDAC/GPS2/Ncoa2 components and endocrine tissues remain outside scope.
statement: The detectable thyroid-receptor/RXR-axis transcriptional response in this acute neuronal assay is small and Thra-selective rather than a generic consequence of perturbing Thrb, RXR partners, coactivators, or Tbl1x/NCoR-related components.

higher_order_basis: The supplied evidence supports a bounded Braf-associated transcriptional output and explicitly rejects expansion to generic RAF/MAPK or Ywhae/Raf1 phenocopy; the retained claim keeps the response narrow and mRNA-signature-limited.
scope: Measured Ywhae, Braf, and Raf1 perturbation mRNA signatures in juvenile neuronal groups, especially 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Basal neuronal RAF-pathway transcriptional output in this screen is limited to a small Braf-associated subcortical Vgf-centered response rather than a generic Ywhae/Raf1/MAPK signature.

higher_order_basis: Multiple core glycolysis target contrasts show flat, weak, or nonphenocopying responses among represented central glycolytic perturbations in postmitotic neuronal groups.
scope: Represented glucose-entry and central glycolysis perturbations in NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic assays.
statement: Single perturbations of represented central glycolysis genes are transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Across many independent NDUF/NDUFAF/Timmdc1-centered comparisons, represented nuclear complex-I and broader respiratory-chain perturbations repeatedly show flat, sparse, near-zero-correlated, or non-overlapping nuclear RNA surfaces rather than a recurrent acute OXPHOS-stress module.
scope: Represented nuclear-encoded Complex-I structural subunits, assembly factors, Timmdc1-related targets, and broader respiratory-chain comparators where supplied, in the postnatal neuronal CRISPR/snRNA-seq assay; does not assert preserved protein, editing, respiration, or enzymatic function.
statement: Represented nuclear-encoded Complex-I subunit and assembly-factor perturbations are broadly buffered at the postnatal neuronal nuclear transcriptome level, failing to produce a shared acute OXPHOS-stress transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: Pvalb-focused Maf-family and Mef2c findings show several detectable but small signatures that partition by target rather than forming a shared maturation-factor or Maf-family response.
scope: Juvenile Pvalb GABA neuron snRNA responses to represented Maf-family and Mef2c perturbations.
statement: In juvenile Pvalb neurons, represented Maf-family and Mef2c perturbations produce distinct small transcriptional outputs rather than an interchangeable shared Pvalb maturation or Maf-family program.

higher_order_basis: Multiple glycine receptor, glycine transporter, gephyrin/collybistin, and inhibitory-synapse perturbation contrasts independently show flat, singleton, or non-overlapping RNA surfaces rather than a coordinated glycinergic pathway response.
scope: Represented glycinergic receptor, transporter, and inhibitory-scaffold perturbations in the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay.
statement: Represented glycinergic receptor, glycine-transporter, and inhibitory-scaffold perturbations do not produce a shared glycinergic-synapse mRNA module in this postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay.

higher_order_basis: Ddhd2-centered evidence separates lipid/lipophagy and autophagy perturbations from a common acute neuronal RNA response, while HSP-neighborhood contrasts bound the result to acute nuclear transcriptomics rather than structural or chronic axonal biology.
scope: Matched neuronal DE surfaces for Ddhd2 and represented lipid/lipophagy, autophagy, HSP, and microtubule-related perturbations.
statement: DDHD2 does not sit in a shared acute neuronal RNA response with represented lipid/lipophagy, autophagy, or HSP-pathway perturbations in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal KAT3 paralog comparisons and the Creb1 comparison agree that these single-gene perturbations do not collapse into one shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic state.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal perturbations of Ep300, Crebbp, and Creb1 where measured, including the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut thalamic signature.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of Crebbp, Ep300, and Creb1 do not produce interchangeable shared transcriptomic phenotypes in the matched postnatal neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: Both Myc- and Mycn-centered perturbations independently lack canonical growth and proliferation transcriptional programs in represented postmitotic neuronal groups.
scope: P16 postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq readout; does not exclude protein-only functions or effects in unsampled dividing progenitors, developmental states, or tumor states.
statement: Myc and Mycn perturbations do not recover canonical proliferative growth, ribosome-biogenesis, translation, or cell-cycle transcriptional programs in P16 postmitotic neuronal cell groups.

higher_order_basis: Distinct Dhdds and Elp2 perturbations converge on up-regulation of overlapping amino-acid supply and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase transcripts in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with assay limits noted for ATF4 activity and tRNA charging.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut perturbation responses; transcriptomic inference without direct ATF4 protein activity or tRNA-charging measurements.
statement: Dhdds and Elp2 perturbations induce a shared amino-acid supply and tRNA-charging transcriptional compensation program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: Several findings identify singleton or private downstream events for individual complex-III-related targets and show that those events fail to recur under same-complex perturbations.
scope: Sparse FDR-supported downstream hits among represented complex-III and TTC19 perturbations in matched neuronal groups.
statement: The few FDR-supported neuronal transcriptomic hits observed among represented complex-III-related perturbations are target-private rather than phenocopies of same-complex perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Atxn2-, Matr3-, Tardbp-, and Tia1-centered comparisons repeatedly find divergence, flatness, or only partial overlap among represented ALS-linked RNA-binding and stress-granule perturbations.
scope: Represented ALS-linked RNA-binding, RNA-granule, proteostasis, and splicing perturbations in juvenile mouse neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: ALS-linked or RNA-granule/RBP gene membership does not imply a shared juvenile-neuron loss-of-function transcriptomic module among the represented perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Direct Cltc perturbation findings and multiple matched cross-perturbation contrasts show that core clathrin disruption reaches a neuronal nuclear response threshold, while adaptor-tier, APP-linked, dynamin, synaptojanin, Bin1-like, and several presynaptic/endocytic neighbors remain flat or sparse.
scope: Represented clathrin/endosomal, adaptor-tier, APP-linked, dynamin, synaptojanin, and presynaptic/endocytic perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; vesicle physiology, APP processing, tau spread, and electrophysiology were not directly measured.
statement: Core Cltc perturbation produces a cell-type-restricted neuronal nuclear transcriptional response that is not phenocopied by represented adaptor-tier, APP-linked, Dnm1, Synj1, Bin1-like, or presynaptic/endocytic neighboring perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Across represented CaV pore and auxiliary-subunit perturbations, Cacna1g is the reproducible multi-gene thalamic exception against a background of flat, singleton, divergent, or non-phenocopy calcium-channel relatives.
scope: Represented voltage-gated calcium-channel pore and auxiliary-subunit perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; transcriptomic response only.
statement: Cacna1g loss elicits a selective 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptional response that is not a generic consequence of perturbing represented voltage-gated calcium-channel pore or auxiliary-subunit genes.

higher_order_basis: The component combines one positive Esrra oxidative-metabolism response with repeated reciprocal contrasts showing Ppargc1a, ESRR paralogs, PPAR neighbors, and Nrf1-related perturbations are flat or divergent rather than interchangeable.
scope: Single-gene ERR/PGC/PPAR/NRF mitochondrial-network perturbations in juvenile neuronal nuclei, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; not combined ERR perturbations or acute ligand/cofactor manipulations.
statement: In juvenile neuronal nuclei, single-gene perturbations of the represented ERR/PGC/PPAR/NRF mitochondrial network are transcriptionally node-specific: Esrra loss yields a detectable partial oxidative-metabolism program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Ppargc1a, ESRR paralogs, PPAR neighbors, and Nrf1-related perturbations are flat or divergent rather than phenocopying one another.

higher_order_basis: Multiple target-centered contrasts agree that same-pathway membership does not predict the measured basal neuronal RNA phenotype: Braf and Map2k1 repeatedly expose the thalamic branch, while represented receptor-proximal, RAS, RAF1, MEK2, ERK2, GEF and RasGAP relatives are flat, divergent or sparse.
scope: Represented Ras/MAPK and RASopathy perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the module is sparse and transcriptomic.
statement: The detectable basal neuronal Ras/MAPK RNA output is restricted to a sparse Braf-Map2k1 thalamic branch rather than being shared across represented upstream RAS/GEF, RAF paralog, MEK2, ERK2 or broader RASopathy perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Across sphingolipid synthesis, salvage, S1P, ceramide transfer, ganglioside and lipid-transfer comparisons, the supplied findings repeatedly show flat, singleton or divergent transcriptional surfaces rather than a recurrent multi-gene neuronal module.
scope: Represented sphingolipid-pathway and lipid-transfer perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq; direct unrepresented enzymes and lipid intermediates were not measured.
statement: Represented sphingolipid-pathway and lipid-transfer perturbations do not form a coherent shared multi-gene neuronal transcriptomic module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Positive Braf/Map2k1 convergence provides the detectable benchmark, while receptor, upstream activator, feedback, MAPK-adjacent and unrelated perturbations fail to reproduce the same RNA module under basal postnatal neuronal conditions.
scope: Primarily 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with matched or related neuronal comparator contexts where specified; assay is snRNA-seq and does not measure kinase flux.
statement: In basal 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, the Braf/Map2k1 Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a-centered RNA module is detectable but is not reproduced by Alk, Fgfr2, Fgfr3, Kras, Rapgef2, D630045J12Rik, Pak2 or Spred1 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Together, the findings establish a directionally oriented sterol/cholesterol RNA module: Htt loss induces loci that Srebf2 loss represses, and the Srebf2-like lowered sterol feature set can recur under selected unrelated perturbations.
scope: Sterol-feature signatures involving Htt, Srebf2, Phf12, and Uba5 perturbations in the specified neuronal groups.
statement: The neuronal sterol/cholesterol RNA module is oppositely positioned between Htt loss and Srebf2 loss and is also lowered by Phf12 and Uba5 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: A direct Cry1 perturbation response plus a Cry2 paralog contrast support a Cry1-specific, cell-restricted Per2 de-repression that is not interchangeable with the Cry2 transcriptional phenotype.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut clock-gene perturbation surface in this juvenile mosaic assay.
statement: Cry1 perturbation selectively up-regulates Per2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without producing a Cry2-like thalamic transcriptomic phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Represented SOX perturbations produce small, restricted, and often directionally discordant effects rather than a common neuronal SOX-family program; Tnnt1 is recurrent but sign-divergent across thalamic perturbations.
scope: Measured SOX-family perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; Sox1, Sox3, Sox6, and Sox13 were not perturbation targets.
statement: Measured SOX-family perturbations do not define a generic neuronal SOX transcriptomic response; their limited thalamic effects are target-specific and can invert shared genes such as Tnnt1.

higher_order_basis: Across glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, androgen, progesterone, estrogen receptor, and p160 coactivator perturbations, findings repeatedly show sparse basal effects and near-zero phenocopy while preserving that other nuclear-receptor signatures are detectable.
scope: Basal postnatal neuronal single-gene perturbations of represented steroid receptors, estrogen receptors, p160 coactivators, and selected chaperone/cofactor partners; not acute ligand pharmacology, sex/hormone-state effects, or forced cofactor recruitment.
statement: Basal perturbation of represented steroid and estrogen nuclear receptors and their coactivator or chaperone partners does not reveal a shared unliganded neuronal steroid-receptor transcriptional module, although other nuclear-receptor perturbations can be detected in the assay.

higher_order_basis: ERBB3-specific nonconvergence with canonical PI3K/MAPK effectors is supported by independent PI3K/AKT flatness findings and bounded by evidence that downstream mTOR-axis RNA effects can still be detected.
scope: ERBB3 and represented PI3K-AKT-mTOR/RAS-MAPK perturbation comparisons in postmitotic neurons; acute receptor phosphorylation was not assayed.
statement: ERBB3 perturbation does not produce a stable receptor-to-PI3K/MAPK neuronal RNA program detectable by the supplied postmitotic neuronal perturbation comparisons.

higher_order_basis: The Gpx4, Gstm5, and Acsl4 findings each test expected oxidative, ferroptosis, glutathione/GST, iron, or ISR sentinels in basal postnatal neuronal nuclei and converge on absent downstream induction, with caveats about survival and unmeasured lipid peroxidation.
scope: Unstressed postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of represented ferroptosis, glutathione/GST, oxidative-stress, and iron-related genes; lipid peroxidation, GPX4 activity, survival before nuclei collection, and challenge conditions are not directly assayed.
statement: Basal perturbation of represented ferroptosis and glutathione/oxidative-stress genes does not trigger a detectable neuronal ferroptosis, NRF2/glutathione, iron-handling, or ISR transcriptional program in recovered nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Ctcf and Setdb1 both affect clustered protocadherins with opposite directions, while Smchd1 and Dnmt3a lack detectable Pcdh phenotypes under the same tested conditions.
scope: Clustered protocadherin transcriptional regulation after Ctcf, Setdb1, Smchd1, Dnmt3a, and Ehmt1 perturbations in the supplied P16/postnatal neuronal assay.
statement: Clustered protocadherin transcription in this postnatal neuronal assay is acutely sensitive to Ctcf and Setdb1 perturbation in opposite directions, but not to Smchd1 or Dnmt3a loss under the tested conditions.

higher_order_basis: Direct Srebf2 loss anchors a coherent down-regulated sterol transcriptional module, while multiple lipid-related comparator perturbations show the same module is readable but not generically reproduced.
scope: Basal postmitotic neuronal nuclear RNA groups with Srebf2 sterol-gene responses and matched lipid-related comparator coverage; sterol abundance and biosynthetic flux were not measured.
statement: Srebf2 loss down-regulates a coherent neuronal cholesterol-biosynthesis mRNA module that is not phenocopied by represented Srebf1, Hmgcr, Mttp, Abca7, Ppara, Bscl2, Fbxw7, Med15, or Minar2 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Both findings constrain interpretation of the mouse juvenile gene-level assay by showing it does not directly report the human TDP-43 to STMN2/UNC13A cryptic-splicing axis or simple whole-gene depletion expectations.
scope: Mouse juvenile gene-level snRNA-seq perturbation readout for Tardbp and Stmn2-related disease sentinels.
statement: Tardbp perturbation in this mouse gene-level assay cannot be interpreted as a direct whole-gene reporter of the human TDP-43 to STMN2/UNC13A cryptic-splicing axis.

higher_order_basis: Phka1 and Phkb findings directly test same-holoenzyme perturbations and reject shared RNA output, while calmodulin and calcineurin comparisons bound sparse calmodulin signatures away from PhK-complex phenocopy.
scope: Represented phosphorylase-kinase components Phka1 and Phkb plus Calm1/2/3 comparators in matched juvenile neuronal groups; PHKA2 and PHKG1/2 were not assayed.
statement: The represented phosphorylase-kinase components Phka1 and Phkb do not define a shared neuronal transcriptional module, and sparse calmodulin paralog responses do not phenocopy that complex.

higher_order_basis: The TAM paralog pair Axl/Mertk and adjacent phagocytic/efferocytosis comparators are jointly flat or nonconvergent in matched neuronal groups despite being literature-obvious pathway relatives.
scope: Represented TAM receptor and phagocytic/efferocytosis-related perturbations assayed in matched postnatal NeuN-positive neuronal groups.
statement: The expected Axl/Mertk efferocytosis axis is not detectable as a shared neuronal transcriptional state after single-gene perturbation in this dataset.

higher_order_basis: Two adaptor-associated perturbations fail to engage canonical Wnt reporter output, while direct Lrp6 perturbation demonstrates that this Wnt readout was detectable in the same neuronal context.
scope: P16 NeuN+ neuronal nuclei, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, for represented Wnt-associated perturbations and canonical Wnt reporter genes Axin2 and Lef1.
statement: Atp6ap2 and Amfr perturbations do not drive the canonical Wnt/beta-catenin transcriptional output that is detectable after direct Lrp6 or Ctnnb1 perturbation in thalamic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Kv3 paralog findings report downstream RNA flatness despite measured self-transcript loss, with Vezf1 defining a thalamic context where Kcnc-related transcripts are outputs rather than sufficient drivers.
scope: Represented single Kv3 alpha-subunit perturbations Kcnc1, Kcnc2, and Kcnc3 in the assayed neuronal snRNA-seq screen.
statement: Single represented Kv3 alpha-subunit perturbations are buffered at the downstream neuronal nuclear transcriptomic level in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Across Maf, Mafg, Bach2, Nfe2l1, Nfe2l2, Mafa, and Mafb-centered comparisons, related bZIP/Maf/CNC/Bach perturbations repeatedly fail to phenocopy one another in matched neuronal contexts.
scope: Represented Maf-family, small-Maf/CNC-bZIP, Bach, AP-1, NRF/ARE, and stress-network perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Represented Maf/CNC-Bach/NRF-family perturbations are transcriptionally non-interchangeable in postnatal neurons, producing target- and cell-context-specific signatures rather than a shared generic bZIP/ARE-family loss-of-function RNA module.

higher_order_basis: Across mGluR, Homer, IP3R, PKC, CaMK, PSD scaffold, and synaptic comparator findings, expected postsynaptic pathway neighbors are flat or nonconvergent at RNA level, with isolated exceptions that do not become shared pathway modules.
scope: Basal 3-4-week neuronal snRNA CRISPR readouts for represented mGluR/Homer/IP3R/calcium-plasticity, PKC/CaMK, and PSD scaffold perturbations.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented mGluR/Homer/IP3R calcium-plasticity and PSD scaffold components generally fail to produce a shared steady-state neuronal RNA module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Macf1 is the only retained proposal-specific facet not fully absorbed by the broader receptor or thalamic Wnt-output claims; it has a direct Macf1 finding and independent Wnt comparator findings from distinct targets.
scope: Macf1 and represented Wnt/beta-catenin pathway comparators in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Macf1 perturbation does not activate the detectable Wnt/beta-catenin transcriptional program observed for Ctnnb1, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

higher_order_basis: RyR, IP3R, mGluR-Homer, PMCA2-associated, calmodulin/CaMK, FKBP12, and calcineurin-related perturbations repeatedly show flat, sparse, or nonconvergent steady-state snRNA responses, with acute calcium physiology outside the assay.
scope: Basal postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented calcium-release, calcium-channel, mGluR/IP3R-Homer, CaM/CaMK, FKBP12, and calcineurin pathway genes.
statement: Core calcium-release and postsynaptic calcium-plasticity pathway perturbations are buffered at the basal neuronal steady-state RNA level in this assay.

higher_order_basis: VDR, PXR/CAR, RXR, AHR/ARNT, and related ligand-sensing nuclear-receptor comparisons show near-flat or nonconvergent matched neuronal perturbation surfaces rather than one interchangeable detoxification or VDR/RXR transcriptional module.
scope: Represented VDR/RXR, PXR/CAR, AHR/ARNT, and related ligand-sensing nuclear-receptor perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; ligand activation and multi-receptor redundancy were not tested.
statement: Represented ligand-sensing nuclear receptor and RXR-partner perturbations do not form an interchangeable postnatal neuronal detoxification or VDR-RXR transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: The two findings support absence of a detectable APP-associated convergent mRNA module and limit evidence for inducible APP-family transcriptional compensation, with caveats about untested family members and non-mRNA compensation.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay of App loss and Apbb2-matched APP/FE65L1-associated perturbations; Apbb1, Apbb3, Aplp1, and Aplp2 perturbations were not represented.
statement: APP-family-associated biology is not recovered as an inducible or convergent mRNA signature in this postnatal neuronal perturbation screen.

higher_order_basis: Disease-associated lysosomal, NCL, hydrolase/cargo and trafficking perturbation findings consistently report absent or nonconvergent nuclear mRNA stress signatures rather than a shared acute lysosomal storage-stress program.
scope: Acute juvenile/postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq responses to represented lysosomal, NCL, hydrolase, M6P-trafficking and PSAP-related perturbations; protein, organelle, enzyme-flux and long-term storage phenotypes are outside the assay.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented lysosomal disease-related genes does not elicit a shared neuronal lysosomal-stress, storage-stress, autophagy, TFEB/MiT or ISR/UPR nuclear RNA program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: DNAJ/Hsp40 findings describe sparse, nonconvergent perturbation surfaces across represented family relatives, with Dnajc19 adding limits from mitochondrial-neighborhood comparisons.
scope: Represented DnaJ/Hsp40-family perturbations and checked proximal mitochondrial comparators in the neuronal screen.
statement: Represented DnaJ/Hsp40-family perturbations did not produce a shared neuronal transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: Across receptor, G-protein, adenylyl-cyclase, PDE, PKA/Epac, CREB-axis, dopamine, and NPSR1-adjacent perturbations, the supplied findings repeatedly report flat, sparse, or near-zero-convergent basal RNA surfaces rather than a shared cAMP-pathway transcriptome, with caveats limiting the claim to chronic basal snRNA-seq rather than acute second-messenger signaling.
scope: Represented dopamine, GPCR, G-protein, cAMP/PKA, PDE, Epac, and CREB-adjacent perturbations in basal juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented dopamine/GPCR and cAMP-pathway perturbations do not collapse into one shared durable basal neuronal mRNA module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The three proposals overlap on the same off-axis hematopoietic/cytokine/myeloid perturbation proposition, with the Gfi1b-Zbtb7a contrast retained as a scope boundary rather than a separate claim.
scope: Represented hematopoietic cytokine receptor, MPL-effector, myeloid-lineage, and hematopoietic regulator perturbations in NeuN-enriched juvenile-brain nuclei.
statement: Represented hematopoietic cytokine and myeloid-lineage regulatory perturbations are largely transcriptionally off-axis for recurrent nuclear RNA responses in NeuN-enriched juvenile-brain nuclei, though this quiescence does not extend to all blood-development transcription-factor comparators.

higher_order_basis: One finding establishes a selective positive Opa1 mitochondrial stress program, and the other shows that this program is not a generic consequence of represented mitochondrial gene perturbation because Aco2 lacks it in overlapping contexts.
scope: P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neuronal CRISPR snRNA-seq assay comparing Opa1 and Aco2 perturbation surfaces.
statement: Opa1 loss elicits a cell-class-selective neuronal ISR-like mitochondrial stress transcriptome that is not a general consequence of mitochondrial gene perturbation represented by Aco2.

higher_order_basis: Tpr:F004 anchors Tpr convergence with proteostasis and UFMylation perturbations, and Ufc1:F002 independently supports the UFMylation-linked portion of that shared neuronal transcriptomic state while preserving the transcriptome-only limitation.
scope: neuronal transcriptomic effects of Tpr, proteasome, and UFMylation perturbations in the reported cell groups
statement: Loss of Tpr shares a neuronal transcriptomic state with proteostasis perturbations, including the UFMylation nodes Uba5 and Ufc1.

higher_order_basis: The two findings jointly show that represented GABA metabolic, transport, and receptor perturbations generally produce sparse, target-local, or absent downstream RNA responses rather than a shared robust nuclear program, with Abat's singleton Ppp6r1 effect retained as a target-specific exception.
scope: Represented GABA synthesis, vesicle-loading, reuptake, catabolism, glutaminase, GABA_A, and GABA_B perturbations in assayed GABAergic and Pvalb neuronal groups.
statement: Sparse perturbation of represented GABA metabolic, transport, and receptor genes does not elicit a shared robust nuclear RNA program in the assayed neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Latrophilin, teneurin, FLRT/UNC5, and adjacent adhesion/guidance perturbations repeatedly show flat, singleton, or nonconvergent neuronal RNA responses despite literature-obvious extracellular recognition relationships.
scope: Single-gene neuronal transcriptomic perturbation surfaces for represented FLRT-latrophilin-teneurin/UNC5 and adjacent synaptic adhesion or guidance targets in the postnatal neuronal assay.
statement: Single-gene perturbation of represented FLRT-latrophilin-teneurin/UNC5 synaptic adhesion components does not produce a shared downstream transcriptional module in the assayed postnatal neuronal populations.

higher_order_basis: Both xenosensor nuclear receptor perturbations show absence of coordinated canonical detoxification/efflux gene programs in the neuronal assay, with the inference limited to sampled P16 NeuN+ neuronal transcriptional outputs rather than ligand-exposed liver or barrier contexts.
scope: Nr1i3 and Nr1i2 perturbations in sampled P16 NeuN+ neuronal groups.
statement: Nr1i3 and Nr1i2 loss do not engage coordinated canonical CAR/PXR detoxification and efflux transcriptional programs in sampled P16 NeuN+ neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Atxn10:F007 and Atxn1:F008 are distinct-target Findings that converge on the same negative proposition: shared ataxia naming does not predict a common acute postnatal neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic response among the represented Atxn perturbations.
scope: represented postnatal neuronal Atxn1, Atxn10, and ataxia-name comparator perturbations
statement: Shared spinocerebellar-ataxia gene naming does not define a common acute postnatal neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic module among the represented Atxn perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The Atxn1 and Cic findings converge in the same thalamic neuronal group on selective CIC-associated derepression while limiting the claim against a broad canonical ETV-centered output.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons after Cic or Atxn1 perturbation.
statement: Cic and Atxn1 perturbations in 151 TH neurons reveal selective CIC-associated target derepression rather than a broad canonical ETV-centered transcriptional burst.

higher_order_basis: Ret/Gfra1 flatness is contrasted with measurable Ntrk and downstream signaling perturbations, supporting biological quietness of the GDNF/GFRalpha1/RET input in these states rather than universal failure to detect receptor/kinase effects.
scope: P16-targeted neuronal states represented for Ret/Gfra1, Trk receptors, and proximal kinase/signaling comparators.
statement: The GDNF/GFRalpha1/RET input is transcriptionally quiet in the measured P16 neuronal states despite detectable sparse responses from other receptor-tyrosine-kinase or proximal signaling perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Gata1 and Klf1 are distinct canonical blood-lineage regulators, and both perturbations lack their expected downstream erythroid readouts in the neuronal assay, supporting a lineage-context boundary rather than a shared neuronal module.
scope: Assayed NeuN+ postnatal neuronal transcriptomes across listed cortical, thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and cerebellar groups; several blood regulators were not perturbation targets, and the claim does not test erythropoiesis in blood-lineage cells.
statement: Canonical Gata1- and Klf1-linked erythroid transcriptional programs are absent from the assayed postnatal neuronal transcriptomes.

higher_order_basis: Direct perturbations of IFNAR receptor components, ISGF3-associated factors, and an IFN transcriptional brake all fail to alter canonical ISG transcripts in unstimulated NeuN-enriched neurons, while comparator findings treat isolated non-ISG hits as nonconvergent boundaries.
scope: Basal postnatal NeuN-enriched neuronal perturbation assay without exogenous interferon or infection challenge.
statement: Basal postnatal NeuN-enriched neurons lack a detectable tonic type-I-interferon/IFNAR-ISGF3-driven ISG transcriptional program in this perturbation assay.

higher_order_basis: A Gabrb2-centered thalamic activity-gene induction is directly observed and bounded by same-family, rho, alpha, delta, and chloride-importer perturbations that are flat, weaker, or non-phenocopying.
scope: Represented GABA_A receptor, Gabrr2, and Slc12a2 perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Gabrb2 loss selectively induces an activity-associated nuclear RNA response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas represented Gabra3, Gabra2, Gabrd, Gabrr2, and Slc12a2 perturbations do not reproduce that multi-gene response.

higher_order_basis: Epm2a and Gaa perturbations both failed to produce expected glycogen-storage or stress-response RNA programs, and indirect glycogen-energy comparators did not substitute as convergent phenocopies.
scope: Postnatal sparse neuronal snRNA-seq readouts for Epm2a, Gaa, and assayed indirect glycogen-energy comparators; biochemical glycogen storage and direct Lafora same-complex perturbations were not tested.
statement: Acute neuronal perturbation of assayed glycogen-storage disease genes does not propagate into a detectable glycogen-quality-control, lysosomal, autophagy, or UPR/ISR transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: The two findings support one atomic non-phenocopy proposition: Atxn1 has a strong acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomic requirement, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, that is not reproduced by Zhx3 despite external interaction evidence.
scope: Atxn1- and Zhx3-matched neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; transcriptomic perturbation evidence only, not a test of stoichiometric complex formation.
statement: The acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomic requirement detected for Atxn1 is not shared by Zhx3, despite reported ATXN1-ZHX3 interaction evidence.

higher_order_basis: Setdb1 provides a positive chromatin perturbation control, while Lrif1 and Zfp961-nominated comparator pathways are flat or nonconvergent, bounding both chromatin-target and PPAR/RXR interpretations.
scope: Basal neuronal perturbation comparisons involving Lrif1, Setdb1, Zfp961, and nominated PPAR/RXR or chromatin-related comparators.
statement: The mostly flat Lrif1 and Zfp961 comparator surfaces are pathway-specific nonconvergence rather than a generic inability of the assay to detect chromatin-linked neuronal transcriptional effects.

higher_order_basis: Same-complex CD3/TCR, Cd4/MHC, and Cd79a/Cd79b BCR-related perturbations are flat, sparse, or nonconvergent in NeuN-positive neuronal nuclei rather than forming latent immune-receptor RNA programs.
scope: Represented CD3/TCR, Cd4/MHC, and BCR/immunoreceptor perturbations in NeuN-positive neuronal cell groups.
statement: Represented lymphocyte immunoreceptor components do not form a latent shared TCR/CD3/BCR-like transcriptional module in the assayed NeuN-positive neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Multiple target-centered Mediator comparisons define a reproducible 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut down-regulated module shared by Med13, Med15, and Med23, with Med13l and Cdk8 serving as non-phenocopying boundaries.
scope: Directly measured Mediator perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with limited 059 and 005 contexts only where stated; many Mediator subunits were not represented.
statement: Med13, Med15, and Med23 perturbations converge on a shared down-regulated 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal module, whereas Med13l contributes only a narrow Grm1 overlap and Cdk8 does not phenocopy the module.

higher_order_basis: Across mitochondrial pyruvate-entry, PDC, DLD-linked, TCA, Fe-S, and malate-aspartate comparator perturbations, most nuclear RNA responses are absent, sparse, singleton-only, or non-phenocopy, with bounded target-specific exceptions.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq CRISPR readouts for represented mitochondrial carbon-entry, PDC, DLD-linked, TCA, Fe-S, and adjacent metabolic targets.
statement: Represented mitochondrial carbon-entry, PDC, TCA, and Fe-S perturbations generally fail to induce a coherent postmitotic neuronal nuclear DE module in this assay, although isolated singleton effects and target-specific signatures remain exceptions.

higher_order_basis: CASPR/paranodal/juxtaparanodal and Kv1-complex comparisons reject transcriptomic phenocopy among structurally or electrophysiologically related axonal adhesion and channel genes, while preserving assay limits on protein clustering and physiology.
scope: Represented CASPR/paranodal/juxtaparanodal adhesion, Kv1 alpha-subunit, and Kvbeta perturbations in basal postnatal neuronal nuclear mRNA.
statement: Kv1-channel and CASPR/paranodal structural relationships do not translate into a shared basal neuronal nuclear mRNA response in this perturbation screen.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Braf and Map2k1 convergence, with Ntrk2 and Shoc2 partial overlap, establishes a sparse same-cell down-regulated thalamic RNA module centered on Vgf with Ptpn5 and Unc13a support.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal transcriptomic perturbation responses; Shoc2 overlap is Vgf-only at FDR level and the readout is RNA rather than phospho-ERK.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Braf and Map2k1 perturbations define a sparse down-regulated Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a-centered RNA module that is partially shared by Ntrk2 and Shoc2 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Independent perturbation-centered contrasts across represented GAG linker, HS biosynthesis/modification, HSPG-core, sulfation-related, and guidance-adjacent targets consistently report flat, sparse, near-orthogonal, or cell-group-specific responses instead of a common acute neuronal DEG signature.
scope: Represented GAG/heparan-sulfate/proteoglycan pathway perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; biochemical GAG chain abundance, sulfation, and matrix structure were not assayed.
statement: Single-node perturbations of represented GAG/heparan-sulfate/proteoglycan pathway genes do not collapse into a common acute postnatal neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The direct Vcp phenotype and the Elf2 pathway-uncoupling result jointly support a restricted Vcp-associated neuronal mRNA response that is not explained by the predicted BAP31-ELF2-VCP axis.
scope: Elf2, Bcap31, and Vcp perturbations in juvenile NeuN+ neuronal nuclei assayed 3-4 weeks after P16 CRISPR; VCP activity, BAP31 protein, proteostasis flux, and non-neuronal promoter binding are outside scope.
statement: In juvenile NeuN+ neuronal nuclei, Vcp-associated transcriptional effects are sparse and cell-type-restricted rather than a dominant output of the literature-predicted BAP31-ELF2-VCP mRNA axis.

higher_order_basis: PSD scaffold, Homer-complex, SHANK/DLG/DLGAP, neuroligin/neurexin, and adhesion-near findings repeatedly show flat or nonconvergent steady-state RNA surfaces rather than a signed shared PSD DEG program.
scope: P16/postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq responses to represented postsynaptic scaffold, Homer-complex, PSD, glutamate receptor-associated, and synaptic adhesion perturbations; protein localization, spines, and receptor currents were not measured.
statement: Represented postsynaptic scaffold and synaptic adhesion gene perturbations generally do not induce a shared steady-state neuronal RNA module in this P16 screen.

higher_order_basis: Carrier-centered findings and enzyme-centered reciprocal contrasts jointly show that Slc25a12 and Slc25a13 depletion do not elicit the stress or synaptic RNA program seen after Mdh1/Got1 perturbation.
scope: Mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier perturbations compared with MAS enzyme perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Slc25a12 and Slc25a13 perturbations are transcriptionally buffered from the Mdh1/Got1-linked amino-acid stress and synaptic remodeling program in the assayed neurons.

higher_order_basis: Sequential or adjacent alpha-dystroglycan/matriglycan-pathway perturbations were measurable but showed near-zero correlations, flat surfaces, or isolated gene/cell-context events instead of shared mRNA convergence.
scope: Represented matriglycan and DAG1-glycosylation perturbations in the postnatal neuronal assay, with DGC comparator context where directly tested.
statement: Sequential alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation pathway perturbations do not yield a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The Bap1, Mbd5, and Asxl3 contrasts independently report non-phenocopy among represented PR-DUB-related genes, despite some members producing detectable neuronal responses.
scope: Represented PR-DUB-related perturbations in matched juvenile neuronal groups, excluding unmeasured PR-DUB components.
statement: Acute neuronal transcriptomic outputs of represented PR-DUB-related genes are not determined simply by shared PR-DUB biochemical membership.

higher_order_basis: Gsk3b is isolated as the only detectable transcriptional responder in an otherwise buffered AKAP/PKA/Reelin-associated biochemical neighborhood, with its response restricted to one thalamic glutamatergic class.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut in the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation assay.
statement: Gsk3b loss produces a small, cell-restricted basal transcriptomic response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut that is not a shared Reln- or AKAP11/PKA-cassette mRNA signature.

higher_order_basis: Hoxa13 and Hoxd13-centered comparisons separate a narrow Hoxa13 pineal response from expected posterior-Hox or Hox/TALE-family convergence, with broader HOX findings bounding the interpretation to represented targets.
scope: Matched postnatal brain groups containing the 217 P MY Pineal Glut Hox13 comparisons and represented Hox/TALE comparator perturbations.
statement: The focal Hoxa13 217 P MY Pineal Glut Acp6/Slc49a4 signature is not a generic Hox13 or Hox/TALE-family transcriptional response in the represented perturbation set.

higher_order_basis: Multiple independent target-centered contrasts show that represented developmental bHLH, proneural, E-protein, REST-axis, PTF1, and MYC/AP4-adjacent perturbations are mostly flat or nonconvergent in mature postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq, with a narrow Tcf4 Pvalb exception.
scope: P16/postnatal mature neuronal nuclei across represented bHLH, E-protein, proneural, PTF1, REST-axis, and adjacent transcription-factor perturbations; narrow Pvalb Tcf4 exception preserved.
statement: Represented developmental bHLH and class-I E-protein perturbations largely fail to form a shared acute transcriptional module in mature postnatal neuronal nuclei, apart from a narrow Tcf4 Pvalb response.

higher_order_basis: Two adenylyl-cyclase findings directly establish shared downstream flatness among represented membrane ADCY paralogs, while beta-adrenergic and PDE10A comparisons define the proximal cAMP and compartmentalized-response boundaries.
scope: Represented membrane adenylyl-cyclase paralogs and proximal beta-adrenergic/cAMP perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Single loss of represented membrane adenylyl-cyclase paralogs is buffered at the basal neuronal nuclear-RNA readout, producing no shared downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: Across mitochondrial protease, OPA1-processing, fission, TIM22/lipid, and proteostasis comparisons, same-organelle perturbations are sparse, divergent, or branch-specific rather than convergent.
scope: Represented mitochondrial protease, proteostasis, OPA1-processing, fission, TIM22-associated, and lipid-related perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Same-organelle mitochondrial perturbations in this neuronal assay are transcriptionally branch-specific rather than interchangeable, with Lonp1-associated stress output not broadly shared by ClpXP, AAA protease, Opa1-processing, or Agk-related perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The two reciprocal TBL-family comparisons establish paralog-specific rather than interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic effects, with the Mecp2-neighborhood comparison bounding the result within broader incomplete MeCP2/NCoR-adjacent phenocopy.
scope: Measured Tbl1x and Tbl1xr1 single-gene perturbations in P16 sparse neuronal assay contexts; Tbl1x/Tbl1xr1 double perturbation was not tested.
statement: Tbl1x and Tbl1xr1 single-gene perturbations are not interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic phenocopies in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Two photoreceptor-lineage transcriptional regulators independently lack their expected retina or pineal target-gene programs in the supplied neuronal assay universe, supporting a lineage-context limitation rather than a silent positive program.
scope: Measured neuronal cell groups lacking a retinal photoreceptor class, with pineal output assessed through the supplied Crx finding.
statement: The postnatal neuronal screen lacks the lineage context needed to recover canonical CRX/NR2E3 photoreceptor transcriptional programs.

higher_order_basis: Ogt and Tnpo3 independently connect neuronal perturbation phenotypes to RNA-processing-linked nuclear logistics, while Tnpo3 limits the interpretation away from generic nuclear transport and Rnpc3 supports the RNA-splicing side of the state.
scope: represented Ogt, Tnpo3, spliceosome/RNA-processing, and nuclear-transport perturbations in postnatal neuronal transcriptomic assays
statement: Postnatal neuronal Ogt and Tnpo3 perturbation phenotypes align with a spliceosome/RNA-processing-linked nuclear logistics state rather than with generic nuclear transport disruption.

higher_order_basis: Across represented P4-family ATPase perturbations, the supplied findings show nonconvergence or isolated effects rather than a common downstream neuronal transcriptomic state.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbation surfaces for represented P4-family targets Atp8a2, Atp9a, and Atp11c, with Vps35 only as an Atp9a pathway comparator.
statement: Loss of represented neuronal P4-family ATPases is not sufficient to trigger a shared downstream snRNA-seq stress program.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal AFF-family perturbation contrasts support the same atomic proposition that Aff2 and Aff3 are not interchangeable at the measured postnatal neuronal mRNA phenotype level.
scope: Represented AFF-family perturbations in the postnatal neuronal assay; Aff1, Aff4, and most SEC subunits were not represented.
statement: Aff2 and Aff3 do not share a detectable postnatal neuronal mRNA perturbation phenotype in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Direct Neurog3 marker absence and failure of represented proneural/endocrine comparators to phenocopy Neurog3 indicate that classical Neurog3-related specification biology is not re-engaged in this mature neuronal perturbation context.
scope: Neurog3 and represented proneural bHLH, E-protein, and endocrine-fate comparators in P16 mature neuronal perturbation data.
statement: The classical Neurog3 endocrine/proneural specification program is not transcriptionally re-engaged by acute perturbation of represented Neurog3/Neurod1-related targets in mature neurons.

higher_order_basis: Setdb1-centered, Pcdh-detectability, KRAB-ZFP, and adjacent chromatin perturbation findings show that the Setdb1-sensitive protocadherin/Atf7ip/Tasor response is detectable but not a generic output of nearby repressive chromatin perturbations.
scope: Setdb1-sensitive protocadherin/HUSH/KRAB-adjacent transcriptional responses in postnatal neuronal groups; excludes unrepresented EHMT2, TRIM28, TASOR, ATF7IP perturbations and repeat quantification.
statement: The Setdb1-sensitive protocadherin/Atf7ip/Tasor neuronal response is detectable but is not reproduced by assayed KRAB-ZFPs, Smchd1, Dnmt3a, Dcaf8-related chromatin perturbations, or Champ1-associated heterochromatin relatives.

higher_order_basis: Both Adcy1 and Crhr1 perturbations independently lack the expected cAMP/CREB-associated immediate-early transcriptional program under a basal, non-stimulus-locked snRNA-seq endpoint.
scope: Basal non-stimulus-locked 3-4-week loss-of-function snRNA-seq measurements for Crhr1 and Adcy1.
statement: Basal Crhr1 and Adcy1 loss-of-function do not recreate ligand- or activity-evoked cAMP/CREB immediate-early transcriptional programs.

higher_order_basis: Kat6a and Kat6b single-gene neuronal perturbation findings converge on flatness, while two therapeutic-warning findings independently state that this sparse postmitotic single-paralog assay lacks the biology required to infer dual KAT6A/B inhibitor pharmacology or safety.
scope: Sparse postnatal neuronal CRISPR/snRNA-seq perturbations of Kat6a and Kat6b, excluding dual catalytic inhibition, drug exposure, pharmacodynamics, non-neuronal toxicity, and proliferative compartments.
statement: Single-paralog Kat6a or Kat6b loss in assayed postmitotic neurons is transcriptionally flat or buffered and cannot be used as a surrogate for dual KAT6A/B catalytic-inhibitor pharmacology or safety.

higher_order_basis: The Dpm1 response converges with an upstream dolichol-backbone perturbation but not with represented distal glycosylation branch perturbations.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut dolichol/glycosylation perturbations; Dpm2 and Dpm3 were not available as perturbation targets.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, the Dpm1 Pdia6/Ttyh3 response tracks the dolichol/Dol-P-Man carrier axis more closely than distal O-mannosylation or GPI-anchor branch perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The Prepl-Cltc contrast establishes detectability of bulk clathrin-traffic transcriptional stress, while AP-adaptor contrasts show nearby adaptor perturbations do not converge on that response.
scope: PREPL, represented AP-adaptor, and clathrin-related loss-of-function perturbations in juvenile CNS neurons.
statement: Prepl and represented AP-adaptor perturbations are not transcriptionally equivalent to bulk clathrin-coated vesicle failure in the assayed juvenile neurons.

higher_order_basis: Across ER-Golgi transport, COPI, COG, SNARE, and Golgi/CDG perturbations, represented pathway neighbors are repeatedly flat, singleton-only, or non-overlapping rather than forming a shared organelle-level response.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq assay for represented ER-Golgi, secretory-pathway, COPI/COG/SNARE, and Golgi/CDG perturbations.
statement: Represented ER-Golgi trafficking and Golgi glycosylation-homeostasis perturbations do not produce a shared broad secretory-pathway transcriptional module in postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Two singleton target events are bounded by comparator findings showing pathway relatives do not reproduce them, making them target-specific RNA events rather than shared Rac/Cdc42/PAK-pathway outputs.
scope: Pak3, Rac1, and related Rac/Cdc42/PAK-pathway perturbations in 308 CB GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, and matched neuronal comparator surfaces.
statement: Pak3-associated Ccm2 induction and Rac1-associated Ranbp1 induction are perturbation-specific singleton transcriptomic events rather than shared Rac/Cdc42/PAK-pathway outputs.

higher_order_basis: The COPII/ER-exit findings independently report flat downstream responses among represented Tfg, Sec23a, and Sar1b perturbations, while contrasting this branch with Sec63 ER-stress positivity.
scope: Represented COPII initiation and ER-exit perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Perturbing individual represented COPII initiation or ER-exit nodes Tfg, Sec23a, and Sar1b is transcriptionally buffered in this neuronal assay, unlike the ER-stress response elicited by Sec63.

higher_order_basis: Both findings independently separate systemic or enterocyte lipid-export disease mechanisms from detectable acute neuron-intrinsic lipoprotein/chylomicron transcriptional programs in the assayed neuronal screen.
scope: P16-specified neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation contexts represented for Mttp and Sar1b; enterocytes, serum lipids, chronic dietary lipid or vitamin deficiency, and non-neuronal systemic consequences were not assayed.
statement: Mttp and Sar1b perturbations do not engage an acute neuron-intrinsic ApoB/chylomicron lipid-export transcriptional program in the assayed postnatal neurons.

higher_order_basis: Multiple Pax-family perturbation comparisons converge on nonconvergence or sparse/null transcriptional surfaces in postmitotic neuronal nuclei.
scope: Represented Pax-family perturbations in the assayed postmitotic neuronal transcriptomes.
statement: Represented Pax-family transcription factors are not transcriptionally interchangeable perturbation nodes in this postnatal neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: All findings contrast HUWE1 with represented HECT/E3 ligases and related neurodevelopmental comparators, consistently identifying HUWE1 as transcriptionally visible while others are flat, sparse, or nonconvergent.
scope: Represented HECT/E3-ligase perturbations and related neurodevelopmental comparators in matched postnatal neuronal CRISPR/snRNA-seq groups.
statement: HUWE1 perturbation produces a target-specific neuronal transcriptomic response that is not a generic HECT/E3-ligase or UBE3A-like phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Family-wide comparisons across represented ZBTB/BTB-ZF perturbations separate broad, focal, flat, and orthogonal neuronal response classes, with limited partial convergence that does not generalize across the family.
scope: Represented ZBTB/BTB-ZF perturbations in juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Shared BTB-ZF/ZBTB family membership is insufficient to predict a common postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Ligand, receptor, STAT paralog, IFN receptor, and curated downstream pathway readouts repeatedly show null, singleton, or near-zero convergent responses, while Rora provides an internal detectable transcription-factor contrast separate from cytokine receptor phenocopy.
scope: Homeostatic postnatal neuronal perturbation surfaces for represented IL-12/IL-23, IFN, IL-6, gamma-c, and STAT/JAK-associated pathway components.
statement: Represented cytokine receptor and STAT perturbations, including IL-12/IL-23, interferon, gamma-c, and class-I cytokine receptor axes, do not expose an active shared basal neuronal cytokine-JAK-STAT transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: Flrt3 has a weak Dapk1/Odc1-centered RNA phenotype that is not shared by represented latrophilin, teneurin, UNC5, LRRTM, or guidance comparators.
scope: Flrt3-matched neuronal groups and represented FLRT3-adjacent adhesion/guidance comparator perturbations.
statement: The Flrt3 Dapk1/Odc1 RNA response is not a shared transcriptomic output of the represented FLRT-latrophilin-teneurin-UNC5 adhesion complex.

higher_order_basis: Got2-specific findings show expected severe-deficiency stress programs absent, while comparator findings demonstrate the same assay could detect ISR-like outputs after Mdh1/Got1 perturbation.
scope: Got2 perturbation across measured neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Postnatal neuronal Got2 perturbation does not elicit the amino-acid/ISR, redox, p53, or MAS-compensation RNA programs expected from severe GOT2-deficiency models, despite ISR-like outputs being detectable after cytosolic MAS perturbations in the same assay.

higher_order_basis: Both findings indicate that acute sparse perturbation of represented mitochondrial metabolic nodes yields near-null or isolated idiosyncratic responses rather than a coherent shared mitochondrial stress transcriptome in P16 neurons.
scope: P16 sparse neuronal perturbations of represented SUCL, TCA, OXPHOS, and mtDNA-linked comparator genes.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented single mitochondrial metabolic nodes in P16 neurons does not elicit a coherent shared ATF4, UPRmt, OXPHOS, mitophagy, or mtDNA-depletion-like transcriptomic stress program.

higher_order_basis: Both Vsx-family findings test canonical retina or embryonic lineage programs in the supplied postnatal brain-neuron perturbation surface and find absence of those programs, supporting a context-limited negative proposition rather than rejection of the canonical mechanisms in their native tissues.
scope: Measured P16 postmitotic brain-neuron nuclei, excluding retina, optic cup, spinal cord, and hindbrain contexts.
statement: Vsx1 and Vsx2 perturbations do not detectably engage their canonical retinal or embryonic lineage transcriptional programs in the sampled P16 brain-neuron Perturb-seq surface.

higher_order_basis: The Mnx1 and Lhx3 findings independently show absence of canonical motor-neuron transcriptional and guidance-program engagement in postnatal brain neurons, with caveats placing the expected biology in embryonic spinal contexts outside the sampled regime.
scope: Lhx3 and Mnx1 perturbations and represented motor-neuron program comparators in sampled P16 brain neurons; embryonic spinal motor neurons and the full spinal motor-neuron regulatory network were not assayed.
statement: The sampled juvenile brain neurons do not engage the canonical embryonic spinal motor-neuron identity program after Lhx3 or Mnx1 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: The component supports one atomic proposition: Grin1 loss induces a defined upregulated adaptive stress/growth-associated transcriptional state in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the Wdfy3 contrast establishes directional specificity rather than generic thalamic perturbation behavior.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut perturbation signatures involving Grin1 and Wdfy3; transcriptomic stress/growth hypothesis only, not proof of a full integrated-stress-response cascade.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Grin1 loss induces a growth/plasticity and stress-linked transcriptional state that is directionally opposed to the Wdfy3 thalamic state.

higher_order_basis: Cross-paralog and related-comparator contrasts distinguish Atp1a3 as the represented Na,K-ATPase alpha subunit with a strong thalamic neuronal transcriptional response, while Atp1a1, Atp1a2, and Nkain2 are flat or divergent.
scope: Neuron-enriched perturbation screen of represented Na,K-ATPase alpha subunits and Nkain2, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Na,K-ATPase-related perturbations are isoform-specific in neuronal nuclei, with Atp1a3 producing a distinct thalamic transcriptional response not reproduced by Atp1a1, Atp1a2, or Nkain2.

higher_order_basis: Neurofilament subunit comparisons consistently show flat or near-self-only transcriptomic effects, with related Aimp1, Gfap, and Plec findings defining interaction, lineage, and cytolinker boundaries.
scope: Acute postnatal neuronal CRISPR snRNA-seq perturbations of represented neurofilament subunits and related GFAP/AIMP1/cytolinker contexts; not axonal protein stoichiometry, phosphorylation, or astrocyte biology.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented neurofilament subunits does not elicit a robust shared neuronal nuclear RNA program or compensatory neurofilament-family mRNA response.

higher_order_basis: Mecp2- and Tbl1x-centered pathway-uncoupling findings show that MeCP2/NCoR/TBL/MBD-adjacent perturbations produce detectable but non-interchangeable neuronal RNA phenotypes, with receptor-family selectivity marking a boundary rather than a shared complex-level output.
scope: Measured neuronal perturbations of Mecp2, Tbl1x/Tbl1xr1, MBD-family, Sin3a, and nuclear-receptor-related comparators; NCOR1/2, HDAC3, and GPS2 were not represented.
statement: MeCP2/NCoR-adjacent perturbations do not form an interchangeable neuronal RNA phenotype in the P16 sparse neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Kdm4b- and Kdm4c-centered Findings support the same single-gene paralog result while preserving the caveat that untested Kdm4a/Kdm4d and double-loss settings are outside scope.
scope: Single-gene Kdm4b and Kdm4c perturbations in measured postmitotic neuronal cell groups
statement: Single-gene perturbation of Kdm4b or Kdm4c does not produce a detectable shared acute neuronal transcriptional module in the measured postmitotic neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: The supplied findings support a paralog contrast in which Gigyf2, but not Gigyf1, can elicit sparse neuronal transcriptional responses, while also showing those responses are too small and heterogeneous to define a broader shared pathway.
scope: Gigyf1 and Gigyf2 perturbations across the assayed neuronal groups, especially thalamic, midbrain-glutamatergic, hypothalamic, and Pvalb contexts.
statement: Gigyf2 perturbation produces sparse neuronal transcriptional responses not observed after Gigyf1 perturbation, but these responses do not define a coherent GIGYF-family core pathway.

higher_order_basis: Rab7 and Vps41 provide direct positive evidence for a late-endosomal/lysosomal compensation module, while Ocrl, Abca7, and Gdi1 show the response is not a generic consequence of perturbing adjacent endolysosomal or Rab-related genes in the same neuronal assay.
scope: Neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces containing Rab7-responsive thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, GABAergic, and pineal groups.
statement: Rab7 loss induces a selective neuronal late-endosomal/lysosomal compensation program that is weakly shared by Vps41 but absent after Ocrl, Abca7, or Gdi1 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Tuba1a and Atxn10 findings define a tubulin/cytoskeletal RNA axis, while Nefh, Plec, Dst, Macf1, and Aimp1 findings show it is not a generic response to neurofilament or cytolinker perturbation.
scope: Tubulin-paralog and cytoskeletal transcriptional responses among Tuba1a, Atxn10, Nefh, and cytolinker comparator perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: A distinct neuronal tubulin-paralog transcriptional state is engaged by Tuba1a and Atxn10 perturbation contexts but is not a generic response to neurofilament, plakin, or cytolinker perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Chemokine receptor comparisons reject a generic chemokine-GPCR neuronal program, and Rac1 provides a distinct sparse Sst boundary rather than pathway convergence.
scope: Represented chemokine receptor, neuroimmune receptor, and indirect Rac-arm perturbations in postmitotic NeuN-positive neuronal snRNA-seq readouts.
statement: Represented chemokine receptor and Rac-arm perturbations do not produce a common postmitotic neuronal transcriptional program, with Cxcr4 and Rac1 limited to isolated non-convergent single-gene events.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal SPRED findings provide direct evidence for silent single SPRED-family perturbations, while broader Ras/MAPK comparisons place that silence within a mostly buffered negative-regulator surface without claiming double-loss behavior.
scope: Single acute Spred1 and Spred2 perturbations in resting postmitotic neurons; double SPRED perturbations and Ras-GTP or phospho-ERK biochemistry were not measured.
statement: Single perturbation of Spred1 or Spred2 is buffered at the neuronal transcriptome level, with both SPRED paralog losses lacking downstream FDR-significant RNA responses in matched postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal same-direction cross-perturbation between cytosolic malate-aspartate shuttle partners supports a shared, cell-context-bounded transcriptional response while preserving restricted overlap limitations.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut acute snRNA perturbation signatures for Mdh1 and Got1.
statement: Mdh1 and Got1 perturbations converge on a shared cytosolic malate-aspartate shuttle-associated transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: Multiple stress-MAPK-adjacent perturbation findings report absent or nonconvergent downstream RNA effects, bounding canonical stress-MAPK/JNK/MARK/Hippo/TLR signaling as transcriptionally silent or non-shared under this juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq condition.
scope: Represented stress-MAPK, JNK, MARK, Hippo, and TLR nodes across matched juvenile neuronal groups; phosphorylation, acute receptor/injury stimulation, and unrepresented closest paralogs are not assayed.
statement: Basal loss of represented stress-activated MAPK-adjacent signaling nodes does not produce a shared neuronal transcriptomic module in this juvenile snRNA-seq screen.

higher_order_basis: IL-2 receptor components, gamma-chain family receptors, STAT/Treg-axis comparators, and Foxp3 all lack expected immune/Treg transcriptional responses in NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei, with isolated Il4ra behavior treated as target-specific rather than a shared cytokine module.
scope: Basal juvenile NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei assayed for represented IL-2 receptor, gamma-chain cytokine receptor, STAT5/Treg-axis, and Foxp3 perturbations.
statement: Represented IL-2 receptor/gamma-chain/STAT5/Treg-axis perturbations do not produce a detectable canonical IL-2/Treg transcriptional program in juvenile NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Marchf6 and Srebf2 contrasts establish a directional inverse sterol-gene module, with Agps and Txndc15 findings placing narrower perturbation responses within the same module in restricted neuronal contexts.
scope: Sterol/cholesterol transcription features involving Marchf6, Srebf2, Agps, and Txndc15 in represented neuronal groups including 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut.
statement: Marchf6 and Srebf2 perturbations define opposing directions of a neuronal sterol-gene RNA module, with Marchf6 loss inducing and Srebf2 loss repressing shared cholesterol-biosynthesis features.

higher_order_basis: Klf9 and Klf13 findings jointly show absence of the expected cAMP/axon-growth gene program in resting postmitotic neurons while identifying a distinct restricted Klf9 thalamic response.
scope: Klf9 and Klf13 perturbations in resting P16 postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Klf9 and Klf13 loss in resting postmitotic neurons do not derepress the canonical cAMP/axon-growth gene program.

higher_order_basis: One finding establishes Bdp1-associated synthetase induction, while the other shows that Polr3b perturbation does not share this mRNA stress response in the same neuronal assay context.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut mRNA stress readouts after represented Pol III-related perturbations.
statement: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase induction is a Bdp1-associated neuronal mRNA response that is not a general consequence of Polr3b perturbation in this assay.

higher_order_basis: SPPL2a, BRI2/ITM2B, and APP-processing findings show that expected protein-processing relationships do not become shared transcriptional modules in sparse young neurons.
scope: Represented SPPL2 proteolysis, BRI2/ITM2B, and APP-processing perturbations in young neuronal snRNA-seq; SPPL2b was not a perturbation target.
statement: Represented neuronal proteolysis and APP-processing relationships are uncoupled from a shared acute nuclear transcriptional response in this assay.

higher_order_basis: ENG- and ACVRL1-centered findings specifically test the vascular BMP9/10-like receptor neighborhood, while Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr3 bound that subset within broader receptor-SMAD nonconvergence in postmitotic neurons.
scope: Sampled postmitotic neurons in the same perturb-seq assay; excludes endothelial, ligand-stimulated, and flow-stimulated vascular receptor contexts.
statement: The represented ENG-ACVRL1 vascular receptor-SMAD circuit is transcriptionally uncoupled in the sampled postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Several mitochondrial or mitochondrial-adjacent targets fail to induce the Opa1-like stress program in matched neuronal contexts despite positive Opa1 detectability, separating mitochondrial stress-responsive perturbations from broad target-class membership.
scope: Ndufb8, Timmdc1, Slc52a2, and Yme1l1 perturbations compared with Opa1-responsive neuronal groups; endpoint and power caveats preserved.
statement: The Opa1-like mitochondrial ATF4/amino-acid stress program is not a generic consequence of perturbing represented mitochondrial or mitochondrial-adjacent targets in this neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: The Ppp2r5d finding defines a sparse, cell-type-restricted neuronal response, and the Ppm1g comparator finding argues against a shared Ppm1g-Ppp2r5d transcriptional phenocopy in this neuronal assay.
scope: Ppp2r5d and Ppm1g neuronal perturbation signatures in the supplied PP2A/phosphatase-related neighborhood.
statement: Ppp2r5d-associated neuronal transcriptional effects are sparse and cell-type-restricted and do not constitute a shared Ppm1g-Ppp2r5d mRNA phenocopy in this dataset.

higher_order_basis: Rho-regulator and myosin-adjacent findings show nonconvergence and flat or singleton responses, with caveats limiting inference to nuclear RNA rather than protein/localization phenotypes.
scope: Represented Rho/Rac/Cdc42-axis, Rho-regulator, and cytoskeletal/myosin perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented Rho-family cytoskeletal and myosin-adjacent perturbations do not collapse into a shared postnatal neuronal mRNA program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Receptor-side, adaptor/regulatory, kinase, and nuclear NF-kappaB perturbation findings consistently show flat or sparse downstream RNA surfaces rather than a coherent basal TNFR/TLR/IL-1-to-TAK1/IKK/NF-kappaB/JNK/p38 module.
scope: Unchallenged postnatal NeuN-positive neuronal perturbation readouts for represented CD40/TNFR/TLR/IL-1, TRAF3, MAP3K7/TAK1, CHUK/IKK, NF-kappaB, JNK, and p38-related nodes.
statement: Represented TNFR/TLR/IL-1/CD40-to-TAK1/IKK/NF-kappaB/JNK/p38 perturbations are broadly transcriptionally silent as a basal module in unchallenged postnatal NeuN-positive neurons.

higher_order_basis: Two distinct perturbations linked to hippocampal or plasticity biology fail to produce durable basal mRNA responses in the pooled 012 group, while the findings explicitly leave evoked activity, morphology, electrophysiology, and finer hippocampal subtypes untested.
scope: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut group after sparse postnatal Rel or Adgrb1 loss in the basal neuronal transcriptomic assay.
statement: Rel and Adgrb1 loss do not produce detectable constitutive transcriptional plasticity programs in the hippocampal-containing 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut group in this basal postnatal neuronal assay.

higher_order_basis: Across independent IFT, dynein-2, BBSome, transition-zone, Cep290, Alms1, ciliary-GPCR, and Hedgehog-adjacent perturbation findings, related ciliary targets repeatedly show absent, singleton-only, or orthogonal nuclear RNA effects in postnatal neurons, while proteasome perturbations demonstrate that broad RNA responses can be detected in the same assay universe.
scope: Represented ciliary transport, BBSome, transition-zone, ciliary-GPCR, and Hedgehog-adjacent perturbations assayed by basal postnatal NeuN+ neuronal snRNA/nuclear RNA; ciliary morphology, protein localization, cargo trafficking, and evoked signaling were not measured.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented ciliary trafficking and ciliary signaling genes in postnatal NeuN+ neurons is largely buffered at the basal nuclear RNA level rather than producing a coherent shared ciliary transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly identify absence of induced transcriptomic repair signaling for the represented Slf2/Nsmce2/Atr axis while showing that broader chromosome-maintenance perturbations can be detected in the same neuronal assay.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbations of represented SMC5/6-localization, checkpoint, and broader SMC/chromosome-maintenance relatives; most direct SLF2 recruiters and core SMC5/6 components were not perturbation targets.
statement: The represented Slf2/Nsmce2/Atr replication-fork-associated axis is transcriptionally uncoupled in postmitotic neurons despite detectable responses from broader chromosome-maintenance relatives such as Smc1a.

higher_order_basis: The reciprocal Dtnbp1 and Ap3b1 findings support a shared absence of detectable acute downstream neuronal transcriptional responses among the represented AP-3/BLOC-related or adjacent genes, while caveats limit untested complex members and protein-sorting phenotypes.
scope: Dtnbp1, Ap3b1, and Slc32a1 in matched juvenile neuronal groups; most BLOC-1 subunits, Ap3b2, and protein cargo-sorting phenotypes were not tested.
statement: Represented AP-3/BLOC-related or adjacent perturbations share a buffered juvenile neuronal transcriptomic outcome without a detectable acute nuclear compensation program.

higher_order_basis: Akap9, Prkar1a, and Akap11 comparisons show broad buffering across represented AKAP and PKA-related perturbations, with Gsk3b defining a restricted nonconvergent exception.
scope: Represented AKAP-family, cAMP/PKA-pathway, and Gsk3b perturbations in postnatal neuronal nuclei.
statement: Single-gene disruption of represented AKAP localizers and PKA core nodes is generally buffered at the basal neuronal nuclear RNA level, with Gsk3b forming a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut-specific exception rather than a shared AKAP/PKA module.

higher_order_basis: Both reciprocal ANTXR paralog findings converge on broad neuronal buffering, with no robust family-level ECM transcriptome in sampled neuronal nuclei.
scope: Antxr1 and Antxr2 perturbations in sampled neuronal nuclei.
statement: ANTXR-family perturbation does not produce a robust postmitotic neuronal ECM transcriptional program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal IL-17 receptor-family and inflammatory-pathway contrasts show that sparse Il17ra and Il17rd neuronal responses are not reproduced by represented IL-17, MAPK/NF-kB, TLR, TNF, or adjacent FGF-family perturbations.
scope: Represented IL-17 receptor-family, MAPK/NF-kB/Traf, TLR, TNF, and adjacent FGFR-family perturbations in matched neuronal groups.
statement: Sparse Il17ra and Il17rd neuronal RNA responses are not reducible to shared IL-17 receptor-family, MAPK/NF-kB, TLR, TNF, or FGFR-family transcriptional modules in this dataset.
