higher_order_basis: The findings identify overlapping positive-neighbor relationships among U2af2, Matr3, Ascc3, spliceosome factors, Tpr, and proteostasis-associated targets, supporting a shared but not necessarily direct stress signature in neuronal transcriptomes.
scope: Restricted transcriptomic signature convergence among U2af2, Matr3, Ascc3, RNA-processing, nuclear-transport, and proteostasis perturbations in the supplied neuronal groups.
statement: U2af2, Matr3, and Ascc3 perturbations converge with RNA-processing and nuclear-transport perturbations on a neuronal stress signature that also includes proteostasis-related responses.

higher_order_basis: The findings from Gigyf2 and Tnrc6a jointly support factor-specific transcriptomic liabilities among represented neuronal mRNA decay and translation-control perturbations rather than a shared generic module.
scope: Represented neuronal mRNA decay/translation-control perturbations in matched groups for Gigyf2 and Tnrc6a.
statement: Adjacent neuronal mRNA-control factors produce factor-specific transcriptomic liabilities rather than a shared generic decay/translation-loss RNA module.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Ddx39b and Thoc1 findings define the strongest same-direction TREX/export-sensitive response in 191 MB P MY GABA, with Prpf6 and Rnpc3 providing broader RNA-processing context without erasing the cell-context restriction.
scope: primarily 191 MB P MY GABA, with broader spliceosome/RNA-processing context from midbrain/thalamic responder groups
statement: Ddx39b and Thoc1 perturbations share a TREX/splicing/nuclear-export-sensitive same-direction transcriptomic state that is strongest in 191 MB P MY GABA and only partly shared by broader spliceosome perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Unc13a- and Unc13c-centered comparisons establish weak or absent Munc13 paralog convergence, while the Unc13b-centered pathway contrast shows this buffering is not a universal property of all represented synaptic priming machinery.
scope: Represented active-zone and synaptic priming perturbations involving Unc13a, Unc13b, Unc13c, and Stxbp1 in the neuronal snRNA-seq assay; some Munc13 groups had missing cell groups or low perturbed-cell counts, and several canonical synaptic comparators were not represented.
statement: Single Munc13 paralog perturbations are transcriptionally buffered and non-interchangeable in this neuronal snRNA-seq assay.

higher_order_basis: Cacna2d2 pan-null data and alpha2delta/CaV related-target contrasts show represented alpha2delta perturbations are largely buffered at the neuronal nuclear RNA level despite detectable Cacna1g effects in the same screen.
scope: Cacna2d1/Cacna2d2 and represented CaV auxiliary-subunit perturbations in the P16 sparse CRISPR neuronal snRNA-seq assay; DNA indels and protein abundance were not measured.
statement: Postnatal sparse loss of represented CaV alpha2delta auxiliary subunits does not induce a detectable cell-autonomous neuronal nuclear RNA program, despite detectable transcriptional effects from Cacna1g in the same screen.

higher_order_basis: One proposal covers ER-chaperone/UPR-like recoverability and non-equivalence among nearby ER-associated components; the supplied findings support this as an atomic ER-stress specificity claim distinct from the broader proteasome machinery claim.
scope: Represented ER stress, BiP/UPR-axis, BiP-cofactor, and ER-associated perturbations in matched neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: ER-chaperone/UPR-like transcription is recoverable after selected perturbations such as Sec63, Hspa5, and Manf, but it is not a generic consequence of perturbing any ER-associated or UPR-axis component.

higher_order_basis: The proposal is already a single canonical biological proposition supported by two circadian-factor perturbations in the same thalamic neuronal context, with assay limitations preserved because both findings measure neuronal nuclear RNA rather than extracellular matrix deposition or secreted protein function.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut after Nr1d1 or Bmal1 perturbation; transcriptomic evidence only, not direct measurement of secretion or matrix deposition.
statement: Loss of Nr1d1 or Bmal1 can drive a shared Pdgfa/Col4a1/Col4a2-positive extracellular-remodeling transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: Mga and Mycn findings provide target-specific sparse signatures, while Myc and Mnt comparisons show these are not shared MYC/MAX/E2F network outputs.
scope: Mga responding groups, Mycn 053 Sst Gaba response, and represented MYC/MAX/E2F comparators.
statement: The sparse Mga and Mycn neuronal signatures are target-specific responses rather than generic consequences of perturbing represented MYC/MAX-network or E2F-related genes.

higher_order_basis: Independent flat or near-flat non-Elongator tRNA-modifier findings support a basal-mRNA buffered branch, while broader tRNA-modifier contrasts prevent overgeneralizing to all tRNA-modification enzymes.
scope: Basal, non-challenged P16 neuronal nuclei assayed for represented non-Elongator tRNA-modification targets, especially Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented non-Elongator tRNA-modification enzymes such as Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1 are largely buffered or flat at the basal neuronal mRNA level in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly separate Klhl7/Klhl20 effects from a generic KLHL-family, autophagy, or Rho-related transcriptional response in the same matched neuronal responder groups.
scope: Klhl7, Klhl20, and measured autophagy/Rho/BTB comparator perturbations in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA.
statement: Klhl7 and Klhl20 perturbations do not define a shared KLHL-family, autophagy, or Rho-related neuronal transcriptional response in the matched responder groups.

higher_order_basis: Ogdh has a defined Prdx5/Borcs7 response that is not reproduced by represented OGDH-complex, PDC, or TCA-neighbor perturbations against a background of mostly sparse comparator responses.
scope: Ogdh-matched mitochondrial enzyme comparator surfaces, especially OGDH-complex, PDC, and TCA-neighbor perturbations.
statement: The Ogdh Prdx5/Borcs7 neuronal response is not a generic OGDH-complex, PDC, or TCA-cycle transcriptional phenotype in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a convergent-module findings establish a recurrent same-direction 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut BAF/mSWI/SNF response, with Arid2 partial involvement and repeated flat, weak, or divergent same-family contrasts defining subunit selectivity and gene-content boundaries.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal transcriptomic responses to represented mSWI/SNF/BAF/PBAF-related perturbations
statement: A subunit-selective BAF/mSWI/SNF transcriptional module operates in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, converging most clearly through Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a with partial Arid2 and weak Smarcd1 involvement on recurrent neuronal signaling or synaptic-scaffold genes, while several represented family members such as Smarca4, Smarca2, Smarcc1, Bicra, Arid1b, and Brwd1 are flat, weak, or divergent rather than interchangeable phenocopies.

higher_order_basis: Multiple GABA_A subunit perturbations and an expected upstream Zkscan1 perturbation fail to trigger alpha/beta/gamma/delta receptor-subunit replacement at the nuclear mRNA level, while protein trafficking or receptor assembly remain unmeasured.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq for Gabra1, Gabra2, Gabrb3, and Zkscan1 perturbations across measured GABA_A receptor subunit transcripts.
statement: Single postnatal perturbations of represented GABA_A receptor subunits do not induce a robust compensatory mRNA replacement program among other measured GABA_A receptor subunits.

higher_order_basis: NuRD/MBD-centered comparisons independently reject transcriptomic phenocopy among CHD4, GATAD2B, MBD2, PHF6, CASZ1, and ZMYND8, while retaining caveats about incomplete NuRD-subunit coverage and transcriptomic rather than biochemical readout.
scope: Represented NuRD-associated, MBD-family, PHF6, CASZ1, and ZMYND8 perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; many canonical NuRD subunits and biochemical complex activities were not directly tested.
statement: Represented NuRD/MBD-adjacent chromatin perturbations do not collapse into a single shared neuronal loss-of-function mRNA signature.

higher_order_basis: The Atp1a3 finding identifies reduced calcium-handling pump mRNAs without same-complex compensation, while cross-paralog findings show Atp1a1 and Atp1a2 do not reproduce the Atp1a3 thalamic transcriptional state.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal nuclei in the represented Na,K-ATPase alpha-subunit perturbation screen.
statement: In thalamic neurons, Atp1a3 loss is transcriptionally coupled to reduced calcium-handling pump mRNAs rather than induction of Na,K-ATPase paralog or accessory-subunit compensation.

higher_order_basis: Both findings reject convergence from represented class-C GPCR, Gi/o, and related signaling perturbations onto the sparse Casr or Gpr156 transcriptomic surfaces.
scope: Represented neuronal groups for Casr and Gpr156 comparator perturbations, especially 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut for Gpr156; several proximal pathway members were not represented.
statement: Sparse Casr and Gpr156 transcriptomic hits are not explained by a shared represented class-C GPCR, GABA(B)/mGluR, Gi/o, or proximal second-messenger perturbation module in juvenile neurons.

higher_order_basis: Atrn lacks the expected acute endolysosomal/autophagy stress output, while Rab7 demonstrates that lysosomal/V-ATPase compensatory transcription can be detected in related assayed neuronal regions.
scope: Measured acute transcriptomic responses in Atrn, Rab7, and V-ATPase-related perturbation contexts; exact Mgrn1 and Tsg101 perturbations were unavailable.
statement: Atrn loss does not trigger a detectable acute endolysosomal/autophagy stress mRNA program in the assayed neurons, even though Rab7 perturbation reveals detectable lysosomal/V-ATPase compensation in related regions.

higher_order_basis: Multiple alpha, beta, beta1-partner, laminin-receptor, and focal-adhesion comparator findings repeatedly show null or isolated non-overlapping effects rather than a shared neuronal adhesion transcriptional state.
scope: Represented integrin, beta1/laminin-receptor, and focal-adhesion-related perturbations in basal postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq; several close alpha, beta3-complex, ligand, and adhesion comparators were untested.
statement: Represented integrin and laminin-receptor perturbations do not produce a shared basal postmitotic neuronal adhesion or beta1/focal-adhesion transcriptional module, aside from isolated target-specific single-gene effects.

higher_order_basis: Independent bHLH-PAS contrasts show the same assay detects CLOCK/BMAL1 circadian output while ARNT/AHR/HIF/NPAS3/AHRR-related perturbations and Bmal2 are flat or nonconvergent.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal perturbation groups containing represented bHLH-PAS, circadian, ARNT-dependent, BMAL-paralog, and RORE-related comparators.
statement: In the assayed postnatal neurons, bHLH-PAS perturbations separate into a detectable CLOCK/BMAL1 circadian-output response and a largely flat or nonconvergent ARNT/AHR/HIF/NPAS3/AHRR/BMAL2-related response.

higher_order_basis: Both findings reject convergence among represented NK-homeobox-related perturbations in sampled neuronal groups, while noting that the observed signatures are near-null or isolated one-gene effects.
scope: Represented NK-homeobox-related and comparator perturbations in Pvalb, CA1/DG, and CA3/CA2-FC/DG neuronal groups.
statement: Represented NK-homeobox-related perturbations do not define a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptional program in the sampled groups.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Kv4 module comparisons support a shared absence of detectable downstream transcriptional output for Dpp6 and Kcnd3, while distinguishing that absence from a positive DE module.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal groups with Dpp6 and Kcnd3 represented; electrophysiological effects and untested Kv4 components are outside scope.
statement: Perturbing the represented Kv4 A-current components Dpp6 and Kcnd3 does not elicit a detectable downstream neuronal mRNA program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Two distinct perturbation targets share the same singleton FDR-level Cdc27 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, while both findings limit the evidence against inferring a broader APC/C transcriptional program.
scope: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut after Unc13b or Slc25a46 perturbation in this assay.
statement: Cdc27 up-regulation is a recurrent singleton biomarker response to Unc13b and Slc25a46 perturbation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut without evidence for a broader APC/C transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: The findings independently test nonapeptide receptor and downstream signaling comparators from Oxtr, Avpr1a, and Avpr1b target perspectives and consistently find disjoint or flat FDR-supported transcriptional outputs rather than a shared receptor-family or Gq/PLC/PKC module.
scope: Represented perturbation targets and matched cell groups in the basal juvenile neuronal snRNA CRISPR assay; conclusions are restricted to assayed targets, FDR-supported transcriptomic phenotypes, and sparse receptor-family surfaces.
statement: Oxtr, Avpr1a, and Avpr1b perturbations do not converge on a shared vasopressin/oxytocin-receptor or Gq/PLC/PKC transcriptional module in the assayed neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Findings across represented Kv1, Kv3, Kvbeta, Kv2/Kv4/Kcnq, and channel-complex genes repeatedly report null, near-null, or sparse non-overlapping mRNA consequences rather than a robust shared channel-loss transcriptional program.
scope: Represented voltage-gated potassium-channel and associated Kv-complex perturbations in postnatal neuronal nuclear mRNA at 3-4 weeks.
statement: Represented voltage-gated potassium-channel and Kv-complex perturbations do not produce a robust shared downstream neuronal nuclear mRNA program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The retained claim consolidates both proposals' shared biological proposition: multiple unrelated perturbations show sparse singleton up-regulated downstream transcripts in the same 009 glutamatergic population, but the downstream genes differ and do not establish a shared pathway.
scope: Singleton downstream RNA responses to Il6st, Lrp8, Zfhx2, and Cpe perturbation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
statement: The 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut population is a recurrent site of sparse, perturbation-specific singleton up-regulation events without evidence for a shared downstream pathway or broad transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: The two proposals overlap on a single supported proposition: PD-linked annotation does not predict a shared acute neuronal loss-of-function RNA program, because some endomembrane or proteostasis perturbations are visible while several disease-family targets remain flat or nonconvergent.
scope: Represented juvenile neuronal CRISPR loss-of-function surfaces for Eif4g1, Park7, Snca, Vps35, Atp13a2, and related Parkinson, trafficking, and stress comparators; not aged dopaminergic vulnerability or human missense biology.
statement: Parkinson-family gene membership does not imply a shared acute neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic program in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Bmal1 and Nr1d1 findings provide direct cross-target support for a shared thalamic downstream state, while Cry1 and Nr1d2 contrasts bound it as selected-node convergence rather than generic circadian-family phenocopy.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut single-endpoint transcriptomic responses; direct binding, co-occupancy, and direct versus secondary effects were not established.
statement: Bmal1 and Nr1d1 perturbations converge on a shared 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut downstream transcriptional state despite opposite positions in the core circadian feedback loop, while retaining target-specific clock-output inversions.

higher_order_basis: Across purinergic, chemokine, TAM, CSF1R-axis, and myeloid-lineage comparator panels, immune-lineage receptor perturbations repeatedly show flat or isolated neuronal DE surfaces rather than recurrent NeuN-positive nuclear RNA programs.
scope: Postnatal NeuN-positive neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of represented microglia-lineage, neuroimmune, TAM, chemokine, purinergic, and phagocytic targets; microglia themselves and several ligands were not sampled.
statement: Represented microglial and neuroimmune receptor perturbations do not produce recurrent cell-autonomous neuronal nuclear transcriptional programs in this NeuN-positive screen.

higher_order_basis: Findings involving receptor-proximal, G-protein, enzyme, purine-adjacent, and nuclear CREB-axis nodes distinguish known biochemical signaling routes from the chronic basal nuclear-RNA phenotypes measured weeks after perturbation.
scope: Basal snRNA-seq readouts 3-4 weeks after sparse postnatal perturbation of represented second-messenger pathway genes.
statement: Acute biochemical linkage to cAMP or CREB signaling is insufficient to predict a chronic basal neuronal CREB/immediate-early mRNA response in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Ntrk2-specific downstream findings and receptor-family contrasts separate a small TrkB response from Ntrk1, Ntrk3, Ngfr/Sort1, and GDNF/RET surfaces.
scope: Neurotrophin receptor and comparator receptor-tyrosine-kinase perturbations in Pvalb Gaba, thalamic glutamatergic, and related measured neuronal groups.
statement: Ntrk2 loss produces a small cell-context-specific transcriptional response, including Akap5 repression in Pvalb GABA neurons, that is not phenocopied by Ntrk1, Ntrk3, Ngfr, Sort1, or Ret/Gfra1 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Multiple perturbation-centered contrasts across Atl/Reep/Spast, long-axon transport, and clinical axonopathy neighborhoods show flat, sparse, or non-overlapping nuclear RNA responses, with caveats that acute somatic snRNA-seq may miss structural and chronic axonal phenotypes.
scope: P16 sparse juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented ER-shaping, HSP, long-axon transport, and related axonopathy genes; structural ER topology, peripheral/lower motor neurons, chronic axonal phenotypes, and physiology were not directly measured.
statement: Represented ER-shaping, HSP, and long-axon transport perturbations do not form a shared acute neuronal nuclear transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Tuba1a provides the direct tubulin-compensation finding, while Map6 and Tuba4a comparisons distinguish it from generic microtubule-neighborhood injury or alpha-tubulin paralog responses.
scope: Postnatal neuronal tubulin and microtubule-neighborhood perturbations represented in the component.
statement: Postnatal Tuba1a loss is read out as tubulin-isotype dosage compensation rather than as a shared microtubule-neighborhood injury or embryonic tubulinopathy-like transcriptional program.

higher_order_basis: The three supplied CCK ligand/receptor findings consistently show absence of downstream transcriptional output after single-gene perturbation of represented CCK-axis members in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
scope: Postnatal sparse neuronal single-gene perturbations of represented CCK ligand, receptor, and proximal Gq-pathway genes.
statement: Single-gene perturbation of represented CCK ligand-receptor axis members is transcriptionally silent at the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq endpoint.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly support that iron-axis perturbations in this neuronal snRNA-seq assay yield absent or punctate transcriptional responses rather than a broad canonical iron-stress response, with Tfrc providing the direct perturbation-effect anchor and Hjv defining cross-perturbation scope.
scope: P16 mosaic neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations involving Tfrc and Hjv, with weak Tfrc/Ireb2 comparator context supplied by Hjv:F004.
statement: Iron-axis perturbations in this neuronal assay produce absent or highly punctate transcriptional responses rather than a broad canonical neuronal iron-starvation or iron-stress program.

higher_order_basis: Across MEF2 paralog, Hdac5 corepressor-neighbor, and Foxj3 regulatory-neighbor perturbations, the robust neuronal transcriptomic response is repeatedly Mef2c-centered rather than a shared MEF2-family or Foxj3-linked program.
scope: Postnatal cortical IT, Pvalb, and thalamic neuronal groups assayed by snRNA-seq perturbation; comparisons use separate guide pools rather than within-cell combinatorial perturbations, and direct binding is not assayed.
statement: Mef2c has a postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response that is not phenocopied by Mef2a, Mef2d, Hdac5, or Foxj3 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Two immune co-signaling perturbation contexts show that represented checkpoint or costimulatory genes do not recover their expected immune programs or detectable matched neuronal DE programs in NeuN-selected nuclei.
scope: Matched NeuN-selected neuronal groups represented for Icos, Cd80, Cd40, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9 perturbations; direct CD80 receptor/paralog and ICOS ligand relationships were not fully tested.
statement: Immune costimulation genes represented by Icos, Cd80, Cd40, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9 lack detectable cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional programs in the sampled NeuN-selected perturbation system.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly distinguish Adarb1's sparse Flnb-dominated response from Adar while placing the Adarb1 signature near non-ADAR regulatory perturbations in the same assay.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal groups represented for Adar and Adarb1 perturbations.
statement: Adarb1 loss elicits a sparse Flnb-dominated transcriptomic state that is not shared by Adar but is approached by non-ADAR perturbations including Tpr, Ogt, Uba5, and Psmb4.

higher_order_basis: Tbx2, Tbx3, Tbx4, and Tbx19 comparisons jointly show weak or absent convergence among represented non-Tbr1 T-box and receptor relatives, while Tbr1 serves as an internal positive contrast for assay visibility of a postmitotic cortical T-box transcriptional program.
scope: Represented T-box subfamily, BMP, and FGF receptor perturbations in juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq groups.
statement: Most represented non-Tbr1 T-box perturbations fail to produce interchangeable neuronal RNA signatures in the juvenile postmitotic screen, despite detectable Tbr1-dependent cortical transcriptional output.

higher_order_basis: A direct Ppm1g cell-type-selective response plus an Xpo7 cargo comparison support a narrow Ppm1g thalamic transcriptional surface that is separable from Xpo7-loss biology.
scope: Ppm1g and Xpo7-cargo-related perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal transcriptomic groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Ppm1g perturbation exposes a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut transcriptional response that is not a cargo-knockdown phenocopy of Xpo7 loss.

higher_order_basis: Cross-comparisons among represented mitochondrial protease and proteostasis genes repeatedly reject same-organelle or same-protease interchangeability in the neuronal RNA readout.
scope: Represented mitochondrial matrix, ClpXP, and inner-membrane protease-related perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented mitochondrial protease perturbations are transcriptomically non-interchangeable in postmitotic neurons, with LONP1, ClpXP, and inner-membrane protease branches separating rather than forming a shared protease-loss module.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Ctnnb1- and Lrp6-centered findings define a selective thalamic Wnt/catenin branch, while receptor-centered findings bound the claim against broad receptor-family interchangeability.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and related postnatal thalamic glutamatergic Wnt/catenin perturbation comparisons.
statement: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the detectable Wnt/catenin transcriptomic state links Lrp6 with Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 rather than broadly extending to Lrp5, Gsk3b, single Frizzled receptors, ROR/RYK receptors, Lgr4, or other catenin-related perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Both Smad6 and Nipa1 findings test expected BMP/SMAD transcriptional outputs and report no ID/SMAD target-gene activation in neuronal snRNA-seq.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal transcript abundance after Smad6 or Nipa1 perturbation; phospho-SMAD protein activity and BMPRII trafficking were not directly assayed.
statement: Smad6 and Nipa1 loss do not activate the expected canonical BMP/SMAD transcriptional target-gene program in assayed postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal comparator findings show that literature-related HERC-family or HERC2-associated ligase perturbations did not produce interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic endpoints in the measured responder groups.
scope: Matched neuronal responder groups and endpoint genes represented for Herc1, Herc2, and Ube3a.
statement: Herc1 and Herc2 perturbations do not behave as interchangeable large-HERC-family neuronal transcriptomic perturbations in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Gbeta5/R7, GPR158/GPR179, inhibitory GPCR, GIRK, class-C GPCR, and cAMP-adjacent perturbations yield flat, sparse, or receptor-specific outputs rather than a common neuronal phenocopy.
scope: Measured single-gene perturbations of Gbeta5/R7-adjacent GPCR/RGS/GIRK, GPR158/GPR179, mGluR, and cAMP-related signaling nodes in postnatal neuronal transcriptomic assays.
statement: Represented Gbeta5/R7-adjacent GPCR/RGS/GIRK pathway perturbations are largely uncoupled from a common downstream neuronal transcriptomic program in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Polr3b findings establish a sparse, cell-selective neuronal mRNA response with a defined thalamic module, while Bdp1 and Taf1b comparators constrain interpretation by showing RNA-production and Pol III components are not interchangeable in this protein-coding mRNA readout.
scope: Postnatal neuronal protein-coding mRNA responses to Polr3b and nearby RNA-production machinery perturbations; direct Pol III small-RNA outputs were not measured.
statement: Polr3b loss produces a sparse, cell-selective neuronal homeostatic mRNA module rather than a broad Pol III or transcription-production shutdown signature.

higher_order_basis: FGF ligand, receptor, receptor-like, downstream RAS/ERK-neighbor, and HS-chain-adjacent comparisons repeatedly yield flat, sparse, or mutually distinct postmitotic neuronal RNA effects rather than shared FGF-axis convergence.
scope: Represented FGF/FGFR/RAS/ERK-axis and HS-chain-adjacent perturbations in postnatal neuronal mRNA readouts.
statement: Represented FGF/FGFR/RAS/ERK-axis perturbations are transcriptionally buffered or sparse and do not form a shared postmitotic neuronal RNA module.

higher_order_basis: Represented imprinted, paternally expressed, PWS-region, and PWS/AS-neighboring coding-gene perturbations repeatedly show flat, sparse, or target-specific postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic effects rather than convergent downstream modules.
scope: Represented acute coding-gene perturbations from imprinted, paternally expressed, PWS-region, and PWS/AS-neighboring loci in juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq; major PWS noncoding genes were not tested.
statement: Acute perturbation of individual represented imprinted or PWS-related coding genes does not produce a shared postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: Independent Figla, Nobox, and Sohlh1-centered findings all show absent canonical ovarian/germline regulon engagement and lack of mutual phenocopying in sampled neurons.
scope: Postnatal sampled neuronal lineages with represented early ovarian and germline-network perturbation targets.
statement: The represented FIGLA-NOBOX-SOHLH-associated early ovarian and germline transcriptional network is not active as a shared perturbation module in postnatal neurons.

higher_order_basis: Three represented Williams-region perturbation contrasts independently show nonconvergent matched neuronal DE surfaces, separating same-locus disease-gene membership from acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic interchangeability.
scope: Represented Williams-Beuren critical-region perturbations in matched acute postmitotic neuronal assay contexts; Gtf2ird2 and several WBSCR genes were not perturbation targets.
statement: Acute loss of individual represented Williams-Beuren critical-region genes yields noninterchangeable neuronal transcriptional responses rather than a shared same-locus disease-gene module.

higher_order_basis: Both perturbations independently test durable nuclear ERK/MAPK-output mRNA programs in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq surfaces and find FDR-level absence, without excluding transient ERK phosphorylation.
scope: Postnatal neuronal Fgfrl1 and Lztr1 perturbation surfaces assayed by snRNA-seq.
statement: Postnatal neuronal Fgfrl1 and Lztr1 perturbations do not induce a durable canonical FGF/ERK transcriptional response.

higher_order_basis: Both perturbations target steroidogenic or endocrine-associated biology, yet both lack the expected downstream transcriptional programs in the basal postnatal neuronal assay.
scope: Basal P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neuronal mosaic screen, with caveats for rare SF-1 VMH cells and acute ligand-stimulated LHCGR responses.
statement: Basal postnatal neuronal loss of Lhcgr or Nr5a1 does not recover expected steroidogenic or endocrine transcriptional programs in the measured neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Both findings describe muted postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic responses for represented centrosomal or ciliary targets, with mostly zero or singleton downstream differential-expression outputs and assay caveats excluding direct structural ciliary readouts.
scope: Represented centrosomal and ciliary perturbations in postmitotic neurons
statement: Represented centrosomal and ciliary perturbations are largely transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic neurons, yielding no common nuclear RNA response in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple AP-adaptor-family perturbation contrasts show focal marker responses that do not transfer across represented AP-related targets.
scope: Represented AP-adaptor-family and clathrin-adjacent neuronal perturbations in matched basal postnatal snRNA-seq contexts.
statement: Focal responses to represented AP-adaptor perturbations are target-specific rather than a generic AP-family or clathrin-adjacent vesicle-trafficking transcriptional signature.

higher_order_basis: Across Notch1, Notch2, and Notch4 target-local contrasts, sparse perturbation of represented receptors, ligand, proteolysis components, and Fbxw7 fails to generate shared directional neuronal transcriptomic responses.
scope: Measured postmitotic neuronal groups in this assay, especially Notch1/Notch2/Notch4 matched contexts.
statement: Sparse perturbation of measured Notch receptors and core processing relatives does not produce a shared postmitotic neuronal Notch transcriptional module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The findings establish a detected Tcf7l2-associated thalamic excitability and synaptic/neuropeptide program and define Tbl1x as uncoupled from the overlapping beta-catenin/TCF7L2 transcriptional response.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nuclei, with related 145 MH-LH TH Glut evidence for Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 overlap.
statement: Tcf7l2 loss disrupts a postmitotic thalamic excitability and synaptic/neuropeptide transcriptional state that is shared with beta-catenin perturbation but not reproduced by Tbl1x perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Tsc2 provides a positive mTORC1/SREBP/lysosome-like neuronal module, while Pkd1 and Fam120a pathway-uncoupling findings bound their nulls as specific non-engagement rather than readout failure, and Srebf2 limits the module to sterol-centered rather than broad lipogenic output.
scope: mTORC1/SREBP/lysosome-related perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups, especially caudal and 155 MB Glut contexts.
statement: Tsc2 loss, but not Pkd1 or Fam120a loss, engages a detectable neuronal mTORC1/SREBP-linked sterol and lysosomal transcriptional program that is not broadly lipogenic.

higher_order_basis: The Alx1-centered and Alx3-centered reciprocal paralog contrasts jointly support the same atomic negative proposition that the matched postnatal neuronal assay does not recover an interchangeable ALX-family transcriptomic module.
scope: Alx1, Alx3, and Alx4 perturbations in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA neuronal groups
statement: Alx1, Alx3, and Alx4 do not form an interchangeable postnatal neuronal ALX-family transcriptomic module in the matched neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Multiple represented skeletal-muscle AChR structural subunits and NMJ-associated targets were directly contrasted in matched postnatal neuronal groups, and the findings consistently report flat, sparse, orthogonal, or nonconvergent RNA effects rather than a shared muscle-channel/endplate pathway signature.
scope: Represented muscle AChR/NMJ pathway perturbations, including Chrnb1, Chrnd, Chrne, Chrng, Ache, Lrp4, and Musk, in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq groups.
statement: Single perturbations of represented muscle AChR/NMJ pathway genes do not recover a shared muscle-channel or NMJ transcriptional module in postnatal brain neurons.

higher_order_basis: Sparse Epha10, Epha5, and Ephb1 findings define private cell/gene responses, with Epha4 and Epha2 bounding them against generic Eph receptor or proximal signaling explanations.
scope: Sparse Eph receptor responder surfaces in CTX-CGE, MEA/LA/CA1/DG, Sst, and cerebellar GABA/glutamatergic groups.
statement: The focal Epha10, Epha5, and Ephb1 downstream mRNA changes are receptor- and cell-group-restricted rather than generic Eph-family responses.

higher_order_basis: DP-family cross-comparisons separate the sparse Tfdp1 thalamic genes from broader E2F/DP-family or cell-cycle programs.
scope: Tfdp1 and Tfdp2 matched thalamic responder comparisons with represented E2F relatives.
statement: The small Tfdp1 thalamic response is not a generic consequence of weakening represented E2F/DP family members.

higher_order_basis: Direct comparator panels show expected autophagy complex, LC3-lipidation, cargo-receptor, mTOR, lysosomal, and BCL2-related perturbations are flat, divergent, or only narrowly overlapping.
scope: Matched neuronal groups queried for represented autophagy and lysosome perturbations, especially Becn1-responsive and Rb1cc1-responsive contexts.
statement: Represented autophagy and lysosome perturbations are not transcriptomically interchangeable in this postnatal neuronal screen, aside from a narrow 155 MB Glut Calr/Ctsb overlap among initiation-associated genes.

higher_order_basis: Chaperone, DNAJ/Hsp40, HSP70/HSP90/HSF1, and Stub1-centered comparisons converge on weak or absent basal neuronal RNA responses for single chaperone/client-regulator perturbations, while core proteasome subunit loss provides an assay-detectable contrast.
scope: Represented proteostasis, DNAJ/chaperone, Stub1, and proteasome comparisons in basal postmitotic juvenile neurons.
statement: Single distal chaperone and DNAJ-family perturbations are transcriptionally buffered in basal postmitotic neurons, unlike core proteasome subunit perturbations that produce broad RNA responses.

higher_order_basis: The component contains one direct Mycn perturbation response and one MYC/rDNA comparator finding; together they support a restricted Mycn effect and argue against a broad MYC-family ribosome-biogenesis program in assayed postmitotic neurons.
scope: Postmitotic P16-targeted neuronal screen, especially 053 Sst Gaba; the Mycn signal is modest and not sufficient to define a ribosome-biogenesis program.
statement: MYC-family perturbation did not produce a broad acute ribosome-biogenesis transcriptional program in the assayed postmitotic neurons, apart from a modest Mycn-specific Sst GABA response.

higher_order_basis: The Findings jointly separate Sucla2 buffering from a detectable compensatory mRNA switch among succinyl-CoA ligase subunits while noting that protein assembly, flux, and enzyme depletion were not measured.
scope: Sucla2 perturbation in measured postnatal neuronal groups, with Suclg1/Suclg2 subunit mRNA readout
statement: Sucla2-associated buffering in this assay is not explained by detectable nuclear mRNA induction of Suclg1 or Suclg2 in measured postnatal neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Creb1 provides the direct detectable thalamic CRE-family transcriptional response, while Prkaca defines that the response is not reproduced by loss of the represented PKA catalytic subunit in the same screening context.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA perturbation screen, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and sampled CREB/PKA-related readouts.
statement: Basal Creb1 loss produces a detectable thalamic glutamatergic CRE-family transcriptional response that is not phenocopied by Prkaca loss.

higher_order_basis: Rgma-, Neo1-, Lrig2-, and Hjv-centered findings jointly reject a simple linear RGMa-Neogenin-BMP or Neogenin-shedding mRNA module in sampled postnatal neuronal nuclei.
scope: Represented RGMa/Neogenin/BMP-receptor/ADAM/Hjv-related perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; mRNA readout only, with protein-cleavage mechanisms not directly assayed.
statement: The represented RGMa-Neogenin/BMP-related perturbation set does not behave as a single linear transcriptional module in postnatal neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Two PMCA paralog contrasts and one PMCA-associated surface-machinery contrast show that the thalamic transcriptional response is selective for Atp2b1 among represented paralogs and is not reproduced by Bsg loss.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and matched represented PMCA/Bsg perturbation contexts; Atp2b4 and Nptn were not perturbation targets, and comparisons use DE surfaces rather than direct calcium or PMCA-complex measurements.
statement: The basal transcriptional response to PMCA perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is Atp2b1-selective and is not reproduced by Atp2b2, Atp2b3, or Bsg loss.

higher_order_basis: Across independent Ptprc, Ptprd, Ptprt, and Il1rapl2 perturbation contexts, represented receptor-PTP or receptor-PTP-associated comparators repeatedly failed to produce shared FDR-level neuronal snRNA-seq signatures.
scope: Represented receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatases and selected associated signaling or adhesion comparators in acute postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq; phosphoproteomic, developmental, immune-cell, structural synapse, and multi-knockout phenotypes are outside scope.
statement: Represented receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase perturbations do not form a shared acute postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq loss-of-function signature.

higher_order_basis: Dlgap4 is a sparse positive exception within a broader postsynaptic scaffold neighborhood whose represented relatives are mostly flat or non-interchangeable at basal RNA level.
scope: Dlgap4, Shank3, Frmpd4, and represented PSD comparator perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Dlgap4 loss produces a sparse cell-type-selective RNA response that is not a general property of represented PSD scaffold perturbations.

higher_order_basis: All proposals express the same pathway-level negative proposition: represented BMP/TGF-family receptor and SMAD single-gene perturbations yield sparse, isolated, mostly null, or non-overlapping neuronal responses rather than a shared canonical receptor-SMAD transcriptomic module.
scope: Represented BMP/TGF-family receptor and SMAD perturbations in postnatal neuronal assay contexts, including listed cortical glutamatergic, MGE GABA, thalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar groups where measured.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented BMP/TGF-family receptors and SMAD components do not form a coherent shared canonical receptor-SMAD neuronal transcriptomic module in this postnatal assay.

higher_order_basis: Far1's positive Insig1/Tial1 response is bounded by flat or non-overlapping ether-lipid and peroxisomal comparators, preventing interpretation as a generic same-pathway response.
scope: Far1, Agps, and represented peroxisome/ether-lipid comparators in postmitotic NeuN-positive neurons.
statement: The Far1 Insig1/Tial1 response is not a generic transcriptional consequence of perturbing represented peroxisomal ether-lipid or peroxisome-pathway genes.

higher_order_basis: The supplied findings independently test transcriptomic convergence among glutathione synthesis, GPX4, ferroptosis, NRF/redox, and glutamate-supply perturbations and repeatedly find flat, singleton, or orthogonal responses rather than a shared neuronal RNA module.
scope: Postnatal sparse-brain neuronal transcriptomic comparisons among represented glutathione/GPX4/ferroptosis/NRF-redox perturbations; biochemical activity, glutathione pools, lipid peroxidation, NRF activity, and indels are not directly assayed.
statement: Represented glutathione, GPX4, ferroptosis, and NRF/redox perturbations do not form a shared basal neuronal transcriptomic module in this postnatal sparse-brain assay.

higher_order_basis: Tek-centered and Elf2-centered contrasts both include endothelial or vascular-receptor proxies and find no shared neuronal phenocopy, with Ets1-centered signaling contrasts further bounding the result to represented transcriptomic perturbations.
scope: Represented endothelial-receptor and related signaling perturbations tested in neuronal transcriptomic readouts.
statement: Represented endothelial-receptor signaling perturbations do not define a shared neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Known biochemical or activity-dependent relationships involving calcium channels, calcineurin, immunophilins, NFATC3, MEF2A, HDAC5, and Synj1 regulators fail to translate into shared constitutive basal snRNA phenocopies.
scope: Basal postnatal neuronal transcriptomic readouts for Synj1 regulatory, calcium-channel, immunophilin, calcineurin, NFATC3, HDAC5, and Mef2a perturbations.
statement: Known activity-dependent or biochemical calcium-calcineurin relationships do not translate into constitutive shared neuronal snRNA phenocopies in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Platelet receptor, megakaryocyte, and GPVI-related findings converge on absent, sparse, or non-coherent neuronal downstream responses among represented targets.
scope: Represented platelet-lineage, megakaryocyte-associated, GPVI-related, and overlapping integrin perturbations in neuronal groups; same-complex Gp1ba partners and beta3-complex comparators were not represented.
statement: Represented platelet-lineage receptor and megakaryocyte-associated perturbations do not form a coherent platelet-like basal neuronal transcriptional module after single-gene perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Calmodulin-linked calcineurin, SK-channel, PhK, and Camta1 comparisons show little, opposite, or absent convergence across expected calcium/calmodulin-associated branches, while Calm paralog findings explain why partial calmodulin-locus perturbation is not a universal proxy.
scope: Juvenile neuronal basal RNA readouts after P16 CRISPR perturbation of represented calmodulin-linked, calcineurin, SK-channel, phosphorylase-kinase, and Camta1 targets.
statement: Represented calcium/calmodulin-associated perturbations are transcriptionally branch-specific rather than a single shared Ca2+-calmodulin-linked neuronal RNA response.

higher_order_basis: Multiple neuromodulatory GPCR and proximal second-messenger comparisons independently show absent, sparse, or nonconvergent basal nuclear RNA outputs despite canonical signaling proximity.
scope: Represented neuromodulatory GPCR, Gq/PLC/Ca2+/PKC/MAPK, cAMP/GIRK, and related effector perturbations in basal postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented neuromodulatory GPCR receptors and proximal second-messenger effectors generally fail to produce a shared basal neuronal nuclear-transcriptome module.

higher_order_basis: The two findings jointly bound expected lipid or FAO-related transcriptional programs by showing sparse Cpt1c effects and absent convergence among represented ETF/FAO-adjacent perturbations.
scope: Represented neuronal lipid-sensing, ETF, FAO-adjacent, and PPAR/PGC1 perturbations in this screen; Etfb, Etfdh, and major ACAD donors were not perturbation targets.
statement: Represented neuronal lipid/FAO-adjacent perturbations did not reveal a broad convergent beta-oxidation transcriptional response, instead producing flat or isolated cell-type-specific RNA effects.

higher_order_basis: Substrate, protease, trafficking, Notch, and synaptic-adhesion findings repeatedly separate biochemical processing relationships from a shared juvenile neuronal mRNA loss-of-function module.
scope: Sparse juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented APP-processing, secretase, Notch, synaptic-adhesion, and endosomal targets.
statement: Represented APP-processing, secretase, Notch, synaptic-adhesion, and APP-trafficking perturbations are largely uncoupled from a shared juvenile neuronal nuclear RNA module.

higher_order_basis: Detectable Rab7 and Vps35 trafficking responses contrast with flat or nonconvergent Vps35l, Washc4, and Lrmda-associated surfaces, bounding the result to target-specific transcriptional responses rather than failure to detect trafficking perturbations at all.
scope: Measured neuronal endolysosomal, retromer, Retriever/Commander, WASH, and LRO-related perturbations; transcriptomic readout only.
statement: The neuronal assay can detect selected endolysosomal trafficking perturbations, but Vps35l, Washc4, and Lrmda do not produce a shared detectable trafficking transcriptomic response.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Elp1 and Elp2 same-complex findings directly establish same-direction convergence on an ATF4/amino-acid stress module, while Elp1/Elp2 positive module findings and Thap11 scoping define the neuronal context.
scope: Elp1 and Elp2 perturbations, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with Elp1 extending into additional thalamic/midbrain/hindbrain responder groups; Elp3-Elp6 were not assayed.
statement: Elp1 and Elp2 loss converge on a same-direction ATF4-like amino-acid stress transcriptional program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

higher_order_basis: The proposals overlap on a shared vulnerable-neuron ER proteostasis proposition supported by same-direction convergence among ER calcium loading, glycosylation precursor supply, dolichol supply, BiP, and ER client-handling perturbations, with Elp2 defining a partial-state boundary.
scope: Vulnerable neuronal groups emphasized in the findings, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, plus additional Hspa5 and Dhdds responder groups where stated; transcriptomic convergence only, not physical interaction.
statement: Perturbations affecting ER calcium loading, glycosylation precursor supply, dolichol supply, BiP, and ER client handling converge on a shared vulnerable-neuron ER quality-control stress state with same-direction UPR/ISR-associated transcriptional features.

higher_order_basis: Represented melanocortin receptor, peptide, and Atrn perturbations independently show flat or absent downstream RNA responses, with consistent caveats that central MC3R/MC4R/POMC/Asip biology and physiological outputs were not directly tested.
scope: Represented Mc1r, Mc2r, Agrp, and Atrn perturbations in broad neuronal and hypothalamic groups; central Mc3r, Mc4r, Pomc, Asip, Mrap, and Mrap2 perturbations were not available.
statement: The assayed melanocortin-system perturbations provide no evidence for a captured basal neuronal melanocortin transcriptional response module.

higher_order_basis: The two PHOX2-family perturbation findings independently test overlapping autonomic/noradrenergic marker programs in recovered postnatal neuronal nuclei and both report absence of the expected transcriptional outputs.
scope: Phox2a and Phox2b perturbations across recovered postnatal neuronal groups in the screen
statement: Phox2a and Phox2b perturbations do not elicit a detectable canonical autonomic or noradrenergic identity program in recovered postnatal neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: The reciprocal paralog-centered findings reject detectable cross-phenocopy between Slc25a12 and Slc25a13 in the P16 NeuN-enriched sparse CRISPR neuronal transcriptomic assay.
scope: Slc25a12 and Slc25a13 perturbations in the P16 NeuN-enriched sparse CRISPR neuronal transcriptomic assay, with Slc25a12 self-transcript decrease detected in one cell group.
statement: AGC paralogs Slc25a12 and Slc25a13 do not form a shared detectable neuronal transcriptional perturbation signature in the P16 sparse CRISPR readout.

higher_order_basis: Across transporter, import, lipid, beta-oxidation, ether-lipid, and maintenance perturbations, findings repeatedly report flat, sparse, or non-overlapping transcriptomic outcomes rather than a coherent peroxisome-wide neuronal RNA module, with sparse target-specific exceptions.
scope: Represented peroxisome-linked lipid, transporter, import, beta-oxidation, ether-lipid, and maintenance perturbations in postmitotic NeuN-positive neuronal snRNA-seq; several closest pathway genes were not represented as perturbation targets.
statement: Represented peroxisome-linked perturbations do not converge on a shared acute neuronal transcriptomic module; observed effects are predominantly flat, sparse, or target-specific.

higher_order_basis: Measured Zic paralog perturbations show divergent or flat acute transcriptomic behavior rather than reciprocal phenocopy across the assayed thalamic and CB-GABA neuronal contexts.
scope: Represented Zic1, Zic2, Zic3, and Zic4 perturbations in the P16 neuronal screen, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA; embryonic and cerebellar precursor compensation is not tested.
statement: Represented Zic paralogs are not acutely interchangeable as postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic regulators in the assayed P16 cell groups.

higher_order_basis: Ligand-, receptor-, and proximal-comparator findings across netrin/DCC/UNC5/DSCAM and Slit/Robo neighborhoods converge on null, near-null, or non-overlapping RNA surfaces rather than a persistent neuronal soma guidance module.
scope: Represented P16 postmitotic neuronal axon-guidance perturbations spanning netrin/DCC/UNC5/Neo1/DSCAM, Slit/Robo, and nearby guidance-cytoskeletal comparators; limited to snRNA-seq soma transcriptomes and represented targets.
statement: Represented axon-guidance ligand, receptor, and proximal pathway perturbations do not produce a convergent robust neuronal soma transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Both findings show that perturbations in ion-channel, AIS/nodal, and excitability-associated contexts can be engaged without broad downstream mRNA rewiring in sparse postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq, while preserving the limitation that protein localization, current density, and network physiology were not measured.
scope: Postnatal sparse neuronal snRNA-seq surfaces for Scn1b, Ank2, sodium-channel, and KCNQ-associated perturbations.
statement: Scn1b-, Ank2-, sodium-channel-, and KCNQ-associated perturbations do not produce broad downstream ion-channel or AIS/nodal mRNA rewiring in assayed postnatal neuronal nuclei.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal contrasts across Vps13a, Vps13b, and Vps13c show flat or non-phenocopying transcriptomic surfaces in assayed juvenile postmitotic neuronal groups.
scope: Represented VPS13 single-gene perturbations in the assayed P16 postmitotic neuronal Perturb-seq context; Vps13d, Xk, and combined perturbations were not tested as targets.
statement: Acute single-gene perturbation of represented VPS13 paralogs does not elicit a shared basal neuronal transcriptomic module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: Independent Fe-S assembly, Fe-S client, export, and iron-homeostasis perturbation contrasts repeatedly show flat, weak, isolated, or nonoverlapping RNA responses rather than a shared neuronal ISC/iron-stress module.
scope: Represented Fe-S assembly, mitochondrial Fe-S client, OXPHOS, and iron-homeostasis perturbations in juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented Fe-S/ISC-related and iron-homeostasis components do not resolve into a coherent shared neuronal iron-sulfur or iron-stress transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Adnp and Chd4 findings support same-direction convergence, while Zmym2 provides a related but limited overlap that bounds the proposition against overgeneralizing to all associated chromatin factors.
scope: Postmitotic juvenile neuronal responses involving Adnp, Chd4, and partially Zmym2, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
statement: Adnp and Chd4 perturbations recover a shared same-direction neuronal ChAHP-related transcriptomic program, with Zmym2 showing only partial overlap.

higher_order_basis: Across Nr4a1, Jund, and Fosl2 contrasts, represented activity-regulated CREB/AP-1/EGR/bZIP/MAPK neighbors show divergent, sparse, or absent matched neuronal transcriptomic responses rather than shared phenocopy.
scope: Matched neuronal groups with represented CREB/AP-1/EGR/bZIP/MAPK perturbation targets.
statement: Represented CREB/AP-1/EGR and related bZIP/MAPK perturbations do not form a shared postnatal neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic module.

higher_order_basis: Both findings support absence of convergence among represented Down-syndrome-related single-gene loss-of-function perturbations while preserving the limitation that this assay does not model trisomic overexpression or missing dopaminergic Synj1 context.
scope: Represented Hsa21/Down-syndrome candidate single-gene loss-of-function perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq groups.
statement: Single-gene loss-of-function of represented Down-syndrome-associated neuronal candidates does not produce an interchangeable postnatal neuronal RNA signature in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Pax8, Otx2, Pax2, Pitx2, and En1-centered findings test canonical developmental relatives in sampled postnatal neuronal groups and consistently find absent, sparse, or nonconvergent transcriptional responses rather than reactivation of thyroid, retinal, Pax/Otx, or midbrain-hindbrain programs.
scope: P16 postmitotic neuronal perturbations of represented Pax/Otx/Pitx/En and thyroid, retinal, or midbrain-hindbrain developmental regulators in measured neuronal groups.
statement: Represented Pax/Otx/Pitx/En developmental regulator perturbations do not recover canonical thyroid, retinal, or midbrain-hindbrain transcriptional programs in the sampled postnatal neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Atp2a2 provides the positive perturbation-effect benchmark for neuronal UPR/ISR detectability, while Vps53 defines the boundary condition: a local Ddit3 hit does not imply full stress-module induction.
scope: Atp2a2 and Vps53 perturbations in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq stress-response readouts.
statement: Vps53 perturbation does not produce the full neuronal UPR/ISR transcriptional program that is detectable after Atp2a2 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Multiple semaphorin, plexin, neuropilin, CRMP, kinase, and cytoskeletal-node comparisons report near-zero or nonoverlapping snRNA signatures, while preserving that non-transcriptional wiring and cytoskeletal mechanisms were not directly assayed.
scope: Represented semaphorin, plexin, neuropilin, downstream CRMP/kinase, and cytoskeletal perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented semaphorin-plexin-neuropilin perturbations do not form an interchangeable shared acute neuronal mRNA-signature module in this screen.

higher_order_basis: The original proposal combined two separable facets; this claim retains the facet separating visible HBP/O-GlcNAc or HBP-to-ER-glycosylation responses from buffered central glycolysis behavior.
scope: Represented central glycolysis, HBP/O-GlcNAc, HBP-to-ER-glycosylation, proteasome, and stress-sensor perturbations in NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic assays.
statement: Hexosamine/O-GlcNAc and HBP-to-ER-glycosylation perturbations occupy a transcriptionally visible RNA response space distinct from buffered central glycolysis perturbations in postmitotic neurons.

higher_order_basis: The component supports a single restricted convergence proposition in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut based on the shared same-direction Pde4a/Ptprf/Rfx3 overlap between Ski and Mib1, while avoiding unsupported biochemical-interaction or full-cilia-pathway claims.
scope: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut perturbation signatures for Mib1 and Ski; based on a small FDR-backed overlap and not a reconstructed ciliary pathway or biochemical-interaction claim.
statement: Mib1 and Ski perturbations converge on a restricted L2/3 cortical up-regulation module containing Pde4a, Ptprf, and Rfx3.

higher_order_basis: Dopamine receptor and downstream cAMP effector contrasts specifically reject a dopamine-receptor phenocopy model, while preserving the restricted Pde10a exception.
scope: Represented dopamine receptor and cAMP effector perturbations in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Loss of represented dopamine receptors does not transcriptionally phenocopy represented G-protein, cyclase, phosphodiesterase, PKA, or CREB-axis perturbations in juvenile neurons.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Ctcf- and Bptf-centered expression-signature comparisons establish a partial same-direction overlap across caudal neuronal groups without implying direct co-occupancy or chromatin looping.
scope: 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA
statement: Bptf and Ctcf perturbations share a partial same-direction neuronal RNA module across caudal brain groups.

higher_order_basis: Frizzled-, ROR/RYK-, PCP-, and LDLR-family receptor findings repeatedly show flat, sparse, or non-overlapping perturbation surfaces, with caveats for missing pathway members and non-transcriptional biology.
scope: Represented Wnt/Frizzled/ROR/RYK/PCP and related receptor-level perturbations in postnatal neuronal single-gene CRISPR readouts.
statement: Single perturbations of represented Wnt receptor-layer and PCP-associated genes are largely transcriptionally buffered, sparse, or nonconvergent in postnatal neuronal nuclear-RNA readouts rather than forming a shared receptor-level Wnt/PCP mRNA module.

higher_order_basis: Sleep- or circadian-associated genes Btbd9, Syncrip, Magel2, and Rorb lack stable endpoint clock-output signatures despite internal Bmal1/Clock/Nr1d comparator evidence that the assay can detect such programs.
scope: Single-endpoint postnatal neuronal Perturb-seq; phase, amplitude, circuit, protein-level, morphology, and post-translational phenotypes remain untested.
statement: Several sleep- or circadian-associated gene losses outside the core positive-limb machinery are transcriptionally uncoupled from stable endpoint neuronal clock-output modules despite detectable Bmal1/Clock/Nr1d clock responses in the same assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple AMPAR subunit, TARP/scaffold, and AMPAR-trafficking-axis perturbation findings converge on flat, near-null, or singleton-only basal transcriptomic responses, with NMDAR responses serving as an internal detectability boundary.
scope: Basal juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq perturbations of represented AMPAR-core, AMPAR-trafficking, and postsynaptic scaffold genes.
statement: Represented AMPAR-core and AMPAR-trafficking/scaffold perturbations are transcriptionally buffered in basal juvenile neurons rather than forming an interchangeable AMPAR-loss nuclear RNA program.

higher_order_basis: PBX/MEIS/PKNOX-centered findings independently show absent, singleton-only, or target-specific perturbation surfaces among represented individual TALE/PBX/MEIS/PREP targets.
scope: Represented individual TALE/PBX/MEIS/PKNOX perturbations in the P16 postnatal neuronal screen, with directly compared HOX context.
statement: Represented individual TALE/PBX/MEIS/PREP perturbations are transcriptionally buffered in the P16 neuronal screen and do not produce a shared homeobox-cofactor response module.

higher_order_basis: Ctcf-centered evidence anchors the non-phenocopy of represented cohesin-machinery perturbations, with additional chromatin-architecture comparisons supporting target-specificity in the acute neuronal assay.
scope: Ctcf, represented cohesin-machinery, and chromosome-architecture perturbations in sampled postnatal neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
statement: Ctcf perturbation produces an acute neuronal transcriptional response, including a CTCF-dominant Pcdh output, that is not phenocopied by represented cohesin-machinery perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Matched-cell retinoid receptor findings identify the Rarb-associated Arhgef4 event as an isolated singleton rather than a reproducible RAR/RXR-family perturbation signature.
scope: Matched 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut retinoid receptor perturbation comparisons; Rara was not represented.
statement: The Rarb-associated Arhgef4 singleton response is not a pan-RAR/RXR perturbation signature in matched neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: The component contains matched perturbation evidence separating the Tuba1a-induced tubulin isoform compensation surface from Dip2b loss in the same neuronal contexts.
scope: Matched 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons assayed after Tuba1a and Dip2b perturbations, limited to the represented tubulin-related transcriptomic targets.
statement: In matched Pvalb GABA and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, the tubulin-isoform compensation response detected after Tuba1a perturbation is not engaged by Dip2b loss.

higher_order_basis: Both findings compare represented RFX-family and ciliary effector perturbations in postnatal neurons and converge on absent or nearly absent acute neuronal transcriptional signatures, with developmental and ciliated-lineage caveats preserved.
scope: Represented RFX-family and ciliary effector perturbations in the postnatal neuronal assay.
statement: Represented RFX-family and ciliary effector perturbations do not produce a shared acute neuronal ciliary transcriptional signature in this assay.

higher_order_basis: The Tpm1 and Tpm3 findings directly reject a paralog-rebound or generic actin-core mRNA response, while Cfl2 bounds the interpretation to postmitotic neuronal nuclei rather than muscle disease biology.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal perturbations of represented tropomyosin, actin-core, and Cfl2-related thin-filament genes.
statement: Tropomyosin and related actin-core perturbations in postmitotic neuronal nuclei do not induce a generic actin-damage or tropomyosin paralog-compensation mRNA program.

higher_order_basis: The Findings place overlapping chaperone genes on opposite sides of a stress-response axis: proteasome-subunit damage induces compensatory HSP/ISR transcripts, whereas Hsf1 loss suppresses overlapping HSP genes.
scope: Psmc1/Psmb4 proteasome-subunit and Hsf1 perturbations in responsive postnatal neuronal groups
statement: Proteasome-subunit perturbation activates an HSF1-linked compensatory chaperone/stress program in responsive neurons, whereas Hsf1 perturbation suppresses overlapping HSP genes.

higher_order_basis: LIM-homeodomain, LDB/LIM-axis, and embryonic identity-factor comparisons repeatedly show flatness or lack of convergence in recovered postmitotic neuronal classes, supporting a lineage-window interpretation rather than a single-target failure.
scope: Represented LIM-homeodomain, LDB/LIM-axis, and embryonic identity-factor perturbations in recovered postmitotic neuronal classes.
statement: The represented LIM-homeodomain and embryonic identity-factor neighborhood is transcriptionally inactive or buffered in sampled postnatal postmitotic neuronal contexts.

higher_order_basis: Across multiple represented Dicer1, Argonaute, TNRC6/GW182, and related miRNA-effector perturbation-centered comparisons, single-gene perturbations are flat, sparse, or mutually nonconvergent rather than forming one shared acute neuronal miRNA-loss transcriptional module.
scope: Represented single-gene miRNA/RISC/TNRC6 effector perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq readouts; absence of RNA-level convergence does not exclude protein-level, biochemical, redundant, or combinatorial miRNA defects.
statement: Single-gene perturbation of represented miRNA/RISC/TNRC6 effector nodes does not produce a coherent shared acute postnatal neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Flt4, Kdr, Sox18, Vezf1, and Nrp2 findings independently test canonical vascular, lymphatic, VEGF, neuropilin, endothelin, and downstream signaling relationships and find nonconvergence in NeuN-enriched neuronal readouts.
scope: Represented vascular/lymphatic VEGF, neuropilin, endothelin, Sox18/Prox1, and downstream signaling perturbations in NeuN-enriched postmitotic neuronal groups.
statement: Canonical vascular and lymphatic VEGF/neuropilin/Sox18 pathway programs are not recovered as shared transcriptional modules in the assayed postmitotic neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Both findings directly compare Kdm5c with Kdm5b and agree that Kdm5c has a detectable restricted response while Kdm5b remains flat; the second finding further rules out simple REST or H3K4 writer phenocopy.
scope: KDM5-family perturbations in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with represented REST and H3K4 writer comparators; only Kdm5b among KDM5 paralogs was represented as a comparator.
statement: Kdm5c and Kdm5b were not interchangeable KDM5-family perturbations in this screen, with Kdm5c producing a small restricted neuronal signature while Kdm5b remained flat.

higher_order_basis: Both findings query EMT-adjacent transcription factor or TGF-beta pathway perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups and show flat or nonconvergent outputs rather than a shared EMT-like neuronal module.
scope: Represented EMT-adjacent transcription factor, ZEB paralog, and TGF-beta pathway perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Represented EMT-adjacent and TGF-beta pathway perturbations do not form a shared neuronal EMT-like transcriptomic module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Chd4 directly produces a metabolic/redox branch in 151, while Setdb1 and Zkscan1 comparisons show adjacent chromatin machinery can be active but the Chd4 response is not a universal chromatin-repression output.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut chromatin-repression perturbation comparisons involving Chd4, Setdb1, and Zkscan1.
statement: Chd4 perturbation elicits a selective metabolic/redox adaptation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a broad stress program or universal chromatin-repression signature.

higher_order_basis: The represented EBF/COE findings converge on weak postnatal signatures with lack of paralog phenocopy, while preserving the narrow Ebf2-specific CA3/DG Tbc1d14 exception.
scope: Represented Ebf1, Ebf2, Ebf3, and Zfp521 perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq groups.
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented EBF/COE-family factors are largely buffered and non-interchangeable in the postnatal neuronal screen, aside from a restricted Ebf2-specific CA3/DG Tbc1d14 effect.

higher_order_basis: The direct Mtor cell-type-selective RNA response is bounded by lack of recovery after a proposed upstream Arhgef9 perturbation and lack of phenocopy by represented PIKK/DNA-damage comparisons.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neuronal perturbation surfaces; RNA readouts do not measure mTORC1 phosphorylation, protein translation, or kinase activity.
statement: Mtor loss produces a small TH/midbrain neuronal snRNA-seq signature that is not phenocopied by Arhgef9 or Prkdc perturbation in the matched assay context.

higher_order_basis: Findings identify a detectable Lonp1-associated stress response while showing Agk and several mitochondrial comparators do not recruit that program.
scope: Agk, Lonp1, and represented mitochondrial comparator perturbations in matched neuronal groups.
statement: The detectable Lonp1-associated ISR-like neuronal RNA response is not a generic consequence of perturbing Agk, Clpx, Clpp, Afg3l2, Yme1l1, or related represented mitochondrial comparators.

higher_order_basis: Both null-target neighborhoods show that nearest-neighbor similarity can nominate extremely weak alignments that do not survive inspection as reproducible differential-expression modules.
scope: Data-driven full-profile nearest-neighbor comparisons for null Cckar and Kcnj6 perturbation signatures.
statement: For null Cckar and Kcnj6 perturbation signatures, numerically nearest full-profile neighbors reflect noise rather than reproducible shared differential-expression modules.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly show that an acute LC3A perturbation is transcriptionally buffered in juvenile neurons and that p62/LC3-axis perturbations do not account for the broader Vcp-associated nuclear RNA state.
scope: Acute juvenile neuronal perturbations measured by nuclear RNA, without direct measurement of LC3 lipidation, p62 protein, autophagic flux, or aggregate pathology.
statement: Acute perturbation of Map1lc3a does not generate a broad downstream neuronal nuclear RNA program and does not phenocopy the Vcp transcriptional state in this assay.

higher_order_basis: A narrow Ndufc2-associated Pdcd6ip response is bounded by same-complex and broader respiratory-chain comparisons showing that represented relatives are sparse and nonconvergent rather than interchangeable phenocopies.
scope: Ndufc2-responsive 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut context and supplied same-complex comparator findings in the postnatal neuronal assay.
statement: The Ndufc2-associated Pdcd6ip response in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut is not an interchangeable Complex-I subunit transcriptional phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Calm1/2/3 perturbation findings repeatedly show sparse, non-overlapping, or absent RNA surfaces despite identical protein coding, with calcineurin and SK-channel comparisons bounding this as a transcriptomic rather than electrophysiological or total-CaM-protein claim.
scope: Single-locus Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3 perturbations in juvenile postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq, with selected calmodulin-dependent pathway comparators; guide engagement, total CaM protein, and electrophysiology were not directly assayed.
statement: Single-locus perturbations of Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3 produce locus-specific, sparse, or absent neuronal RNA responses rather than an interchangeable calmodulin-protein depletion transcriptional signature.

higher_order_basis: Nek1 produces a restricted Mdm4 response in one neuronal cell class, while comparator perturbations argue against interpreting that response as a generic NEK, ciliary, DNA-damage, ALS, or mitotic transcriptional module.
scope: Nek1 and represented NEK/ciliary/DDR/ALS/mitotic comparator perturbations in the assayed juvenile neuronal dataset.
statement: Nek1 selectively down-regulates Mdm4 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut without engaging a broader NEK, ciliary, DNA-damage, ALS, or mitotic transcriptional module.

higher_order_basis: Sgcd-centered and Snta1-centered contrasts identify a narrow two-gene thalamic Sgcd response while multiple DGC/DAPC neighbors remain flat or fail to reproduce Sik2/Porcn.
scope: Represented DGC/DAPC and sarcoglycan-related perturbations in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut context and broader matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Within the broadly buffered represented DGC/DAPC perturbation set, Sgcd has a weak target-specific 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Sik2/Porcn response that is not a shared complex-wide neuronal RNA program.

higher_order_basis: Snrnp70, Snrpb, and Snrpn contrasts show that physical or paralogous snRNP membership does not imply shared neuronal gene-abundance phenotypes, with broader spliceosome responsiveness providing assay context.
scope: represented Snrpb, Snrpn, Snrnp70, and spliceosome comparator perturbations in the neuronal gene-level assay
statement: Represented Sm-related snRNP targets do not share a common postnatal neuronal gene-abundance signature solely by paralog or particle membership.

higher_order_basis: TRPM7 and CNNM2 establish absence of a shared magnesium-homeostasis stress module, while TRPA1/TRPV1 contrasts support that represented TRP-channel relatives do not form a broader shared basal channel-family transcriptional program.
scope: Postnatal brain-neuron perturbation readout for represented CNNM2/TRPM7 magnesium-homeostasis and TRP-channel comparators.
statement: Represented TRP-channel and magnesium-homeostasis perturbations do not elicit a shared basal postnatal brain-neuron transcriptional stress or sensory-channel module in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Each target-local comparison tests represented serpin or extracellular protease-control neighbors and rejects shared neuronal transcriptomic phenocopy despite family or pathway adjacency.
scope: Matched neuronal transcriptomic perturbation comparisons among represented Serpini1, Serpine2, Serpinb6a, Lrp1, and F2-related surfaces; direct tPA/plasmin genes and several clade-B relatives were not assayed, and several signatures were sparse.
statement: Represented serpin-family and LRP1/extracellular protease-control perturbations do not produce a shared neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic signature.

higher_order_basis: Matched perturbation contrasts across insulin/IGF receptors, class IA PI3K subunits, Akt3, Rptor, and related proximal nodes repeatedly show basal RNA flatness or nonconvergence, whereas downstream Tsc2/Srebf2-sensitive mTOR-axis perturbation can produce interpretable sterol or mTOR-related transcriptional output.
scope: Basal sparse postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented insulin/IGF, PI3K, AKT, Rptor/Mtor, Tsc2, and Srebf2-associated pathway components.
statement: In basal postnatal neurons, single-gene perturbation of represented receptor-proximal insulin/IGF/PI3K-AKT nodes is transcriptionally buffered, whereas downstream Tsc2/Srebf2-sensitive mTOR-axis perturbation can produce an interpretable RNA phenotype.

higher_order_basis: Two reciprocal same-coatomer comparisons reject COPI phenocopy between Copa and Copg1, with broader secretory-pathway findings placing this within a generally buffered Golgi-trafficking context.
scope: Measured COPI subunit perturbations Copa and Copg1 in matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Copa and Copg1 perturbations do not produce a shared COPI-collapse transcriptional signature in matched postnatal neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Independent perturbations of represented pituitary-lineage regulators repeatedly fail to move canonical anterior-pituitary hormone and developmental targets in NeuN-enriched postnatal brain nuclei, with caveats that anterior-pituitary endocrine/progenitor cells were not assayed.
scope: P16/P37-P44 NeuN-enriched brain snRNA-seq perturbations of represented anterior-pituitary and Rathke's-pouch transcription-factor genes.
statement: Acute postnatal neuronal perturbation of represented anterior-pituitary regulators does not engage a detectable pituitary hormone-cell transcriptional program in sampled brain cell groups.

higher_order_basis: Both Grm6 and Gpr179 perturbations leave canonical retinal ON-bipolar signalplex transcripts unchanged, and related represented perturbation targets are flat or sparse in postnatal brain neuronal nuclei.
scope: Grm6/Gpr179-linked ON-bipolar mGluR6/TRPM1/RGS-GNB5 signalplex genes and comparators in postnatal brain neuronal snRNA-seq, outside retinal localization, ERG, visual behavior, or TRPM1 gating assays.
statement: Perturbing represented ON-bipolar cascade genes does not produce a coordinated transcript-level retinal signalplex response in postnatal brain neurons.

higher_order_basis: The Camta1 negative result directly rejects basal Calm-family or Camta2 transcript regulation after Camta1 loss, and independent Calm paralog findings bound it against a broader shared calmodulin-transcript depletion program.
scope: Basal nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after P16 CRISPR across Camta1 and calmodulin transcript perturbations in measured juvenile neuronal groups; not activity-evoked calmodulin protein regulation.
statement: Camta1 loss is not read out as basal Calm1, Calm2, Calm3 down-regulation or compensatory Camta2 up-regulation in measured juvenile neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: Agtr1a-, Agtr2-, Agtrap-, and Atp6ap2-centered contrasts show flat, singleton, divergent, or nonconvergent responses among represented RAS, angiotensin receptor, proximal Gq, V-ATPase/PRR, and Rac-related perturbations.
scope: Represented renin-angiotensin, angiotensin receptor, proximal Gq, Atp6ap2, Agtrap, and Rac-related perturbations in basal neuronal assay contexts.
statement: Represented renin-angiotensin receptor and proximal signaling perturbations do not form a shared basal neuronal transcriptomic module, with the Agtrap Elmo1 response remaining an isolated CNU-MGE GABA event.

higher_order_basis: Both findings test ionic migraine/channelopathy relationships in the same postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic assay and converge on the absence of a shared broad downstream RNA state.
scope: Postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq loss-of-function perturbations of Atp1a2, Cacna1a, Scn1a, and related channelopathy or synaptic-release comparators.
statement: Familial migraine and related channelopathy genes do not produce a recurrent postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Multiple NMDA-receptor subunit perturbation contrasts independently reject same-receptor phenocopy and identify distinct subunit- and cell-class-specific transcriptomic response surfaces.
scope: Represented NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations in the acute postmitotic transcriptomic assay, with Grin2c not represented as a perturbation target.
statement: Represented NMDA-receptor subunit losses produce subunit- and cell-context-specific neuronal RNA phenotypes rather than a generic NMDAR loss-of-function transcriptional signature.

higher_order_basis: A BMP type-I receptor perturbation and a SMAD effector perturbation both lack canonical BMP-SMAD downstream transcriptional outputs under basal postnatal neuronal conditions.
scope: Smad1 and Bmpr1a perturbations in basal postnatal neuronal nuclei; does not exclude acute phospho-SMAD changes or sparse subtype effects.
statement: Basal Smad1 and Bmpr1a loss does not elicit a canonical BMP-SMAD Id/Msx transcriptional program in the assayed mature neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: The Hspa8 finding establishes the restricted chaperone/co-chaperone response, while the Dnajc5 finding shows that this response is not shared by an expected CSPalpha-system partner.
scope: Four responsive neuronal groups in the P16-to-P37/P44 snRNA-seq perturbation dataset
statement: Hspa8 loss elicits a small, sharply cell-type-restricted neuronal chaperone/co-chaperone transcriptional response that is not shared by Dnajc5 perturbation.
